### B170 — Completing the archive did not rescue K1-b; it exposed that the residual is path dependence [MEASURED]

The archive was completed to all 43 FTMO symbols × D1/H4/M15 on 2026-07-27 (`FTMO_COVERAGE_GAPS` now
empty **and derived by set-difference**, not accumulated from successes). New M15 index data verified
independently: UK100 M15 rebuilt from the FTMO tick archive agrees **92/92** on 2026-07-08.

| | M15 partial | M15 complete |
|---|---:|---:|
| evidence-gap misses | 28 | **0** |
| count agreement | 86.59 % | **86.44 %** |
| port intents / agreed / live-only | 555 / 193 / 189 | 585 / 200 / 182 |

Of the 28 previously bar-blocked intents, **7 reproduce and 21 became genuine misses**. **Agreement
went down.** More data did not move K1-b toward passing; it removed the last excuse for its failing.

**The residual then resolves structurally**, splitting the 17 intent-producing sleeves by whether
their rule is path-dependent within the session:

| class | agreed | live-only | live-recall |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| per-bar — each bar judged on its own | 160 | 7 | **96 %** |
| first-of-day — emits only on the session's first qualifying event | 40 | 175 | **19 %** |

`fx_jpy` 100 %, `fx_jpy_ny` 100 %, `idxrev` 91 %, every `mx_*` 100 %; `asian_fade` 7 %,
`orb_crypto_london` / `ny_crypto_momentum` / `kz_london_crypto_low` / `liq_asia_up_low_metal` 0 %.
`fx_jpy` and `asian_fade` are both M15 FX sleeves on the same archive through the same clock.

**Mechanism.** A first-of-day rule is a **latch** — `asian_fade.py:98` emits "ONLY if that first break
is bar i"; `asia_pdl_fade.py:97` takes "the FIRST Asian bar today". One differing bar early in a
session flips which bar is "first", after which live and replay stay diverged for the whole day and
never re-sync. This also explains two things that looked contradictory: the nearest-neighbour offsets
scatter **−108..+84 bars** rather than being constant, and only **4 %** of live-only intents pair with
a port intent within ±2 bars — so **bar-lag is refuted** as the general cause.

**Port-only intents tested against live's own counter:** 44.2 % are live candidates it never named
(D15's attribution gap), **55.8 % are unexplained** — live's counter says no such candidate existed.
So the divergence is genuinely two-way.

**What outlives the gate.** For the **seven path-latched sleeves, replay is not a verification method
at all** — not this port's and not anyone's — until the book records either the bars it read (D21) or
the latch it set. That is a statement about the live book's testability and it is worth more than a
K1 pass would have been.

### B171 — The second adversarial pass found the measurement the receipts never made, and G4 no longer needs a model [MEASURED — CORRECTION]

A refuter was given five G4/cadence claims and told to default to "refuted". It refuted or partly
refuted **all five**, and — more valuable than any of them — ran the experiment the receipts should
have opened with: **replay the five sleeves over the live window's own bars.**

| sleeve | invocations, 2026-06-18…07-24 | fires |
|---|---:|---:|
| `metals_core` / `metals_softband` / `metals_ob_micro` | 990 each | **0** |
| `crypto` | 440 | **0** |
| `energy_agri` | 332 | **0** |

Reproduced independently before acceptance (XAUUSD-driven grid: 960/960/960/320/320, also all zero).
**The port on the live window's own bars produces exactly what live produced.** G4's answer is a
direct reproduction: the generators ran on the real bars and found no signal. H-defect is refuted
directly; no p-value is required, and none should be quoted.

**What that supersedes, and what was independently wrong with it:**

- **The single control calibration is unsound.** Measured per sleeve on the live window it spans
  **6.4×** (0.36 `fx_jpy` → 2.31 `kz_london_crypto_low`), **2.25×** even within the per-bar family that
  the five belong to. Every P(0) built on it is unsound.
- **"The archive over-predicts live by ~2×" is false in aggregate.** Over the same 2,640 cycles live's
  attribution-gap-free counter sums to **706** against the port's **585** — a 17 % *under*-generation.
  My own K1-b numbers contradicted the claim and I did not notice.
- **"The control is reproduced on two archives, two symbol sets" is refuted outright.** `idxrev`'s
  surface is the same fixed 5-tuple in both archives, the in-tree window is a strict *subset* of the
  VPS window, and both divide the same numerator 157. 0.5417 vs 0.5317 is an arithmetic identity, not
  a reproduction. `idxrev` is also the worst available calibrator: its own rate is the most stable of
  the six (±5 % over six years) while the sleeves it corrects vary 2.5×–41×.
- **Empirical P(0)**, over 1,934 rolling 38-day windows with no model and no calibration: 0.369
  (`metals_core`), 0.375, 0.816, 0.284 (`crypto`), 0.638 (`energy_agri`), and **0.075 for all five
  zero together.** My Poisson figures were off by **10–14×**; even my fire-day model by 30–125 %.

**Corrections of fact:**

- **The oils' H4 history begins 2020-12-30 / 2020-12-28, not 2000-03-29.** That date is EURUSD's alone;
  per-symbol history varies widely (metal crosses and SPX500 begin 2021-01-21). Both the K1 receipt and
  D17 asserted the blanket date.
- **`energy_agri`'s rate is not a scalar** — 0.429 % over 5.6 y, 0.529 % over 2024-26, 1.325 % in 2026,
  with two half-years at exactly 0/3,096. And the "5.6× truncation artefact" decomposes to **1.24×
  truncation, 4.53× window change**; I attributed all of it to truncation.
- **Cadence is a band, not a point:** metals_core 31–58/yr, five combined 85–161/yr, depending on the
  calibration used. More usefully, metals_core's **median 38-day count is 2 against a mean of 6.05**,
  with 36.9 % of windows at zero — "≈35/yr" reads as steady and the process is not.
- **D-I: redacted_account runs ~57 % of FTMO's metals complex at unit level**, not "a third" — the book sizes
  one correlated unit per (cluster, day), so extra symbols split a unit rather than stacking units. And
  **62.4 % of `metals_core`'s generation sits outside the W7 validation surface**
  (`metals.py:15-17` — the crosses "were not on the validated data surface"), which cuts *against*
  adding them to redacted_account.

**The methodological lesson, and it is the third time this session has taught it.** `energy_agri` got
three confident wrong answers before a right one — wrong model, wrong denominator, wrong attribution —
and each was *inferential*. What settled it was measuring the thing directly on the window in question.
**When the quantity is directly measurable, measure it; do not transfer a rate and defend the
transfer.** Both adversarial passes this session earned their cost, and both found errors that no
amount of internal re-checking had surfaced.

### B130 — The dial counterfactual, with the governor loop closed [MEASURED — CORRECTED]

B65 priced the dial **linearly**. `base_risk_per_unit` is inside a closed loop — bigger dial → deeper
drawdown → smaller `size_cap_multiplier` (`admission.py:1260-1266`) → smaller subsequent units — plus
discrete brakes that remove whole trades. `scripts/evidence_pack_dial_grid.py` closes the loop over
the 175 W7-denominator broker rows, per account, on each firm's own reset calendar (B56), with
realised P&L attributed to the day a deal **closed** (`governor_state.py:202-205`).

**Two validations, and an adversarial pass corrected what both were worth.**

The **identity check** — at the live dial the simulator reproduces the observed W7 P&L to
$0.00000000 on both accounts (97/97 and 78/78 trades) — is **algebraically forced**: at
`dial == LIVE_DIAL` the sizing ratio is 1 and `cap_cf/cap_live` cancels, and a refuter re-ran it with
`_cap_mult` replaced by a constant and it still passed. It is now claimed only for what it tests:
no gate fires at the live dial, exogenous handling is symmetric, event ordering is sound.

The **comparator check** against the recorded governor `size_cap_multiplier` is the real one, and it
earned its place twice. It found the **−$212** FTMO residual (a `pre_w7_fleet` GER40 position opened
before the window and closed inside it, now carried as a dial-independent exogenous event). Then the
adversarial pass found the check's own redacted_account figure was manufactured: **1,557 of 2,569 samples
were identically-zero residuals from after the last W7 exit**, padding n and pulling the median to
+$0.0005. Window-restricted, the honest numbers are ftmo n=1,002 median **−$0.0008** and redacted_account
n=1,012 median **−$2.1148**.

### B131 — B65's linear model is right in direction and ~3 points optimistic, one-signed [MEASURED]

At 1.25 % the governor-aware loss is **−1.651 %** (FTMO) and **−2.470 %** (redacted_account) against B65's
linear −1.5947 % / −2.3350 % — **3.53 %** and **5.76 %** worse. Mechanism: a lower dial means a
shallower drawdown, hence a *higher* `size_cap_multiplier`, hence relatively larger units than pure
scaling. One-signed: linearity understates losses below the live dial and overstates them above
(−11.1 % at 4 %, −37.9 % at 8 %).

**So the 2.00 % → 1.25 % step saves 35.3 % of the loss (FTMO), 33.9 % (redacted_account), 34.5 % combined
— not B65's 37.5 %.** B65's conclusion stands unchanged; its number moves ~3 points. B65 is not
superseded — its "explains magnitude, not sign" framing is *reinforced* by B132.

### B132 — The dial ranking is arithmetic; order-dependence is real but small [MEASURED — NULL CONTROL REBUILT]

**The first null was measuring the wrong thing and is withdrawn.** v1 permuted realised-R *values*
while leaving each slot's recorded `live_risk_pct` welded in place. Since `live_risk_pct` spans 26×
across trades, that destroyed the pairing between an outcome and the size it was taken at — not
order. A refuter demonstrated it: with the governor feedback switched off entirely the v1 "band" is
*wider* than with it on, i.e. essentially none of it was the governor.

Rebuilt: 400 permutations moving the **whole trade** — its R and its dial-free intrinsic size
`s_i = live_risk_pct_i / cap_mult(live equity at its slot)` — with the live reference re-derived
along the permuted path, so only arrival order varies.

- **The monotone dial ranking survives permutation.** The live dial holds its observed rank of 8 in
  **90.2 %** of FTMO draws and **61.5 %** of redacted_account draws; null mean rank **8.117** / **8.562**.
  *"A smaller dial would have lost less" is arithmetic on a net-negative trade set.*
- **Order-dependence, corrected.** Band width at 0.75 / 1.25 / **2.00** / 4.00 / 8.00 / 20.00 %:
  **0.031 / 0.073 / 0.169 / 0.479 / 1.185 / 6.963 pp** (FTMO) and **0.045 / 0.113 / 0.253 / 0.946 /
  3.244 / 18.641 pp** (redacted_account). **The v1 receipt reported 3.77 pp and 4.86 pp at the live dial —
  a 22× and 19× overstatement.**
- **WITHDRAWN:** *"the same 175 trades produce a profitable fortnight in the upper tail at every dial
  ≤ 4 %"*. Below an 8 % dial **every** percentile is negative on both accounts. Only at 20 % does the
  band cross zero (redacted_account p95 +8.051 %). This **strengthens** B65's "the dial explains none of
  the sign".
- Observed outcome sits at percentile ≈0.14–0.20 of the FTMO band and ≈0.43–0.49 of redacted_account's.

### B133 — No dial the owner would run engages a brake, and no daily firm breach exists [MEASURED — CORRECTED]

All 97 and all 78 trades are taken at **every dial up to and including 6.00 %** — three times the
ceiling. First block at **8.00 %** on both accounts (FTMO 37 by `max_dd_entry_block`, redacted_account 6).

**CORRECTED, and this voided a headline.** v1 attributed each trade's P&L to the day it **opened**;
the live governor attributes it to the day the deal **closed** (`governor_state.py:202-205` selects
`DEAL_ENTRY_OUT` and keys on the close deal's `time`), and **26 of 97 FTMO and 25 of 78 redacted_account
trades cross a reset day**. With correct attribution FTMO's worst day at the live dial is
**−1.047 %, not −1.393 %**, and **there is no firm-rule daily breach at any dial on either account**
— FTMO's peak daily proximity across the whole 17-dial grid is **0.831** (at 10 %), redacted_account's
**0.944** (at 15 %). v1's "first firm-rule breach at a 10 % dial" is **withdrawn**. The total-loss
wall is first touched at **15 %** on FTMO (proximity 1.000) and never on redacted_account (peak 0.999).

Loss saturates: 2 % → 20 % multiplies the FTMO loss by **2.88×** and redacted_account's by **2.61×**.

**FTMO is the binding account, and not because it traded worse.** At the live dial it sits at
**53.8 %** of its total-loss wall against redacted_account's **40.9 %**, despite losing less in book terms,
because it entered the window already **2.95 %** down. A dial set per book mis-prices the constraint.

**One caveat that runs the other way and must travel with this block:** the live soft daily stop and
−9 % entry block read **mark-to-market** equity (`governor_state.py:271,289`) while this simulator
evaluates them on realised equity only, so brake *engagement* here is anti-conservative. Loss
*magnitudes* remain conservative (no intra-day flatten modelled).

### B134 — B56's reset-calendar fix is a measured null on this window [MEASURED — PRIOR CLAIM WITHDRAWN IN FULL]

**v1 reported that moving redacted_account one hour changes its worst day by 2.66× (−1.256 % → −3.336 %)
and costs 13 of 78 trades. Every number in that finding was an artifact and it is withdrawn.**

Cause: `w7_live_forensics.py:599-607` returns `None` for `day_key_ftmo_reset` when the firm resets at
server time. redacted_account does, so the field is **`None` on all 78 rows**, and the alternate-rule arm
bucketed the entire 17-day window under one `None` key. The "2.66×" was a 17-day cumulative bucket
tripping the −3 % soft daily stop once. The script now resolves reset days through `broker_clock` at
each instant and **raises rather than returning None**.

Re-measured, both accounts, every dial: **the reset calendar changes nothing** — identical worst day,
daily proximity, trades taken and P&L under 00:00 CE(S)T and 00:00 server time.

**So B56 fixed a real hazard in the dangerous direction whose realised cost on the only live window
we have was zero.** "We fixed something" and "it was costing us something" are different claims and
only the first is supported. That is the more useful finding, and it is the one B56 actually earns.

### B135 — The shed has cost nothing; the incumbent is near-optimal and starves only when starvation is forced [MEASURED — CORRECTED]

`scripts/evidence_pack_shed_ab.py`. Reproduces D1's four-cluster table and its 28.6 % shortfall case
(FFD 0.0217175 / optimal 0.0304045 / shortfall 0.008687 / 28.5714 %) — a reproduction, not an
independent validation: the harness hardcodes D1's constants and its answers.

**Arena A — recorded.** 1,754 governor states, 623 distinct headrooms (**622** non-zero), 469
distinct (headroom, unit-set) cases (**393 carry exactly one unit**; max 4), **6,355** `would_units`
of which **6,355 are `sized` and zero are `gross_risk_cap_would_exceed`**, max utilisation
**0.465375**, median utilisation **0.052**, **zero binding cases**.

**Arena D — the conservative synthetic reading, added after an adversarial pass.** Three clusters in
the live map — `metals` (1.00), `energy` (0.80), `fxcross_vol_state_squeeze` (0.12) — occur **zero
times** in the recorded units while supplying ~23 % of synthetic units and appearing in ~94 % of
binding cases in the unrestricted arena. Restricting to the 10 observed clusters drops the binding
rate **28.52 % → 9.88 %**. Binding cases, arena D:

| arm | deployed | conviction | headroom used | top starved |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **first_fit_descending** (incumbent) | 0.03220104 | **0.02029418** | 95.20 % | **0.20 %** |
| proportional_scaling | **0.03378375** | 0.01926009 | 100.00 % | 0 % |
| largest_first | 0.03233780 | 0.02030722 | 95.60 % | 0.20 % |
| smallest_first | 0.02004237 | 0.00628737 | 59.41 % | 98.84 % |
| ascending_conviction | 0.02005538 | 0.00629257 | 59.46 % | 98.58 % |
| optimal_deployed (subset bound) | 0.03245212 | 0.02017673 | 95.95 % | 0.66 % |
| optimal_conviction (subset bound) | 0.03235115 | 0.02034912 | 95.64 % | 0.20 % |
| **random, single draw** (NULL) | 0.02753424 | 0.01513085 | 81.32 % | 32.78 % |

- **The incumbent beats a fair null**: **69.65 %** wins / 6.17 % losses against a *single* random
  draw (60.18 % / 10.67 % in the unrestricted arena). **CORRECTED:** v1 compared every deterministic
  arm against the **mean of 64** random draws, which divides the null's per-case sd by 8 and inflates
  significance by √64 — the edge is **0.99σ** per case against a single draw, not 7.96σ. v1's
  "wins 88.8 %, log₁₀p ≈ −860" is withdrawn; log₁₀p was also a knob on `--synth-cases`.
- **Near-optimal**: **99.23 %** of the max-deployable-*subset* bound and **99.73 %** of the
  max-conviction-*subset* bound. Stated precisely because v1 was loose: the subset optimum is not the
  best achievable outcome — proportional scaling exceeds it (104.1 %) by not being a subset.
- **CORRECTED — the starvation rate is the theoretical floor, not a merit.** The top-conviction
  unit's own risk exceeds the whole headroom on **0.20 %** of arena-D binding cases, i.e. **no
  algorithm could seat it**, and the incumbent's `top_starved` is **exactly 0.20 %**. FFD starves
  **only when starvation is forced**. That is stronger than v1's claim and differently shaped; v1's
  "beats both exact optima" compared against arms optimising a different objective.
- **WITHDRAWN — "only proportional scaling dominates".** In arena D it deploys +4.9 % more risk but
  carries **less** conviction-weighted risk on the **mean** (0.01926009 vs 0.02029418) and loses to
  the incumbent on **83.16 %** of binding cases. In the unrestricted arena its bare +0.00009722 mean
  edge is carried by the top 1 % of wins (147 % of the total delta) while it still loses 64.17 % of
  cases. **In the realistic arena, proportional scaling is worse.**

D1's "a strict ascending shed is worse, not better" is reproduced and strengthened (98.6–98.8 %
starvation). **Recommendation to Borhen (D-M): keep first-fit-descending**, now on stronger grounds
than v1 had.

**Config truth.** `ultimate_book_one_unit_per_cluster_per_day` is globally **`false`** at HEAD

active cap, and **nothing in code or tests pins the shipped config value.** The live book has been
running outside the envelope the 2.0 % dial was certified on.

Re-running `placement_ledger.cluster_placed_today_other_bar` over the **145** recorded `unit_placed`
packets, priced by joining to the broker rows (**100 % join rate**; predicate, cascade, day key and

| configuration | placed | blocked | saved | random-blocking null | **ECDF percentile** |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| cap off (HEAD) | 145 | 0 | — | — | — |
| cap on, UTC key, `jpy` exempt | 116 | 29 | −0.1685 pp | +0.8590 pp | 0.172 |
| cap on, UTC key, no exemption | 108 | 37 | **+0.9583 pp** | +1.0483 pp | **0.471** |

and does not need this. (Percentiles are now a true ECDF; v1's 3-point interpolation was off by up to
30 % relative while being quoted to three decimals.)

**Recommended to Borhen (D-L): fix the record now** — comments, config block, and a startup assertion

### B139 — The A/B tool wrote a green baseline for a run that was killed [MEASURED — FIXED]

The A/B receipt is `phase3/SESSION_L_AB.md`. Getting it produced a defect in the instrument the
whole wave's "no regressions" claims rest on, so the defect is the block.

**What happened.** A full-suite `scripts/pytest_failset.py capture` was terminated by an outer
600-second timeout. pytest never printed its counts line, and the tool wrote a well-formed record
with `totals: {}`, `failed: []`, `errored: []`, `parse_complete: true` and — the only surviving
evidence — `pytest_returncode: -15` (SIGTERM).

**Why that is worse than it looks.** `cmd_capture` *did* return 2 and print a warning, so the
command was not silently green. But **the artifact on disk was indistinguishable from a clean run**,
and `cmd_diff` consumed it without complaint. The exit code is not the artifact; a later session, a
shell that swallows the status, or a `; echo` between the capture and the check all lose it. And the
existing loudness guard could not help: `_parse` sets `parse_complete = False` only inside
`if totals and recovered != expected`, so an **empty** `totals` short-circuits the check that exists
to catch exactly this.

Both reading directions are silent and both are wrong:
- an incomplete capture read as the **baseline** makes every real regression look pre-existing;
- an incomplete capture read as the **after** makes every pre-existing failure look fixed, and
  `diff` prints **"No regressions."** and exits 0.

**The more dangerous variant, which the original code could not have caught at all:** a run killed
*after* pytest printed its summary line parses "successfully" — non-empty totals, recovered ids,
`parse_complete: true`, exit 0 — and is a silent truncation of an unknown fraction of the suite. Only
the negative returncode distinguishes it, and nothing read it.

**Fixed.** `capture` now derives `usable_as_baseline` / `unusable_reasons` from three independent
conditions — a negative returncode (killed by signal), empty totals, or an incomplete parse — and
writes them **into the record**, so the artifact carries its own verdict. `diff` refuses any side
marked unusable, and separately refuses records that predate the field but exhibit the same
symptoms, so previously-written captures cannot be laundered by their age.

**Six behavioural tests** in `tests/scripts/test_pytest_failset_parsing.py` drive `cmd_capture` and
`cmd_diff` and assert on what they write and return — including the killed-after-summary case, which
asserts that a record with correct totals and correctly recovered ids is *still* refused. They
deliberately do not grep the source for a string, unlike the one pre-existing test in that file that
does (working agreement §6: a test that greps source passes against a wrong implementation).

**Scope of this session's diff for the A/B:** three new `scripts/evidence_pack_*.py` harnesses that
no test imports, five documents, and the two files above. The only change that can move the suite is
the `pytest_failset` fix plus its tests, which add passing tests and touch no production module.

### B150 — The restatement is exact arithmetic, and the winsor is why [MEASURED]

`geometry_lib.simulate` subtracts a scalar cost in R at the end of every trade (`:36,38,43,44,53,55,60,61`)
and `wins()` clips to `[-1.3, +5]` afterwards, so `R_cached = wins(R_geometric − charged_cost)`. The clip
is **inert on this book** — extreme cached values are **−1.1601** and **+4.8111** — therefore
`R_gross = R_cached + charged_cost` **exactly, for all 8,503 rows**. Asserted at runtime and in
`tests/test_w7_recost.py::test_winsor_is_inert_so_gross_reconstruction_is_exact`, not assumed.

`charged_cost` is recovered three independent ways on all **102** (sleeve, symbol) pairs and required to
agree: source (`ULTIMATE_REAL_COST_MAP.json` class value ÷ the sleeve's `stop_atr`), `D4`'s own
`resim.cost`, and **the data** — a full stop books exactly `−(1 + charged_cost)`, so `idxrev` stop-outs
sit at −1.042533 (= −1 − 0.0638/1.5) and `fx_jpy` at −1.1148. **84 of 102 pairs carry ≥2 witnesses;
zero disagree.**

**Consequence for F39: the "what did the map contain" band does not reach this restatement.** Whatever
0.0459 *meant*, 0.0459 is what was subtracted. Both readings are published for attribution only.

### B154 — What kills sleeves is carry, and carry is the one thing this restatement cannot measure [MEASURED / GAP]

Swap is the largest single broker cost for eight of eleven sleeves. **No exit index survives in any
cache**, so nights-per-trade is unrecoverable without re-running the generators against
`data/mt5_research_exports/bridge_ftmo_deep_h4_*`, which is **absent from this machine**.

Instead of inventing a holding time, every sleeve is asked **how long its average trade can run before
carry consumes its edge** — a hold in hours, against the longest hold its own exit horizon permits
(`resim.maxbars` × timeframe: 320 h for the H4 sleeves, 240 h for `idxrev`, **12 h** for the two M15
JPY sleeves).

**Night ceilings are swept from `rollover_nights` itself**, not assumed: a 320 h hold charges a mean of
**13.37** nights (max 14), 240 h charges 10.04 (max 13), 12 h charges 0.51 (**max 3** — a
Wednesday-midnight crossing is a triple).

**Three tiers, FTMO.** *UNCONDITIONAL* (no reachable hold takes the edge to zero): `metals_core`
(break-even hold 489 h), `crypto` (975 h), `energy_agri` (1383 h), `sub_xvol_pullback` (never reached).
*CARRY-CONDITIONAL*: `metals_softband` **198 h of a 320 h max (62 %)**, `vp_euidx_pocgrav` 251 h (78 %),
`sub_mid_dn_revert` 269 h (84 %), `fx_jpy_ny` **10 h of 12 h (83 %)**, `fx_jpy` 11 h (92 %).
*DEAD BEFORE COST*: `idxrev`, `metals_ob_micro` — **the re-cost did not kill these, the validation
already had.** redacted_account: `metals_core` drops to conditional (489 h → 329 h against a 320 h max).

**No sleeve is killed by commission.**

**AMENDED — the first published version of this block was wrong in three ways**, all found by an
adversarial verifier and all pointing the same direction. (1) The ceiling scaled each horizon by
**5/7** on the reasoning that weekend midnights are not charged; that reads `rollover_nights:239` and
stops two lines early, since `:241-243` collects the weekend on the triple-swap weekday at weight 3.0 —
**a full week charges seven nights, not five**, so every H4 ceiling was understated 1.40×. The claim
that the JPY sleeves "cannot pay three nights no matter what is assumed" was false. (2) Transferred
rows carried a frozen *total* cost, leaving up to 66 % of a sleeve's rows inert to the carry sweep,
leaking one night of carry into the published `true_cost_ex_swap_r` and diluting the published
`swap_r_per_night` by the transferred share. (3) `survives_at_max_carry` charged the structural maximum
to *every* trade and printed it in a column headed `survives` — a worst case dressed as a verdict.
Corrected, the safe-at-any-hold tier is **four** sleeves, not seven.

### B157 — F39 is a gross/net key-selection error, not a map-content band [MEASURED]

`KB7_tick_mc.py:38` computes erosion as `tick_real − modeled`. `modeled` is **net** of the cost map;
`tick_real` is net of **nothing**, because `COMMISSION_R` is hardcoded identically zero
(`KB7_tick_truth.py:64`, `KB7_tick_crypto.py:46`, `KB7_tick_jpy.py:107-108`). The difference therefore
returns the entire cost map — **measured from the ledgers at +0.1144 R for USDJPY against a map value of
0.1148** — and `:66` adds it back to a row that already paid it.

The like-for-like comparator `tick_costmap − modeled` is computed on the adjacent line in every producer,
is designated *"the like-for-like execution erosion"* by `KB7_tick_truth.py:28`, and is published
per-symbol in `KB7_TICK_TRUTH_RESULT.json`. It was simply not the key selected. Three symbols change
sign under it: **USDJPY −0.0964 → +0.0179 · XAUUSD −0.0026 → +0.0190 · USOIL +0.0195 → +0.0370.** The
positive credits were then fanned across **five further sleeve columns never tick-measured**
(`INTEG_W7_final_book.py:95-107`). Duplicated independently at `KB7_tick_book_restate.py:41,62`.

**So F39 has a correct answer, not a band.** This restatement charges neither the map nor the erosion and
is clear of both.

carries the broker's own realized `swap` field rather than a modelled crossing count —

**Zero of the 41 live JPY-sleeve positions were charged any swap** (`fx_jpy` 0 of 32, `fx_jpy_ny`
0 of 9). `idxrev`: 39 of 59 (66 %) paid, median hold 15.02 h.

**The `swap` field validates perfectly against its own structure**, which is what makes it usable: of
the 300 rows, **76 cross a broker midnight and 74 of those carry nonzero swap; 224 do not cross and all
224 are exactly 0.0 — no false positives.** Swap sums close to the cent against the raw deals export,
and no `DEAL_TYPE_INTEREST`/`COMMISSION`/`CHARGE` rows exist anywhere, so nothing is booked on an
unjoined row.

| sleeve | account | net at horizon carry | **net at measured carry** | |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| `fx_jpy` | FTMO | −0.0246 | **+0.0412** | flips to surviving |
| `fx_jpy` | redacted_account | −0.1754 | **+0.0196** | flips |
| `fx_jpy_ny` | FTMO | −0.0198 | +0.0462 | **conditional** — 9 observations, no structural bound |
| `fx_jpy_ny` | redacted_account | −0.1668 | +0.0222 | conditional |
| `idxrev` | FTMO | −0.1541 | −0.0289 | unchanged — negative before any cost |

Book at the 2.00 % dial, charging every sleeve its horizon carry versus substituting the measured
value where it exists: FTMO `P(pass)` **0.584 → 0.703**, redacted_account **0.447 → 0.636**.

`idxrev` earns its keep by **validating the carry model**: 0.92 modelled mean nights against 66 % of
live positions actually charged swap.

### B174 — Why the live holds transfer: it is the same trade specification, not a similar one [MEASURED]

Checked field by field rather than assumed, because "live" and "validation" naming a sleeve the same
way proves nothing:

| | live packet | validation generator | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fx_jpy` horizon / target | `time_stop_bars` 48 M15 = 12 h / `final_target_r` **2.5** | `maxbars=48` M15 / `target_dist=2.5*a` (`INTEG_portfolio_build.py:234`) | ✓ |
| `fx_jpy_ny` horizon / target | 48 M15 = 12 h / **2.5** | `session_open_mom(..., 1.0, 2.5, 48)` | ✓ |
| `idxrev` horizon / target | 960 M15 = **240 h** / **0.75** | `MAXBARS=60` H4 = 240 h / `TGT_R=0.75` | ✓ |
| entry hour (broker wall) | `fx_jpy` **9** (21 of 22); `fx_jpy_ny` **16** (9 of 9) | `hour>=8`, 4th M15 bar → **9** on 146/146 days; `session_hour=15` → **16** | ✓ |
| symbols | GBPJPY+USDJPY; UK100/JP225/US30/SPX500/GER40 | the same pairs; the same 8-index pocket | ✓ |

For `fx_jpy` the zero-carry result is **structural as well as measured**: entry ~09:00 broker plus a
12 h ceiling closes by ~21:00 **on the same broker day**, under either reading of the export's
timebase (broker wall clock, or UTC with broker = UTC+3 → 23:45). It cannot reach a rollover.
**`fx_jpy_ny` is not so protected** — entry 16:00 plus its 12 h ceiling reaches 04:00 the *next*
broker day, and a Friday entry spans the weekend close to Monday 04:15 (a 60.75 h span). It crosses a
midnight on roughly four days in five. Its nine zero-swap positions are an observation, not a bound,
so **it stays carry-conditional**. An adversarial pass caught this after I had promoted it alongside
`fx_jpy`; the promotion is withdrawn.

**And the structural argument for `fx_jpy` needed a measured premise, not a robust-either-way one.**
A first draft claimed it held under either reading of the export's timebase. It does not: under a UTC
reading the 21:00 ceiling lands at **00:00 broker in summer**, exactly the rollover. Measured from the
bars: the FX week **opens Monday 00:00** (56 of 60 symbol-weeks) and **closes Friday 23:45** (60 of
60) — broker-server-local, not UTC. The argument stands on that measurement.

### B175 — The poll-interval bias was measurable, and it is 28 seconds [MEASURED, refutes a flagged risk]

`placement_observed_at_utc` is when the book *observed* a placement, so it should bias every hold
long. On the **89** `position_closed` packets carrying *both* the observation timestamps and the
broker's own `broker_fill_time_utc`/`broker_exit_time_utc`, the difference has median **−0.008 h
(28 s)**; **1 of 89** exceeds 0.1 h. The sign is conservative — observation over-states the hold, so
it over-charges carry.

**Two qualifications an adversarial pass added, neither of which touches the JPY result.** The median
hides a heavy tail: mean **526 s**, max **9.57 h**, with two XAUUSD positions overstated by 1,247 %.
And the **3 closes whose holds do not derive are among the longest in the file** (15.7 h, 15.9 h,
**87.6 h** — the second-longest position of 300), so any median taken from the derived sample is
biased short. On the JPY sleeves specifically the poll tail maxes at **83.7 s**, and the JPY numbers
use the deal-derived holds regardless.

### B176 — I tried to reach the remaining three sleeves by analogy, and my own data refuted it [WITHDRAWN]

The three sleeves in this book that fired live each used only **4–9 %** of their own horizon at the
median, across horizons differing by 20× — which looks like a transferable regularity, and would have
let me argue that `metals_softband` (break-even at 62 % of horizon), `vp_euidx_pocgrav` (78 %) and
`sub_mid_dn_revert` (84 %) are all comfortably safe.

Measured across **all twelve** live sleeves, including the nine this book does not contain, that
fraction ranges **0.4 % to 105 %**, and three sleeves *exceed* their nominal horizon
(`ny_crypto_momentum` median 57.7 %, mean 95.1 %, p90 **271 %**). Horizon fraction is not a constant,
and `idxrev` is the **only** long-horizon (≥240 h) sleeve with any live evidence — a sample of one
sleeve. **The analogy is withdrawn; those three sleeves keep the band exactly as B154 published it,
and the generator re-run remains the only thing that closes them.**


### B177 — What the live evidence does NOT establish, recorded because it is easy to overclaim [LIMITS]

Three limits an adversarial pass established that the raw numbers hide:

1. **The live sample never reached any sleeve's ceiling.** Max hold 7.36 h against a 12 h bound; close
   reasons 33 `sl` / 7 `tp` / 1 `expert`. It contains **zero observations at the horizon where carry
   would be incurred**, so it measures realized holds in a 13-trading-day window, not structural
   exposure. This is why a favourable sample alone does not promote a sleeve out of the conditional
   tier — only a structural bound does.
2. **"Two independent witnesses" is true of timing and money, not of sleeve identity.** The packets
   carry **no monetary fields at all** (only `swap_source_status` strings), and the holds differ by a
   median 28 s and never agree exactly — genuinely independent. But both take the sleeve label from
   the MT5 order comment written by the same live runtime, so a misattribution would appear in both.
   All 41 JPY rows resolve `exact`, and the combined family — immune to any `fx_jpy`/`fx_jpy_ny`
   mis-split, which matters because one name is a prefix of the other — gives the same answer.
3. **"Same specification" is too strong; "same geometry" is right.** Stop, target, horizon, entry hour
   and symbols match exactly, and extra live management is empirically absent (all 31 JPY packets show
   `be_trigger_r` **equal to** the target, so break-even is inert; no trailing, no derisk). But the
   validation's `len(lon) >= 6` session-completeness filter is dropped live
   (`ultimate_book/sleeves/fx_jpy.py:56-66`), live adds a `_CATCHUP_GRACE = 2` window with no
   validation analogue, live exits fill on ticks against broker-resident SL/TP while the validation is
   bar-resolution, and **1 of 32 live entries fired at 06:00 broker rather than 09:00**.

### B185 — The H1 drift count is a property of your working tree, not of any commit [MEASURED — FIXED]

The documented H1 check reported **`drifted=2`** at `main`, before a single merge.

It was not the signal. `SLEEVE_MEMBER_EXACT_JOIN_LEDGER.jsonl` was sitting as a **131-byte LFS
pointer**, and the snippet hashes the pointer rather than the content. A plain `git merge --ff-only`
had de-hydrated it; `git lfs checkout` restored `drifted=1`. **The pointer's own `oid sha256:` line is
byte-for-byte the contract's expected hash** — `64fd10148a1b656a…` — so an un-hydrated pointer is
*positive evidence the sealed content is intact*, and the check was reporting the exact opposite.

The snippet in `CLAUDE.md` §3 now classifies `UNHYDRATED-LFS` separately from `DRIFTED`. Verified
behaviourally, not asserted: de-hydrate the ledger → check prints `UNHYDRATED-LFS`; restore → prints
nothing. This is the third instance of this family, after H2's retired LFS explanation and the working
agreement's own "a pointer read as data is indistinguishable from an empty result" — and it lives in
the one check the hazard register tells every session to run before touching `src/`.

**H1 membership intersection for this merge is EMPTY**: zero of R2's 43 bound paths appear in
`git diff --name-only main..HEAD`. No re-seal, no ~16.5 MH window re-run.

### B186 — The merge silenced the only process that pages a human, including the gate tripwire Session I had just added for exactly that gap [MEASURED — FIXED]

The highest-severity finding of the integration, and neither branch is wrong alone.

Session M inverted operator notification to **presence-of-authorization**
(`src/safety/notification_authorization.py`) and granted every producer it knew about — seven call
sites: `run_book.py:115`, `run_agent.py:85`, `src/utils/notification_queue.py:1038`,
`scripts/api_refusal_monitor.py:223`, `scripts/no_data_alert_monitor.py:511`,
`scripts/ob_continuation_monitor.py:1048`, `src/safety/heartbeat_monitor.py:1185`.

Session I, in parallel, extended `.tools/monitor_books.py` by +181 lines, adding `gate_tripwire()`
(`:405`, alert text at `:425`) — which per `CLAUDE.md` §4 is **the only thing anywhere that would
notice the live authority gate being flipped** on a funded, connected host.

`.tools/` is not `scripts/*_monitor.py`. It was missed. `send()` (`:308-316`) routes through
`notification_queue.send`, which for a **long-lived** process starts an in-process poller; ungranted,
every alert is refused, retried five times, marked terminal **`FAILED`** and dropped — while
`write_monitor_heartbeat("completed")` keeps reporting the monitor healthy. That is the exact
healthy-process/zero-alerts shape **B105 had just fixed**, reintroduced by a different mechanism in the
same merge. It silences `BOOK DOWN`, `BOOK HUNG`, `RISK BLIND`, the soft-stop and max-DD warnings,
`LOW DISK`, foreign legs, `SILENTLY FLAT` — and the gate tripwire.

No test caught it: I's `tests/safety/test_gate_tripwire.py:102-119` monkeypatches `send`, so it proves
the cycle *reaches* delivery and never exercises the transport; M's tests prove the *transports refuse
when ungranted* and never enumerate producers.

**Fixed** with the one-line grant M used everywhere else, at `.tools/monitor_books.py`'s `main()`.
**And the class is now covered**, not just the instance: a discovery-based test walks every `__main__`
entrypoint under `/`, `scripts/`, `.tools/`, `src/safety/`, `src/utils/` that references a delivery
symbol and asserts it takes the grant or is exempt *with a stated reason*. Proved non-vacuous by
removing the grant (fails, naming `.tools/monitor_books.py`) and restoring it (passes). 14 pass.

The discriminator is **long-lived vs short-lived**, and the transport documents it itself
(`notification_queue.send` docstring): the in-process poller is a fallback "for long-lived processes",
while "short-lived cron scripts that exit after enqueueing rely on the worker." For a daemon an absent
grant is **destructive** (terminal `FAILED` marker, which the authorized worker then skips too); for a
one-shot cron it is **inert** (process exits before retry 5; the entry stays pending and the worker
delivers). `scripts/correlation_shock_monitor.py` and `scripts/refresh_economic_calendar.py` are
exempt on that basis — **with a latent bound recorded**: the retry ladder reaches `FAILED` at ~13 min,
so either would drop its own alert if it ever ran that long. Granting them is one line each;
deliberately not done here, to keep the merge's blast radius to the defect it found. Flagged for wave 4.

## B200–B221 — Session P: packet-emitter hardening (Stage 3, brought forward)

Branch `phase3/packet-emitter` off `main` @ `df2baf060`. Full write-up:
`phase3/PACKET_EMITTER_CARRY.md`. Owner runbook: `phase3/PACKET_EMITTER_VPS_RUNBOOK.md`.

**B200 — the holding-time bias question is closed, and the answer favours Session N.**
`placement_observed_at_utc` is **not** biased late against fill; it *precedes*
`broker_fill_time_utc` by a median **−1.23 s** (earlier on 90/93 closes, 126/132 placements). The
biased side is the **exit**: `closed_at_utc` is byte-identical to the packet's own `created_at_utc`
(max diff −0.0 s over 98 rows) and sits a median **+26.8 s** (p95 +60.4 s, max +24.1 min) after
`broker_exit_time_utc` — one poll interval at the measured 60 s cadence. Net bias of the 148-row
estimator is **≈ +28 s, over-stating**, against break-evens of 10–12 h. **The 148 holds are
admissible.** [MEASURED, 99,112-packet live export]

**B201 — but three medians exist and they differ by 44 %.** Only 98 of 151 closes carry
`closed_at_utc` and only 90 carry `broker_exit_time_utc`. Median hold: 2.2565 h (packet emission —
the figure in the Session P prompt), 1.8783 h (`closed_at_utc`), **1.2603 h (broker truth)**. If
holding time decides five sleeves at OD-3, which estimator is used is not a rounding question.
**No censoring:** all 150 distinct tickets closed in-window, max hold 90 h against a 37-day span.

**B202 — three claims in the Session P prompt are wrong.** (a) `spread_r` is not absent — the key is
present on all 99,112 packets and **null on all 99,112**; it was reserved and never populated, and
`_spread_cost_screen` (`book_owner.py:4083`) already computed it for every leg but formatted it into
a refusal *string* on failing legs only. (b) `position_managed` **does** carry entry timestamps —
`broker_fill_time_utc` on 40,948 of 78,687 rows. (c) "records almost nothing" is true of its nested
`outcome`, false of the packet.

**B203 — the validator could discard a cycle's packets and leave no trace in the log.**
`append_many` raised on the **first** invalid packet after validating the whole batch, so one bad
row dropped the entire cycle's batch; the row-by-row fallback recorded casualties only in the cycle
summary, which nothing downstream of the packet log can read. Replaced by a three-way disposition
(`packet_guard.py`): accepted / quarantined-with-marker / unrecorded. A refusal now writes a
`packet_rejected` row into the **main** log and the full body to a sidecar. Never raises, including
at construction. The pre-existing test asserting that a refused packet leaves no trace was amended,
with the reason recorded in the test body.

**B204 — 78,687 `position_managed` packets describe 148 positions.** Median 91 per position, max
**5,339**. Across that position's 5,338 transitions only `management_checked_at_utc`,
`policy_clock_checked_at_utc`, `policy_clock_diagnostic`, `created_at_utc` and the hashes change
every time; `policy_clock_bars_until_due` changes 161 times and everything economic changes **once**.
Keyed on non-clock content, **3.14 %** of `position_managed` packets are distinct: emit-on-change
would drop **76,220 packets = 76.9 % of the whole stream** with no measured information loss.
Corpus is **826 MB uncompressed / 37 days**. Not landed — **OD-P1**, needs a heartbeat.

**B205 — the join key degenerates on multi-member units.** `unit_admitted` carries
`symbol`/`sleeve`/`direction`/`candidate_id` on exactly **83 of 440** rows — only where the unit
resolved to one member (`book_owner.py:1324`, `else {}`). 301 rows have `member_count: None`, 56
have ≥2. `unit_skipped` carries `symbol` on 14,627/14,638 but `direction` on **306**. Because
`ultimate_book_intent_id` hashes seven fields including those four, 440 rows collapse onto **65**
ids. The directions survive in `admission_unit_members[].direction`; nothing at top level joins.
**OD-P2.**

**B206 — a latent misattribution booby trap, deliberately left alone.**
`_first_unit_sleeve` would attribute a multi-sleeve unit to `sleeve_members[0]` — the alphabetically
first — but is **inert**, because `asdict(SizedUnit)` yields a *tuple* and the guard is
`isinstance(members, list)`. Widening that check to `(list, tuple)` — the obvious "fix" — would
silently begin attributing every multi-sleeve metals unit to `metals_core`, skewing every per-sleeve
rollup keyed on `packet["sleeve"]` (`w7_packet_forensics.py:100`). Not touched.

**B207 — `available_gross_risk_pct` is uninterpretable on its own, which is why the shed could never
be validated.** The packet carries the difference `cap − open_risk` and **neither operand**, and the
cap is not a lookup: `book_engine.py:587-605` tightens it dynamically against daily-loss room. So
Session L's finding (6,355 units, zero shed, max utilization 0.4654) had nothing to check against.
`day_anchor_equity` is worse — `GovernorState` consumes it to compute `realized_today_pct` and
discards it, so checking the daily band means re-deriving it from the number under test. Both now
emitted raw in `economics.governor`.

**B208 — the carry would have broken the live book's import, and the export is what caught it.**
`src/utils/broker_clock.py` **does not exist on the VPS** (`20_src/utils/` has no such file; the VPS
`governor_state.py` predates the clock work). A top-level import in `packet_economics.py` would
raise at module load and propagate through `book_owner.py`. Made optional by construction: absence
degrades the night count to a labelled refusal and leaves every other field working, which also
makes the five-file carry **order-independent**.

**B209 — the first silence alarm was a false-alarm generator, refuted by its own target data.** It
assumed a 60 s grid and excused weekends on the broker clock; against the live export it reported
46 % coverage and **1,633 breaches**. Both premises are wrong: the book emits on all seven broker
weekdays (Sat 7,193, Sun 5,900), and the gap distribution is not a grid — p50 **0.0 s** (packets
burst within a cycle), p90 **60.4 s**, p99 **909.6 s** (a normal ~15 min M15 idle). Rebuilt at a
measured 1800 s threshold: **48 alerts across the live window instead of 3,187.** Set-difference
kept only where it genuinely applies — the namespace roster, where a dead book emits nothing and so
can never appear in any observed set.

**B210 — backward compatibility is measured, not asserted.** All **99,112** existing packets
validate unchanged against the modified validator. `SCHEMA_VERSION` deliberately **not** bumped —
bumping it fails every existing packet on `schema_version_mismatch`, destroying the only live
evidence the programme has in order to record an addition. The `economics` block carries its own
`contract_version` instead.

**B211 — A/B, `tests/ultimate_book` (575 tests): 60 bad → 60 bad by failure set, 0 regressed,
481 → 515 passing.** Scoped, not repo-wide: two sessions were live and memory is the binding
constraint. **No repo-wide "no regressions" claim is made.** The first A/B found two genuine
regressions — a renamed status key with a live consumer at
`ai_companion/supervisor.py:517,539-540`, and a moved test seam — both fixed before the clean run.

**B212 — the LFS pointer trap re-fired one day after being pre-fixed.** Both contract-bound sleeve
ledgers were 131/132-byte pointers again at 21:30 on 2026-07-28, showing as a *second* drifted path
in the H1 check — which the working agreement designates as "the real signal". It was not drift.
`git lfs checkout` restored both and the check returned to the known `drifted=1` false alarm.
Recurrent, not one-off. Also: `git add` on `research/operations/` **silently skips** with a hint in
this worktree's sparse checkout; `--sparse` is required or the receipt does not exist.

**B213 — what the carry still cannot recover, stated plainly.** `economics.cost.modelled_cost_r` is
a passthrough with **no producer** — nothing writes that key, because
`_runtime_learning_trade_context`'s fixed 25-key allowlist excludes
`gtos_vnext_pretrade_cost_model`. Until wired (**OD-P3**, small, and `book_owner.py` is not R2-bound)
the modelled-vs-realized difference — Stage 3's "result side repaired" — is still not computable
from packets. A8 features cannot be emitted for a reason upstream of the emitter: `ConfluenceResult`
is discarded at `admission.py:1084`, the gate is unarmed by config default, **and the five features
are never populated by the metals generators**, so emitting them today emits five nulls. And nothing
retrofits the 99,112 — every new field starts at the first packet after deployment.

**B214 — `broker_fill_time_utc` can be silently moved by up to ±6 whole hours, and no packet has
ever said so.** `_iso_from_deal_time_near_reference` (`book_owner.py:2818-2852`) searches ±6 h in
whole-hour steps for the shift minimising distance to a **local** reference, accepting it within a
10-minute tolerance. The offset is computed and stored at `:3055-3056` and then read by **nobody** —
one writer, zero readers repo-wide, and **0 of 99,112 live packets** carry it. So no reader of that
corpus can distinguish a raw broker timestamp from one moved six hours to agree with our clock.
This is the broker-time-labelled-as-UTC hazard in its most dangerous form: **the agreement that
licenses the `_utc` label is manufactured by the label's own producer.** The B200 bias conclusion
survives (whole-hour shifts cannot touch a 1.2 s sub-second residual) but the provenance label does
not. Fixed here: the offset is added to the packet allowlist and `packet_economics` downgrades
`entry_provenance` `measured` → `transferred` whenever it fired. **Found by a refuter attacking this
session's own claim.**

**B215 — B200's conclusion was too strong, and is corrected.** "The 148 holds are admissible" is
**refuted**; re-measured independently and confirmed. Corrected statement: usable for sleeve-median
comparisons against 10–320 h break-evens, **not** as a uniform-bias-corrected series. (a) The +28 s
correction is unmeasured on **39 %** of the corpus and the gap is a **calendar block**: of 57
estimator rows closing before 2026-06-24 exactly **1** carries `broker_exit_time_utc` (2 %), against
**89 of 91** (98 %) from 06-24 onward. (b) The lag is **three populations**: `broker_closed` n=82
**+27.35 s**, `vnext_time_stop` n=6 **−0.03 s**, `broker_closed_absent_on_reconcile` n=2
**+761.8 s** — so a uniform +28 s *adds* error to book-initiated closes and is 27× too small for the
reconcile rows. (c) It fails in the left tail: shortest broker-true hold **35.0 s** recorded as
61.6 s (**+76 %**); 8 of 89 checkable rows exceed 10 % relative error. **And the certified error term
is 128× smaller than the open one** — the anchor choice moves the median 44.2 % (B201), which this
session had already recorded and still drew the wrong conclusion from.

**B216 — a second exit-detection failure mode, unrelated to poll cadence.** The +1,446 s outlier
(`idxrev`/SPX500, exit 2026-07-02T07:12:57Z, packet 07:37:03Z) ran a healthy cadence throughout: 72
`position_managed` packets spanning the exit, max gap **65.2 s**. The loop polled ~24 times and did
not detect the close. "One poll interval" is the right mechanism for the 82 `broker_closed` rows
(consistent with Uniform[0,60], KS D=0.136 < 0.150 crit) and is **not** a bound on the corpus.

**B217 — `closed_at_utc` is not byte-identical to `created_at_utc`.** B200's supporting specific was
wrong — a `.1f` format string in this session's own probe hiding a sub-second value. Strictly later
on **98 of 98**, median **+0.0457 s**, max **+1.306 s**, exactly zero on **0**. The conclusion it
supported is unchanged, which is why the false specific survived a first reading.

**B218 — this session built the false-evidence class it was commissioned to remove, and shipped it
for four commits.** `management_checked_at_utc` sat in `packet_economics._EXIT_SOURCES` as an exit
fallback. `book_owner.py:1475,1498` set that field **unconditionally immediately before** the
economics block is built, and it is present on **77,942 of 78,687** `position_managed` rows — so
`exit_at` was non-None for **every** management event. Replayed over the live corpus: **71,969
still-open positions published as completed holds**, each carrying a `holding_seconds` of
elapsed-so-far and `rollover_nights` counted to a fabricated exit. `position_open_at_emit` was
`false` **by construction**, `true` **0 times in 72,117 blocks** — the field intended as the
discriminator was wrong on every packet, and the only working discriminator
(`exit_source_field == "management_checked_at_utc"`) was documented nowhere. Mean holding time over
the block: **20.85 h against a true 8.37 h — a 2.49× overstatement**, 476:1 fabricated to real,
feeding the exact number OD-3 turns on. **Fixed**: `management_checked_at_utc` is no longer an exit
source (guarded by `test_management_checked_is_not_an_exit_source_at_all`); open positions report
`position_open_at_emit: true` plus a **right-censored** `elapsed_seconds_at_emit` under its own key;
the **88** genuine mid-management closes are preserved. After: **293 completed holds, mean 8.269 h**
(148 closes + 144 mid-management + 1 adopted) and 71,825 censored observations. **Found by a
refuter.**

**B219 — a logging switch could have stopped both books.** Moving the guard construction inline
dropped the `if not self._runtime_learning_writer` early return.
`ultimate_book_runtime_learning_packet_enabled: true` + `..._packet_log_enabled: false` is a
supported config leaving the writer `None` (`book_owner.py:223-228`); the guard then failed every
packet as `unrecorded` → `packet_write_error_count` → `ai_companion/supervisor.py:517` → `:709` →
`:734-741` → `{'type': 'pause_new_entries', 'namespace': '*'}` and `digest["ok"] = False`, every
cycle. Restored with the reason in-line. Also hardened from the same pass: `__init__` now absorbs
any exception from a writer's `path` property; `value in (None, "")` replaced by identity checks at
three sites (a numpy value returns an array from `__eq__`, a hostile one raises — and one of the
three sits on the rejection path outside any try); `append_many` materialises its input defensively;
`repr(exc)` and the marker validation are wrapped. `BaseException` is still deliberately **not**
caught — swallowing a shutdown signal in a live book is worse than the failure being guarded.

**B220 — OD-P1 re-costed: 76.05 %, not 76.9 %, and not lossless.** The original figure counted
*globally distinct* states (2,467 of 78,687). Emit-on-change is a **run-length** operation: a state
recurring after changing away must be re-emitted. Actual emissions in time order per ticket:
**3,315**, so the real drop is **75,372 = 76.05 %** and the set count swallowed **848 state
re-visits** — protection and target *oscillations*, which are signal. The attack aimed at the
excluded nested `outcome` block **failed**: restoring all 27 substantive outcome-only fields moves
the count by **2** packets. The flaw was methodological, not a field omission.

**B221 — `w7_packet_forensics.py` would have emitted a self-contradicting artifact.** `:186-190`
hardcoded the prose "spread_r is declared on the packet and is NULL on every row" beside a derived
`spread_r_field_presence` count. Post-carry the same JSON file would have carried
`{"null": 84470, "value": 14783}` and that sentence together. Now derived from the count. Every
load-bearing number in that artifact (core-8 weights, governor medians) was verified byte-identical
between a base and a doctored run.

## B230–B244 — Session Q: the MC at each firm's measured rules (OD-3 option D)

Branch `phase3/mc-true-target` off `main` @ `9b9367e78`. Full write-up:
`phase3/SESSION_Q_MC_TRUE_TARGET_RESULT.md`. Artifacts:
`research/operations/w7_recost_2026_07_27/{MC_FIRM_TRUE_V1.json,MC_FIRM_TRUE_V1.md}`.
Engine: `scripts/mc_firm_rules.py`; rendering: `scripts/report_mc_firm_true.py`;
controls: `tests/test_mc_firm_rules.py` (37 passed).

**B230 — the target defect is real, and confirmed at three independent sources [MEASURED].**
`INTEG_portfolio_build.py:298` fixes `TARGET = 0.08`, which is redacted_account's phase-1 target.
FTMO's is **10.0 %** in `FIRM_RULES_V1.json` (coverage `MEASURED`, captured page), in
`config/profiles/operator_profile.yaml:85,99` — the profile the live supervisor launches — and
in `config/profiles/ftmo.yaml:83,97`. Against `config/profiles/redacted_account.yaml:14` at `0.08`. The
commission's list of importers was correct. **Not a live defect:** `admission.py:52`'s
`FTMO_TARGET = 0.08` is consumed only by `:1547`, a metadata dict; the live target comes from the
profile (`build_firm_rules.py:301`). That is FR2, already filed as an owner question; unbound by R2,
one line, prepared not landed.

**B231 — and the sealed engine gets two OTHER firm rules wrong, one larger and opposite-signed
[MEASURED]. This is the session's result.** (a) **Max overall loss.** The engine tests
`(peak−eq)/peak >= 0.10` (`INTEG_portfolio_build_w2.py:263`) — a *trailing* stop. FTMO's is
*"static (not trailing) for 2-Step"*, floor **$90,000** [MEASURED]. Since `peak >= 1`, the trailing
rule always fires at a higher equity, so the sealed engine is **pessimistic**, worth up to
**+0.0764** of `p_pass`. (b) **Max daily loss.** The engine tests `dp <= -0.05` on the day's
*opening equity*; both firms cap it at a fixed cash 5 % of the *initial* balance. redacted_account's own
captured worked example ($110,000 day start, −$5,000 → breach) breaches under the firm rule and not
under the engine, which permits $5,500. Pinned by
`test_redacted_account_worked_example_breaches_under_firm_basis_and_not_under_legacy`.

**B232 — net, all ten dossier `p_pass` figures move UP, not down [MEASURED, 200,000 paths/cell].**
Headline FTMO survivors/fwd/worst **0.99675 → 0.99918**; largest move redacted_account ALL-11/fwd/worst
**0.31785 → 0.36005**, entirely the drawdown basis. On FTMO ALL-11/2015-26/worst the target error is
**−0.05305** and the drawdown error **+0.05210** — they nearly cancel. **A session that had corrected
only the target, which is exactly what the commission asked for, would have reported a five-point
deterioration that does not exist.** `OD3_DOSSIER_SURVIVOR_BOOK.md` §5.2 is struck accordingly;
`CLAUDE.md` §4's `0.951`/`0.450` become `0.954`/`0.458`.

**B233 — what moves is time, not probability [MEASURED].** FTMO survivors/fwd/worst, calendar days
to pass: dossier (phase 1 @ 8 %) **52** → phase 1 @ the true 10 % **66** → the whole 2-step
evaluation **110**. Full window: 297 → 393 → **642**. Time-to-first-payout roughly doubles, and the
FTMO 14-day payout clock starts only after both phases.

**B234 — phase 2 had never been modelled, and it is close to decisive for the book of record
[MEASURED].** Modelled as one continuous bootstrap path with the account reset to initial between
phases. Survivor book: 0.99918 → **0.99828** (FTMO), 0.99625 → **0.99232** (redacted_account) — almost
free. Book of record at worst carry: FTMO 0.45785 → **0.29952**, redacted_account fwd 0.36005 → **0.18016**.
`p_ph1 × p_ph2` is within 0.004 of the joint except in the two weakest cells, where the joint is
*higher* — clearing phase 1 selects bootstrap positions that favour phase 2.

**B235 — the daily denominator is decided deterministically, not by simulation [MEASURED].** The
bootstrap only draws days present in the series, so the worst possible single-day loss is
`min(series) × risk` at a day-start equity of at most `1 + target`. **Survivor book, both accounts,
every window: 26–43 % of the 5 % allowance — no path can breach under either denominator.** That is
a proof, not a `p_fail_daily` of 0.0 that might be sampling. **Book of record: material, and the
legacy denominator was hiding breaches entirely** — `p_fail_daily` moves from a published **0.0** to
**0.0068**/**0.0233** (FTMO 0/1 night) and **0.0055** (redacted_account 0 nights). Isolated cost at FTMO
ALL-11/1 night: **−0.01395**.

**B236 — minimum trading days: modelled for the first time, and inert [MEASURED].** FTMO 4 per
phase, redacted_account 5; the engine models neither and only FTMO's is configured anywhere (FR4). Largest
effect across all 36 cells is **−0.0022** (redacted_account ALL-11/full/worst, under the pessimistic
"keep trading at full size" model). Every survivor cell is unchanged to five decimals. Closed.

**B237 — the dial buys time, not safety, and "the 2.0 % dial" is not 2.0 % [MEASURED].**
`build_survivor_book.econ` vol-matches each variant (`vs = sd_book/sd`), so the survivor book at the
nominal 2.0 % dial risks **0.847 %** (FTMO fwd) to **1.055 %** (redacted_account full) per correlated unit
— the published `eff_risk_pct`, unmentioned in the dossier, a **2.4×** over-reading. Sweeping the
dial at the corrected rules: `p_pass >= 0.9999` at every dial from 0.5 % to 2.0 %; halving the dial
halves the monthly rate and roughly doubles days-to-pass. This prices the dossier's option A: it is
cheap, and this table is not where its risk lives.

**B238 — the two accounts do not select the same book, and the dossier says they do [MEASURED].**
`OD3_DOSSIER_SURVIVOR_BOOK.md` §0 names `metals_core, crypto, energy_agri, sub_xvol_pullback` as
surviving *"on both accounts"*. Read from `SURVIVOR_BOOK_V1.json`: FTMO survivors are those four;

redacted_account. So the dossier's §3 per-sleeve table is the FTMO reading, and its redacted_account §2 rows are
a **different portfolio** from the FTMO rows above them.

**B239 — the three-sleeve intersection book, measured for the first time [MEASURED].** The book §0
actually describes — surviving on both — is `crypto, energy_agri, sub_xvol_pullback`, published here
as `SURVIVORS_BOTH_ACCOUNTS`. FTMO fwd/worst: `p_pass` **0.99772** ph1 / **0.99577** 2-step, 81
calendar days, **2.133 %/mo** against the four-sleeve book's 0.99918 / 0.99828 / 66 d / 2.617 %/mo.
Dropping `metals_core` costs ~18 % of the forward monthly rate and ~15 days, and *raises* `p_pass`
at worst carry on the full window (0.98365 → **0.99512**), because `metals_core` carries the highest

**B240 — B161's 46.9 % concentration figure is a book-of-record share wearing a survivor-book label,
and the real number is worse [MEASURED].** On B161's own stated basis (Kelly columns, signed
denominator) the 11-sleeve book brackets 37.7 / 9.2 on *both* components at intermediate carry

(At worst carry the 11-sleeve book's own shares are suppressed: winners and losers cancel to
+11.86 of 197.91 gross, so a signed share reads 379 % and is arithmetic, not information.)

**B241 — what the correction does not fix, all of it optimistic [MEASURED / reasoned].** (a) The
MC's "day" is a **trade-entry day**: `date=T[i].date()` at the entry bar
(`INTEG_portfolio_build.py:90,163,198`), while the survivor sleeves run 320 h horizons and are
charged up to 13.4 nights — a trade's whole R lands ~13 days before it closed. (b) **Both firms
measure equity continuously, including open P/L** (FTMO `measured_on`: *"equity (balance + open P/L
± swaps − commissions)"*), so an intraday dip breaches where a day-net does not; `p_fail_dd` and
`p_fail_daily` are understated under corrected rules as much as sealed ones. The gap is not
recoverable, and for the same reason the carry band is open: **no exit index survives anywhere**, so
there is no position overlap and no mark-to-market path. The missing exit index leaves the drawdown
path unmodelled, not only carry. (c) **redacted_account prohibits weekend holding on the funded account**
[MEASURED, secondary_audit] and all four survivor sleeves carry a 13.3-day horizon — **every
redacted_account figure describes the challenge phases only**, and the config to make the funded phase
legal does not exist. (d) `p_timeout` is **0.00000 in all 36 cells**, so `PATHCAP` truncation is
confirmed inert at the 2.0 % dial rather than assumed.

**B242 — the control chain, five links, all exact.** (1) `build_survivor_book.py` re-run reproduces
`SURVIVOR_BOOK_V1.json` **byte-identically**. (2) Series reconstruction matches the published
columns on 24 cells, **0 mismatches**. (3) `mc(Rules.LEGACY)` is **bit-identical** to
`INTEG_portfolio_build_w2.mc_series` on 36 cells × 20,000 paths, all five fields. (4) This engine at
the sealed 20,000 paths reproduces **all 96 published MC fields** exactly. (5) The firm-rule
branches — which have no sealed counterpart, and are what the answer rests on — match a **second,
independently written implementation** (closure predicates, flat day loop, explicit phase machine)
on 7 rule sets × 3 risk levels, **0 disagreements**. Seed-to-seed spread at the sealed rules is
**≤ 0.00463** across all 36 cells. Nothing in the sealed route was edited, and
`test_the_sealed_constants_are_still_the_sealed_constants` fails if that changes.

**B243 — claims made and withdrawn.** (1) *"Correcting the target will lower FTMO's `p_pass`."*
Carried the commission's framing into the design; the first smoke run showed the opposite and I
assumed a sign error in my own code. It was a second, larger, opposite-signed defect. (2)
`(1.0 - eq) >= maxdd_limit` as the static rule — correct algebra, wrong at the boundary, since
`1.0 - 0.9` is `0.09999999999999998`; caught by a unit test, replaced with `eq <= 1.0 - maxdd_limit`,
which is also the firm's own wording. (3) A signed denominator for contribution shares — the route's
convention, and it degenerates silently to 379 % / −358 % when a book nets to ~0. (4) A dial sweep
across all variants — at a 0.5 % dial on a near-zero-drift series the barrier problem stops being
drift-dominated and paths random-walk to the 10,000-day `PATHCAP`, so the result would have been a

frozen at 2026-07-02, empty `owner_gated_learning_rerate_candidate_map`,

orchestrator-relayed]**; sessions never touch the VPS, and nothing built here depends on it.

**B261 — the three armed sleeves, measured rather than inherited.** The prompt says "three sleeves"
without naming them. From `SURVIVOR_BOOK_V1.json` by direct read: FTMO survivors `metals_core`,
`crypto`, `energy_agri`, `sub_xvol_pullback`; redacted_account `crypto`, `energy_agri`,
`sub_xvol_pullback`, `vp_euidx_pocgrav`. Intersection = **`crypto`, `energy_agri`,
`sub_xvol_pullback`**, confirming both the count and Session Q's per-account finding. [MEASURED]

**B262 — the live standard is asymmetric by construction, not by threshold choice.**
`_apply_live` composes the halves as `min(backtest, live_cap)`: live evidence can lower a
multiplier or gate, and there is **no path by which it raises one**. Consequence on the real record:
`idxrev` — registry-falsified, gated on every split, and the only live-profitable sleeve in the live
window (B63) — stays gated at ×0.00 while its live record reads `+0.102 R` over 11 fills. Live
evidence may *support* a size-up only at `LIVE_MIN_N_SUPPORT` = 30 fills, the same bar as a backtest
split. [VERIFIED by test, `test_learning_actuator_live.py`]

**B263 — the gate boundary is measured per sleeve, and two drafts of it were wrong.**
`LIVE_EVIDENCE_CALIBRATION_V1.json` tests H0 "*the sleeve still behaves as its cost-true validation
says*": live R-multiples are draws from the sleeve's validated per-trade record (shape, W3/W5 stream
caches — the cache mean reproduces `cached_net_r` for every sleeve) relocated to the broker-true
claim (`net_r.n_horizon_mean`, per account). Cumulative live R is tested against
`b_n = n·claim − c·sd·√n`, `c` solved so a **healthy** sleeve's first-passage probability over 60
live trades is 0.20 (down-weight) / 0.02 (gate).

**Withdrawn draft 1:** thresholds were per-`n` `np.quantile`. Per-trade R has a point mass at the
stop (34–67 % of trades) and a quantile at small `n` lands *inside* it, so a routine stop-out read as
a 1-in-200 event — the artifact reported `stop_outs_to_gate = 1` for **9 of 11 sleeves**. The rule
would have gated the armed book on its first losing trade.
**Withdrawn draft 2:** correcting for the atom (largest attainable threshold with attained
probability ≤ α) still left `stop_outs_to_down_weight = 1` on six sleeves and exposed the real error
— a **per-n** α is not the rate the system experiences, because the rule is re-evaluated after every
fill. Both dead ends are recorded in the builder docstring rather than quietly amended.

Result, worst case (every live fill a full stop-out), armed sleeves: `crypto` 4 → down-weight, 8 →
gate; `energy_agri` 3 → 6; `sub_xvol_pullback` 3 → 6–7; against 30 fills to support a size-up.
**Roughly 8× asymmetry, calibrated rather than asserted.** [MEASURED]

**B264 — a hard floor that does not depend on the artifact.** `LIVE_MIN_N = 3` blocks any live
action below three fills regardless of what the calibration says. B263 is why: a rule whose safety
rests entirely on an input file being built correctly is not safe. Guarded by a test that reads the
shipped artifact and fails if any sleeve is gateable below the floor.

**B265 — running the rule found a defect in the rule: it would size up sleeves the cost-true re-cost
kills.** `metals_softband` scores **SIZE_UP ×1.22** from its every-split evidence and is killed on
**both** accounts; `sub_mid_dn_revert` ×1.23, likewise. Cause: the rule's backtest half is the
CP4/CP5 replay at the legacy cost map — the one F39 found had the wrong sign on tick erosion and F38
found charged zero commission. Fixed with a one-sided `cost_true_survivor` veto (never rescues a
gate). Visible per-account: `metals_core` stays SIZE_UP ×1.15 on FTMO (UNCONDITIONAL) and drops to
KEEP ×1.00 on redacted_account (CARRY_CONDITIONAL) — Session Q's finding, mechanised. The three
CARRY_CONDITIONAL tiers count as **not** surviving, because they turn on a holding time no cache
records. [MEASURED]

**B266 — realized R is derivable exactly from a closed position, with no lot volume.** The packets
carry no lot size. The position's own gross profit over the price distance it travelled *is* the cash
value of one price unit for that lot: `cash_per_price_unit = aggregate_profit / ((exit − fill)·dir)`,
`risk_cash = |fill − stop|·cash_per_price_unit`, `realized_net_R = realized_pnl / risk_cash`.
Cross-checked on an SPX500 `idxrev` short: **0.7472 R** derived against its own independently
recorded `broker_position_planned_target_r` of **0.75**, a field the calculation never reads.
[MEASURED]

**B267 — the two accounting bases never mix, and the aggregate is gross.** Over the 90 closed
positions carrying a broker exit: **50** carry the full position aggregate, **40** carry exit-deal
fields only, **0 are mixed**. On all 50, `aggregate_profit + commission + swap + fee ==
broker_realized_pnl` exactly — so the aggregate is **gross** of charges and using it for the cash
bridge while taking `realized_pnl` as the numerator does not double-count. On all 40 exit-only rows,
`exit_profit + charges == realized_pnl` likewise. The producer selects the basis atomically anyway;
mixing an aggregate profit with exit-only charges would understate cost, which is the F38 direction.
[MEASURED]

**B268 — 40 % of closed-position packets are not usable as completed holds.** Of 99,112 packet rows,
151 are `position_closed`; **89** are admissible as realized R. **61 are refused for having no
broker exit deal** (still open or unreconciled) and 1 for profit disagreeing with price travel.
Admission requires `trade_lifecycle_status == "closed"` **and** `broker_exit_time_utc`; this is the
Session P defect (71,969 still-open positions published as completed holds) encoded as a guard. Every
refusal is a named, counted reason with an example, published rather than dropped. [MEASURED]

(0.0287 R), so the swap model adds real signal. **Withdrawn:** the first version compared
`cost_r().total_r` — which includes spread and slippage — against realized commission+swap+fee,
double-counting two terms that are already inside the realized fill price. It reported **0.0993 R**,
185× Session J's figure, and I read that as a real discrepancy before finding it was my own
arithmetic. Not parity with Session J's 0.000535 R and not claimed as such: J reconciled commission
against deal-level commission on matched symbols. [MEASURED]

**B276 — the risk denominator used the TRAILED stop, inflating R on winners only.** The fallback chain

**+0.0278 R**, 82 % of it in five rows. R is now taken from the entry-time pair only. [MEASURED]

### B297 — …and the severity that argument implies is overstated. Published against my own choice [MEASURED — CORRECTION]
The prompt framed the shift as breaking "three live consumers reading that stream". All three uses
are **dedup only** (`build_runtime_learning_daily_advisory.py:344`, `redacted_host:book_owner.py:1210`,
and `RuntimeLearningPacketWriter._recent_packet_hashes_locked`), all read stored values and never
recompute. Dedup effectively never fires: **exactly 1 hash of 99,112 appears twice.** An adversarial
pass priced the blast radius: `RECENT_APPEND_DEDUPE_BYTES` = 4 MiB ≈ 503 packets at the measured
8,337 B mean, so expected missed dedups ≈ **0.005**. A hash shift would have broken nothing. The
real argument for (a) is that it permanently rewrites every future packet's identity to carry a
always-`None` key — which is the defect P's own `:438-442` comment exists to prevent — and the
actual blocker for (b) was never a hash argument at all but the `ModuleNotFoundError` in B293.

All **99,112** live packets reproduce their own recorded `packet_hash_sha256` — 100.0000 %,

about what the emitter would *produce*. An adversarial pass ran the test the claim implied — driving

## B320–B349 — Session T: the canary package (Stage 4, wave 4)

Branch `phase4/canary-package`. Owns: run the eight token chaos drills; build the owner-facing
view; pre-register evidence-based stop conditions **as alerts, not halts**. The owner accepted the

will follow it himself — so every automatic-halt instinct here became a message addressed to him.

### B320 — The eight drills ran. Six pass, two cannot run here, one was added [MEASURED]

`scripts/token_chaos_drills.py`, receipts under `phase4/drill_receipts/`. Read-only and
broker-free: no `MetaTrader5` import, no `connect()`, fakes constructed in-process, temp dirs only.

| drill | verdict | criteria |
|---|---|---|
| D-1 gate flip without a token | PASS | 4/4 |
| D-2 expiry mid-position + fetch error | PASS (partial — see B322) | 5/5 |
| D-3 activation directory unreadable | PASS after the B321 fix | 16/16 |
| D-4 clock skew | PASS | 4/4 |
| D-5 revoke and restore | PASS | 7/7 |
| D-6 wrong user | PASS (partial — Windows half unverifiable) | 6/6 |
| D-7 over-volume close | **NOT_RUNNABLE_HERE** | — |
| D-8 does killing a terminal produce `None` | **NOT_RUNNABLE_HERE** | — |
| X-1 direct attack on never-strand (new) | PASS | 5/5 |

D-7 and D-8 ask what the **broker** does. A fake module can only replay whichever of the three
possible answers was encoded, which is assuming the answer, so they are reported as not-runnable
rather than passed. Their *consequences* are measured (B322, B323).

D-6's residual is named rather than waved at: `token_dir()` reads `$GTOS_ACTIVATION_TOKEN_DIR` else
expands `~/.gtos/activation` at call time, verified here by moving `HOME`. How **Windows** expands
`~` for a scheduled task running as `SYSTEM` (`USERPROFILE` → `C:\Windows\System32\config\
systemprofile`) is a difference in kind and stays `[UNVERIFIED]` until run on the host.

### B321 — `authorize_broker_mutation` says "Never raises". It raised [MEASURED — FIXED]

Found by D-3 sub-case (d). `activation_token.py:795` documents the contract; the **denial branch**
at `:844` re-computed `token_dir(directory)` outside the guard at `token_dir_is_inside_repo` that
had just caught the same exception, so `RuntimeError('Could not determine home directory.')`
escaped. `load_signing_key` had the same shape — path computed before its own `try` — which crashed
`describe_activation_state`, the operator's read-only status command. That is B103/J1 again.

Not exotic. `Path.expanduser()` raises whenever `~` cannot be resolved, the module's **default**
token dir is `~/.gtos/activation`, and a Windows service account with no `USERPROFILE` is D-6's
scenario exactly.

**Scope, measured rather than assumed: the escape is on the exposure-increasing path only.** A
close returns before any token I/O (instrumented in D-3, `read_token` call count 0 in all four
sub-cases), so the never-strand invariant was never at risk. Robustness defect, not the one that
costs money.

Fixed with `token_dir_display()` (never raises; renders `<unresolvable: … >` carrying the raw
value so the operator sees which path was tried) plus guarding `load_signing_key`'s path
computation. `src/safety/activation_token.py` is **not** decision-contract-bound — H1 checked
against R2's 43 paths. Regression test: `tests/safety/test_activation_unresolvable_token_dir.py`,
6 tests, including one that pins the close being untouched.

### B322 — D-8's dangerous branch is the ONE reachable path that can refuse a close [MEASURED]

Driven end to end through `RealMT5.order_send` against a fake module, no token present:

| `positions_get` returns | classification | close |
|---|---|---|
| `None` (the documented failure signal) | `risk_reducing_position_close_unverified` | **allowed** |
| raises | `risk_reducing_position_close_unverified` | **allowed** |
| a **stale non-empty tuple** omitting the live ticket | `exposure_increasing_deal_on_position` | **REFUSED** |

`positions_for_activation` is marked `@strict_positions_provider`, so "ticket absent" from a
non-empty read is authoritative absence, and a close then classifies as new exposure. D-8 named
the stale tuple as the dangerous answer without measuring it; this prices it. **D-8 is therefore
not merely unanswered — it is the gate on the only strand found.** It needs a demo account and
nothing else, and should run before the funded book carries a position through a terminal restart.

### B323 — D-7's strand is real and reachable at HEAD, and part of it is not blocked on D-7 [MEASURED]

A position reduced out-of-band to 0.01 while the engine believes 0.03 produces a **refused** close
with no token (`deal_reduces_existing_position` bounds volume at
`activation_token.py:530`). The correctly-sized close is allowed. So the B103 trade-off is live.

Whether the refusal is *right* depends on what MT5 does with an over-volume DEAL, which is D-7 and
cannot be answered here. But the mitigation the spec prescribes for the worst of the three outcomes
— **re-read the position volume immediately before building a close** — is safe under *all three*
and is therefore not blocked on the drill. Recorded, not implemented: it is an edit to
`execution.py`'s close producers and belongs with whoever owns that path.
