### B329 — The canary page, and the stop conditions pre-registered before the first fill [DELIVERED]

`scripts/canary_watch.py` — one command, one page, the five questions the prompt asked for. Read-
only, imports no broker module (pinned by a test), renders to stdout and optionally to a file. No
server: he is not going to run one.

`phase4/CANARY_STOP_CONDITIONS_V1.json` — C1 cost deviation · C2 swap and holding time · C3 sleeve
tripwires of the JPY kind · C4 book composition · C5 authority gates · C6 book alive · C7 no fills
· C8 drawdown headroom. Each states its measurement, its trigger, **the evidence the trigger came
from**, and what a fire would mean. Committed before any live fill exists, because a threshold
chosen after seeing the data is a rationalisation.

Three design decisions worth recording:

1. **Alerts, never halts.** The owner declined automatic stop conditions. Nothing in the tool can
   halt, flatten, resize, or move a gate, and it is not built so that it could.
2. **Exit 0 / 1 / 3**, not 0 / 1. "Nothing is wrong" and "nothing could be checked" are different
   states, and collapsing them is precisely how `monitor_books` read as all-clear while mute.
3. **Provenance on every number.** Balance and equity are `[input]` — the tool holds no broker
   connection. Several balance figures in circulation are claims; a page that renders claims and
   measurements in one typeface invites the reader to trust the wrong one.

C1's thresholds are anchored on a re-run of `scripts/reconcile_cost_layer_to_broker_truth.py`
(2026-07-29): mean absolute error **0.000535 R** over **175** fills, worst single fill
**0.006388 R**, pooled actual commission **0.05908 R**, null control (the shipped zero-commission
model) **0.05908 R**, ratio **110×**. Every figure the prompt supplied for the cost layer
reproduced exactly — the one inherited claim in the prompt that survived measurement unchanged.

### B330 — Every alert trigger is proven to go red, and three of my own tests passed for the wrong reason [MEASURED — FIXED]

The prompt's instruction was that a check which has only ever been seen green has tested nothing.
`tests/test_canary_watch.py` carries a red **and** a green fixture per condition (45 tests). That
was not sufficient. A mutation sweep — disable each of the 16 alert triggers in turn, require the
suite to fail — found three that survived:

- **C1**: the red fixture perturbed commission by a multiplier, which tripped the *single-fill*
  trigger as well, so the test passed with the *rolling* trigger disabled. Fixed by solving for a
  target error of 0.015 R — above the 0.01 R rolling threshold, below the 0.02 R single-fill one —
  so only one trigger can speak.
- **C5**: the red fixture flipped a gate with no token present, so the "gates are LIVE but no valid
  token" branch fired and the test passed with the gate comparison disabled. Fixed by minting a
  real token and arming fully, leaving one gate wrong.
- **C4's** generate-but-unweighted branch and **C5's** standing-token branch had no dedicated test
  at all.

After the repairs: **16 of 16 mutations caught.** The sweep is the receipt; the pass count is not.

### B331 — The joint P(0) of 0.075 is for FIVE sleeves, not three [CORRECTION]

C7 needed a calibrated silence horizon. The dossier (`OD3_DOSSIER_SURVIVOR_BOOK.md` item 6) and the
Session R prompt both give **0.075** as the empirical joint P(zero in 38 days) — and both say "for
all **five** silent together". Reading it as the three-sleeve joint would set the horizon roughly a
fortnight early, on the one alert whose entire design constraint is not to cry wolf.

C7 instead derives from the three published per-sleeve figures (0.369 `metals_core`, 0.284
`crypto`, 0.638 `energy_agri`): product 0.0669, per-day joint no-fire 0.0669^(1/38) = 0.9313,
days until P(silence) < 0.05 = **42.1**. Pre-registered at 42, and re-derived from the spec's own
inputs by a test so an edited threshold cannot pass as pre-registered.

**It is a lower bound on the horizon, and the tool says so.** The sleeves share a market regime;
the published five-sleeve joint (0.075) *exceeds* the independence product for those five, which is
evidence of positive dependence, which makes long joint silences more likely. So 42 days is the
earliest defensible point and the alarm errs toward silence — the right direction.

Also recorded from the same source, because it is easy to misread: `OD3_DOSSIER_SURVIVOR_BOOK.md`
item 8 states the script behind these rolling-window figures is **not committed**, only its outputs.
`phase3/receipts/G4_GENERATION_RATE.json` carries `p_fireday` (0.2615 / 0.1258 / 0.4090), which are
**different numbers** and not the rolling-window P(0). The C7 figures are therefore **cited, not
reproduced**, and the spec says so at the point of use.

### B333 — A float bug made ~11 % of position sizes impossible to close [MEASURED — FIXED]

**This outranks everything else in this session, and every drill I ran was one layer too low.**

`_normalize_volume` (`execution.py:2345` pre-fix) computed
`math.floor((lots - volume_min) / volume_step)` on a raw binary quotient. With
`volume_min == volume_step == 0.01`, `(0.03 - 0.01) / 0.01` is `1.9999999999999998`, so **0.03
normalized to 0.02** — and `_close_request_execution_geometry:2418` refuses any close whose
normalized volume differs from the requested one by more than 1e-9.

Why it is a strand and not a rounding nit:

- **nine** close producers route through that check (`:8005, 8162, 8215, 8331, 8405, 8482, 8547,
  8602, 8729`) — full close, TP1, TP2, final target, time stop, flatten;
- the live book **always** takes the verified-geometry branch, because
  `ultimate_book/execution_packets.py:318-319` sets both selected-cell risk fields that
  `_trade_requires_verified_broker_geometry` (`execution.py:1889-1893`) keys on;
- each producer returns **before** `safe_place_order`, so nothing ever reaches the activation-token
  layer — which is why eight chaos drills and X-1 all missed it;
- and there is **no recovery**: `book_owner.py` records `{action}_close_failed` and retries next
  tick, recomputing the identical volume, refused identically, forever.

Measured (mine, reproducing the refuter's claim independently rather than accepting it):

| geometry | volumes refused |
|---|---|
| `volume_min=0.01, step=0.01` | **33 of 300** two-decimal sizes |
| `volume_min=0.10, step=0.01` | **100 of 291** |
| `volume_min=0.01, step=0.001` | 42 of 300 |

And it was **not idempotent**: 14 reachable *normalized outputs* were themselves refused (0.29,
0.47, 0.57–0.59, 0.94, 1.13–1.19, 1.88), so the engine could place a position at a volume it could
never afterwards close.

**Against real broker data** — `vps-export-20260725/extracted/09_mt5_api/*_history_deals_get.jsonl`
priced against the same export's `*_symbol_specs_traded.json`: of **327** real close deals on the
two funded accounts, **44 (13.5 %)** carried a volume the engine would have refused, including
**8 of 78 (10.3 %)** engine-initiated (`DEAL_REASON_EXPERT`) closes. Real affected positions
existed on XAUUSD, BTCUSD, ETHUSD, GBPJPY, NDX100, US30 and JP225.cash.

**Fixed**: a step-count epsilon (`_VOLUME_STEP_EPSILON = 1e-9`) before the floor, plus an explicit
never-exceed clamp. The epsilon can only promote a quotient already within 1e-9 of an integer — a
lot size within 1e-11 of the next step, far below any broker's resolution — so a genuinely
mis-aligned volume still rounds **down**. `src/components/execution.py` is **not**
decision-contract-bound (H1 checked against R2).

`tests/test_execution_volume_normalization.py`, 22 tests: every broker-valid volume round-trips
across five geometries; normalization never rounds up; off-grid volumes still round down onto the
grid; idempotence; sub-minimum still refused; `volume_max` still caps; the legacy
`require_broker_geometry=False` branch untouched; and the 327 real broker deals now yield **zero**
refusals. Reverting the fix fails 7 of the 22, so the suite is not vacuous.

> **One consequence needs Borhen's explicit blessing.** The same function serves the entry path, so
> an entry asking for 0.03 lots now places **0.03** instead of 0.02 — a one-step size increase in
> the ~11 % of cases affected. That is the *correct* behaviour (the engine gets the size it decided)
> and the truncation was never a deliberate policy, but it is a change to placed size on a live
> funded account, and §1 reserves the risk dial to him. Flagged, not assumed.

### B334 — Two more close-refusal paths above the token layer, recorded not fixed [MEASURED]

Both found by the same adversarial pass, both verified by me at source.

**`live_broker_authority: false` strands open positions.** `book_owner.py:2344-2353` returns before
flattening anything, recording `flatten_request_observed_broker_mutation_disabled`; `:2506-2517`
skips routine exit management as observe-only. So the natural "stop it now" reflex — shutting the
brake — leaves every open position with **no exit management at all**. Operationally the rule is
**flatten first, then shut the gate**, and that is now the second item in the operator page's
close-refusal section. Not fixed: making the gate close-permissive is a change to what a brake
means, and that is the owner's call.

**A runtime halt refuses closes, and its risk-reducing carve-out uses the lossy reader.**
`execution.py:530` calls `self.mt5.get_positions(request.get("symbol") or self.symbol) or []` —
which masks a failed broker read as `[]` (`mt5_real.py:324-325`) and filters by magic (`:335`).
That is the **exact** defect B101 repaired at the activation layer, still live one layer up: under
an active halt, a close of an adopted or foreign-magic position, or one attempted during a
transient read failure, is refused with `runtime_halt_active_no_order_send`. Narrower than B333 —
it needs a halt to be active, and a halt is a deliberate operator act — but it is the same shape,
and the single-definition rule the token layer adopted has not reached this call site's *reader*.

Also corrected: **CLAUDE.md H6's sentence "There is no longer a raw `mt5.order_send` in the
repository outside the gated engine path" is false as written.**
`scripts/flatten_all_positions.py:49` and `scripts/emergency_close_and_stop_redacted_account.py:304,360`
call the raw module with no activation gate and no halt guard. That is **deliberate** — both are
listed with their arguments in `tests/safety/test_activation_token.py::_DECLARED_MUTATION_SITES`,
and both are pure flattens, so gating them would only add a way for an emergency flatten to fail.
The design is right; the sentence overstates it. Not edited here: CLAUDE.md is the root briefing and
three sessions are in flight against it.

### B336 — I pre-registered a swap threshold without measuring it, and it would have cried wolf from day one [MEASURED — FIXED]

C1's commission threshold was derived from a re-run of the reconciliation receipt: baseline mean
|error| **0.000535 R** over 175 fills, so 0.01 R is ~19× baseline and above the worst single fill.
C2's swap threshold was set to **the same 0.01 R** — by copying it, not by measuring swap.

Measured, on the same 175-fill corpus, `cost_r`'s `swap_r` against realized swap:

| | mean \|err\| | p50 | p90 | p95 | p99 | worst |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| commission | 0.000535 | — | — | — | — | 0.006388 |
| **swap** | **0.010324** | 0.001671 | 0.023763 | 0.058044 | 0.158322 | **0.195101** |

**The swap baseline mean error is above the threshold I pre-registered for it.** On chronological
rolling-5 windows, **39 of 171 (22.8 %)** of the baseline corpus exceed 0.01 R. The alert would
have fired on the very data its thresholds were derived from, on the one page whose entire design
constraint is not to cry wolf.

Re-derived from the measured distribution: rolling-5 at **0.10 R** — the smallest round value above
the worst chronological rolling-5 window the corpus produces (0.0943) — which fires on **0 of 171**.
Single fill at **0.25 R**, above the worst ever measured (0.1951). Guarded by
`test_c2_swap_does_not_fire_on_the_BASELINE_corpus`, plus a test pinning the *relationship* so a
future edit cannot drop the threshold back below the baseline.

**The substantive finding underneath the correction:** the swap model is **19× less accurate** than
the commission model and its coverage is `MODELLED`, not `MEASURED`. Swap is the largest single
broker cost for eight of eleven sleeves, and holding time is what OD-3 now waits on — so the weaker
half of the cost layer is carrying the more decision-relevant quantity. C2's band is an order of
magnitude wider than C1's, and that width is the measurement, not a tuning choice.

This is the same error §3 item 6 of the working agreement records against the orchestrator —
asserting where a measurement was cheap — committed by me, inside the artifact whose stated purpose
is that thresholds are derived rather than chosen. Recorded rather than quietly amended.

### B356 — My own conflict resolver silently dropped a 147-line section [CORRECTION]

Recorded because it is the exact defect the prompt sent me to look for, produced by the tool written
to prevent it. The throwaway helper that resolves append-shaped conflicts printed *"1 append-hunk
resolved, both sides kept"* while keeping only theirs, discarding **all 147 lines of Session Q's
section**. Cause: its conflict regex used `.*` for the marker labels under `re.S`, so the greedy
label swallowed the entire ours-side and the `ours` group matched empty.

**It was caught by grepping for the section headings immediately after, not by the tool** — the
merged file had `## B200–B221` and `## B260–B289` and no `## B230–B244`. The helper now pins the
resolved line count against before-minus-markers and refuses when a side is lost. Two lessons, both
cheap: label groups must be `[^\n]*`, and a resolution step needs an assertion that does not come
from the same code as the resolution.

A second, smaller artifact of the same conflicts: git places the shared `\n---\n` separator block
*before* the conflict region, so a literal both-sides concatenation runs one session's last
paragraph straight into the next session's `##` heading. It happened twice (Q→R, R→S) and was
repaired by hand both times.

### B365 — `--tags` does not bound the conviction count within a decision day, and arming mid-day is +25 % size [MEASURED — REFUTES B359]

Found by an adversarial pass sent to break this session's own CLAUDE.md corrections, and it is the
most decision-bearing thing wave 4 produced after the strand fix.

**Struck from B359:** *"the Kelly-lite conviction multiplier keys on sleeves firing that day, so
`--tags` bounds it."* The first half is true; the inference is not.
`RunningConvictionLedger` (`running_conviction_state.py:33-82`) **persists** a per-`decision_day`
union of firing sleeves to `pipeline_state/ultimate_book/<namespace>/firing_sleeves.json`, and
`admission.py:1188` takes `na = max(na, n_active_override.get(day, 0))` — **monotone upward within
the day**, wired at `book_engine.py:761`.

It is armed on the live account: `kelly_lite: true` (`agent_config.yaml:1303`),
`kelly_conservative: true` (`:1304`), `kelly_running_count: true` (`:1305`). The exported VPS ledgers
carry **6–7 distinct firing sleeves per day** (FTMO 2026-07-24: 7, mostly candidate/expansion
sleeves, not the W7 eleven). So a **restart mid-decision-day under a narrow `--tags` inherits that
day's wider firing set**: under the half-Kelly bins `((1,1,0.748),(2,3,0.991),(4,99,1.241))`, an `na`
of 2 → 7 moves the multiplier 0.991 → 1.241, **+25.2 % on every unit placed that day.**

**Mitigation, and it belongs in the arming ceremony: arm at a decision-day boundary, or delete that
namespace's `firing_sleeves.json` first.** `_KEEP_DAYS = 2` plus today-only return keys mean a stale
prior day cannot contaminate a fresh one — the hazard is same-day only.

Two `--tags` failure modes from the same pass, both worth knowing before the ceremony: `--tags ""`
is falsy at `run_book.py:340`, so an empty string silently means **all BUILT sleeves** (fail-open);
an all-typo `--tags` produces an empty spec list and the book stands down silently every tick
(`registry.py:144` drops unknown tags with no fallback and no error — fail-closed, but mute).

### B367 — The guard I synthesized had a hole big enough to drive a wave through [CORRECTION — FIXED]

B352 replaced R's and S's declaration check with T's looser `_allocated` applied to **both**
endpoints. R and S had deliberately kept the **lower** bound strict (`f"B{lo}" in agreement`) and
loosened only the upper one. I did not notice that asymmetry was load-bearing, and dropped it.

An adversarial pass priced the loss. `WAVE_4_WORKING_AGREEMENT.md` contains **57 of the integers
0–999** somewhere in its prose — section numbers, percentages, counts — and **31 of them have no
`B{n}` anywhere**. So `((71, 969), "WAVE_4_WORKING_AGREEMENT.md")` **passed all eight tests in the
file** while exempting every unwritten citation from B71 to B969 as a "forward allocation". The
blanket-hole control only catches ranges straddling B56 or B58; that one cleared both.

Fixed with something stricter than any of the three inputs: `_declared_as_one_range(lo, hi,
agreement)` requires the pair to appear as **one row of the allocation table** —
`rf"(?<![0-9])B{lo}\s*[–—-]\s*B?{hi}(?![0-9])"` — so the exemption is traceable to a single
allocation rather than to two numbers that happen to share a document. Both spellings of the upper
bound are still accepted, which was T's point and survives. Verified: `(380,409)`, `(350,379)` and
`(260,289)` pass; `(71,969)`, `(0,969)`, `(43,694)`, `(30,650)`, `(5,8)` all fail.

**And the same pass found the entry is currently inert, which I had asserted away rather than
measured.** The block ceiling is B364 and the one declared range is (380, 409), entirely above it —
so emptying `IN_FLIGHT_WAVE_RANGES` changes the forward-allocation set not at all. My `assert
IN_FLIGHT_WAVE_RANGES` guard checked non-emptiness and could not see that. The test now classifies
each entry as **ACTIVE** (it exempts a citation the ceiling does not) or **PRE-DECLARATION** (it sits
entirely above the ceiling and starts working when that wave writes its first block) and **refuses a
DEAD entry** — below the ceiling and exempting nothing, which is a hole waiting for a typo.

Three more of the same class, all from the prose audit, all fixed here:

- **`WAVE_4_WORKING_AGREEMENT.md` still said Q was "not yet merged"** and still said the account is
  being armed "on three sleeves" — the *fourth* place wave 4 says three, and a fourth distinct
  meaning. Both corrected in place; the armed-set correction is flagged as such because that document

- **Q's range was tabled two ways** — `B230–B244` in the wave-4 agreement and `CLAUDE.md`,

### B369 — Two of the strand fix's five stated invariants are false as written; both are unreachable on either funded account [MEASURED]

An adversarial pass attacked the fix arithmetic rather than the tests. It could not break it where it
matters and did break two claims about it. **The fix is kept unchanged** — this was an integration
session and the money path is not the place for a late arithmetic edit — and the comment in
`execution.py` now states exactly what holds.

| stated invariant | verdict |
|---|---|
| every broker-valid volume round-trips | **false in general**, true where it matters: it fails at step-counts above ~1.7e7, and all **42** traded symbol specs on both funded accounts are `(min 0.01, step 0.01)` with `volume_max` ≤ 1000, i.e. max step-count 99,999 — a ~100× margin. An **exhaustive sweep of all 99,999 grid points** post-fix: 0 failures (pre-fix: 7,534). |
| nothing ever rounds UP | **false.** The clamp falls back to `round(lots, 8)`, which rounds to nearest. 145 inputs return up to ~5e-9 lots **above** the request. Economically nil; `test_normalization_never_rounds_up`'s 1e-12 tolerance cannot detect it. |
| sub-minimum is still refused | **false, and this one is a regression the clamp introduced.** With `volume_max < volume_min` (nothing validates that ordering), `lots=5.0` at `(0.10, 0.01, 0.05)` returns **0.05** — below the minimum and off-grid — where the pre-fix code returned 0.10. No real broker presents this geometry. |
| a mis-aligned volume still rounds DOWN | **holds** across 43,194 fuzz pairs over 19 geometries against an exact `Decimal` reference |
| `volume_max` still caps | **holds** — no over-max case found in the same sweep |

**The repair for both defects is one line and is handed on, not made here:** the clamp should step
DOWN to the largest grid point ≤ `lots` and return `None` if that is below `volume_min`, never
`round(lots, 8)`.

Also corrected in the shipped artifact: the comment said `(0.03 - 0.01) / 0.01` is
`1.9999999999999998`; it is **`1.9999999999999996`**. And **all ten line citations in that comment
were stale** — the 34-line comment shifted the very lines it cited, so `:8215` came to point at
`result = self.safe_place_order(request)`, the exact call the comment says is never reached. Replaced
with a grep target that cannot rot.

**Test-suite weakness worth carrying:** 15 of the 22 tests are **non-discriminating** — they pass
identically with the fix reverted (all five `never_rounds_up` params, all five `rounds_down` params,
one round-trip param, and the four guard tests). The 7 that do discriminate are the ones B353 used.
And every parametrized sweep stops at `lots = 30.00` while `volume_max` is 1000, so the tests cover
**3 %** of the permitted lot range; the adversarial pass closed that gap by exhaustive sweep and it
is clean.

**Data or dependency absence: 344 (56.0 %). Code-shaped: 237 (38.6 %).** So §5's claim that a large

**B430 — a `min_oos_positive_fold_frac` of 0.50 is the coin-flip point and carries no
information; an absolute leave-one-out floor is scale-blind.** Found by this session's own
adversarial test before any refuter ran. A synthetic sleeve with all its edge inside one fold
(fold means 0.167, −0.180, **3.175**, 0.033, 0.070) pooled to **+0.653 R/day**, retained
**+0.0225** once its best fold was deleted — comfortably "> 0.0" — and reached ADMIT. Replaced
with a scale-free retention ratio (`min_drop_best_fold_retention`, 0.50 at B / 0.60 at A) plus a
raised positive-fold floor. The same adversary now rejects at 3.4% retention. [MEASURED]

**B431 — three concealment attacks, one mechanism, and one of them admitted a sleeve that lost
17,840 R.** An adversarial refuter landed 6 of 8 attacks, including on the strictest option. A
sleeve of 23,325 trades, 22,740 losers, lifetime −17,840 R passed all seven gates with q 0.0285.
Mechanism: put the losses where the scored statistic does not look. (a) Fold 0 is never scored —
50,000 losing trades placed there changed the scored numbers **bit-identically** and still counted
toward `min_trades_total`. (b) Day-mean aggregation weighs a day with 12 losers the same as a day
with 1 winner — 2,688 losers of 2,913 trades, −715.8 R lifetime, ADMITTED at all three options.
(c) Blackout drops were reported as a **count**: 2,200 losers took a sleeve from +94.7 R to
−2,105 R with every scored number frozen. Fixed by a `lifetime` gate over every priced trade
including fold 0, a per-**trade** expectancy floor beside the per-**day** one, publishing blackout
R, and counting only scored-fold trades toward the sample floor. [MEASURED]

**B432 — the significance gate was mathematically unpassable in a reachable regime.** A block
sign-flip null over B blocks has only `2**B` distinct outcomes, so its smallest attainable p is
`(1 + n_perm*2**-B)/(n_perm+1)` regardless of `n_perm`; `max(p_boot, p_perm)` promotes that to the
gate's floor. `block_length_auto` used `2/sqrt(n)` — a **significance** threshold, not a
**decorrelation** criterion — and pinned the block at the `n//4` cap when no lag qualified,
forcing B=4 and a floor of **0.0626**, above every threshold all three options can set. A series
with mean +0.2793 R/day and a naive one-sided t of **13.49** produced gate p **0.1254**; sweeping
the block on the same series moved the decision statistic **1250×**. Now: AR(1) decorrelation
length `ceil(ln(0.01)/ln|rho1|)`, cap `n//min_blocks` with `min_blocks=8`, `perm_p_floor`
published, and a sleeve whose floor is at or above alpha is **NOT_EVALUABLE rather than REJECT** —
a statement about the evidence, not the sleeve. [MEASURED]

**B433 — the day-block correction is real but incomplete, and the residual is documented.**
Measured over 500 replications at n=250: at rho=0.4 the naive iid t-test rejects at 0.154 against
a nominal 0.05 (3.1×) while the gate rejects at 0.060 (1.2×); at rho=0.7 naive 0.264, gate 0.104
(2.1×). Forcing a longer block closes it (0.043 at L=30), which is what attributes the residual to
the block rule rather than to either test. Under a true iid null the bootstrap p is uniform
(KS 0.0148–0.0236 against a 0.0304 critical value over 2,000 replications). [MEASURED]

**B434 — `regime_inflation`'s contamination flag has a sign error and is defeated monotonically by
making the concealed loss bigger.** `validation_integrity/regime_inflation.py:239` computes
`fwd_all_mean_ratio = mean_in_window / mean_all` and `:303-305` flag on `ratio >= 1.5`, a
**positive** threshold. Once `mean_all` goes negative the ratio goes negative and the flag can
never fire. Measured: 0 hidden losers → ratio 0.862, flag False; 500 → ratio **−0.847**, flag
False; 50,000 → ratio −0.847, flag False, verdict string still `"CLEAN: selection window is
representative"`. `:294-295` guards `ratio > 0` so the haircut also collapses to its 0.05 floor.
Same sign-error family as F39. Guarded at `walkforward/gate.py`'s call site (a negative ratio is
treated as contamination); **the module itself is untouched and needs a fix.** [MEASURED]

**B435 — the broker-truth cost artifact is a look-ahead, it is first-order, and its bias direction
is knowable.** `TICK_SPREAD_MEASUREMENT.json` measures spread over broker wall clock
**2026-06-18 → 2026-07-24** — 37 days — and `cost_r` charges that single p50 as a constant to
every trade regardless of era (`model.py:347-372`); commission is fitted from the same July-2026
deal export and swap from current symbol specs. The mx pilot's panel runs 2007–2026 with only
**175 of 2,675 trades (6.54%)** in 2026 at all. Cost came to **33%–219% of gross R** and flipped
`mx_ger40` (+0.094 → −0.023) and `mx_us30` (+0.048 → −0.057) from gross-positive to net-negative
on its own. Retail CFD/FX spreads compressed over 2007–2026, so historical trades are
systematically **under**-costed and every pooled OOS mean is **optimistic by an unmeasured
amount**. Unavoidable with the archive that exists; now stamped on every gate result. [MEASURED]

**B436 — 22.0% of the pilot's generated rows were duplicates, because the driver did not apply
live's own idempotency key.** Live places each `(sleeve, symbol, decision_bar)` at most once —
`book_owner.py:163`, enforced by `PlacementLedger`, with `decision_bar_iso` named as the key at
`book_engine.py:546-548`. Driving the **union** of every symbol's D1 closes re-fires a 5-day
symbol's last closed bar on the weekend instants contributed by 7-day crypto symbols, which the
staleness guard permits for two intervals. Measured: **589 of 2,675 rows (22.0%)**, reaching 36%
on the FX/index sleeves and 0.5–11% on crypto — 2/7 = 28.6%, the shape of the cause. Verdicts do
not move (duplicates are byte-identical so the day-**mean** is unchanged) but the sample gate,
which counts trades rather than days, had been told it had 28% more evidence than it had.
[MEASURED]

**B437 — a purged trade's outcome re-entered the train set through any surviving trade sharing its
entry day.** The purge is a trade-level filter that produced a set of **days**, and the train
series was then read out of the pre-computed day-mean panel. Two trades on 2023-12-20 — one kept,
one purged for closing inside the test fold — yielded a train value of 1.5 = mean(−1.0, +4.0)
while the receipt reported `n_purged_trades: 1`. Measured blast radius on the mx family: **0 of
4,151 train days**, because one-symbol D1 sleeves carry at most one distinct trade per day. It is
guaranteed to fire on `sub_xvol_pullback` (12 trades on one date) and the M15 JPY sleeves. It
could not have flipped a verdict — `train_r` enters no gate — but it corrupted the published
IS→OOS degradation. Train days are now re-aggregated from surviving trades only. [MEASURED]

**B438 — the fidelity gate keyed on the sleeve name alone, so relabelling bypassed it.**
Identical trades named `asia_pdl_fade` (30% live-recall, first-of-day) → NOT_EVALUABLE; renamed
`crypto` → **ADMIT, q 0.00510**. Fixed with `GateSpec.sleeve_symbol_allowlist`, built from the
production resolvers by `walkforward/registry.build_symbol_allowlist` — which calls
`admission.effective_registry` and `symbol_map.build_broker_symbol_resolver` rather than crossing
the boundary by hand. When no allowlist is supplied the gate records that the check was **skipped**
rather than passing it silently. [MEASURED]

**B439 — cost is a price drag over the declared stop, and nothing cross-checked the stop.** The
same XAUUSD trades at gross +0.11 R: `sl=$5` → cost 0.1006 R → REJECT (p 0.337); `sl=$20` → cost
0.0274 R → ADMIT (p 0.0127); `sl=$60` → ADMIT (p 0.0044). Both are plausible gold stops.
`sl_distance_price=1e6` was accepted silently, flooring cost at the flat slippage term. Fixed with
a sealed `sl_over_price_band` (default 1e-5 .. 0.5); a trade outside it is refused as implausible
rather than priced. [MEASURED]

**B440 — multiplicity is corrected within a run, so submitting sleeves singly launders the
correction 13–18×.** 20 zero-edge sleeves over 60 seeds: judged together (m=20) **6** admits;
judged one at a time (m=1) **79** admits at B_balanced. P(at least one junk admission per
campaign) goes **8.3% → 71.7%** at B and 3.3% → 46.7% at A. A family of one also silently disables
both overfitting diagnostics — DSR needs ≥2 sleeves for its cross-trial Sharpe variance and PBO
needs ≥2 columns. Mitigated with `declared_family_size` (the correction uses
`max(actual, declared)`); it is on the caller's honour because **no persistent trial ledger exists
in this repo** — `validation_integrity/trial_budget_ledger.py` can build one and has never been
run. [MEASURED]

**B441 — thin folds created a perverse incentive: trading less in a bad regime bought a pass.** A
fold whose test side falls below `min_trades_per_fold` was excluded from the pooled statistic and
from the stability count. Measured at A_strict: **7 losers in a bad fold → ADMIT** (positive-fold
fraction 1.0); **8 losers → REJECT** (0.8). Adding one more loss flipped the verdict. Thin folds
now count as non-positive in the stability denominator and are capped by `max_thin_fold_frac`.
[MEASURED]

**B442 — the entry-convention divergence was published as an absolute value, overstating it 107×
in the flattering direction.** The pilot compares entry at the decision bar's close against the
sleeve's next-open contract (`market_expansion_d1.py:5-8`). Reporting `|next_open − close|/stop`
gave a mean of 0.077 R and invited the reader to assume a large advantage. The signed,
direction-adjusted quantity is **+0.00152 R** — seven of ten sleeves positive, i.e. close entry is
marginally **disadvantaged**, and `mx_btcusd`, the only sleeve near significance, is +0.0079
against itself. Now published signed. [MEASURED]

**B443 — what the refuters could NOT break, measured rather than assumed.** The circular block
bootstrap is Efron & Tibshirani Algorithm 16.1 verbatim and its p is uniform under a true null
(KS 0.0148–0.0236 vs a 0.0304 critical value, 2,000 replications). `max(p_boot, p_perm)` is a
valid conservative p-value. `benjamini_hochberg` agrees with `statsmodels.multipletests(fdr_bh)`
bit-for-bit on rejections **and** q-values across the BH-1995 reference table, non-monotone input,
and exact ties. `simulate_detail` reads nothing at the decision bar except its close — 4,000
random paths with the decision bar's o/h/l/v poisoned differed on **0**. The embargo is genuinely
train-side: replacing in-fold holds with 90-day holds left it unchanged. [MEASURED]

## B511 [MEASURED] The builder's partition guard was fail-open in three compounding ways

`learned_edge_dataset_builder.py` at the parent commit:

1. `--registry` was optional (`:754`); `--out` and `--route-dir` were `required=True`, it was not.
2. `partition_role_for_day` returned `(None, None)` for any day no partition covers (`:684`).
3. The only refusal was `role == "SEALED"` (`:710`).

Omitted, every row got `partition_role: None`, which is not `"SEALED"`, so `SealedPartitionError`
could not be raised at all. A day covered by no partition passed for the same reason. The frame
was written to disk containing those rows.

Mitigated one stage downstream **by accident, not design**: `learned_edge_trainer.py:542` kept
only rows whose `partition_role` was in `("TRAIN", "TRAIN_DEVELOPMENT_GRADE")`, and `"None"`
matches neither, so training raised. The frame artifact itself was still unsafe.

## B513 [MEASURED] The trainer had no purge and no embargo, and its docstring said otherwise

`learned_edge_trainer._train_head_with_oof` split folds as
`train = [r for r in eligible if r.get("fold_key") != fold_day]`. That is leave-one-day-out:
**every future day is in train**. No purge, no embargo anywhere in the module. The docstring at
`:550-552` claimed "Week blocks keep the purge/embargo boundary at the block edge (>= the 48h
label horizon...)"; no code implemented it. The v1 registry header states the intended doctrine —
"Purge = 48h label horizon; embargo = 1 trading day at every train/validation boundary" — as prose
with no enforcement.

Second, smaller leak in the same function: `numeric_specs = _numeric_specs(rows)` was computed
once over ALL rows including out-of-fold test rows, and reused in every fold, so the scaler's
mean/std and 0.5%/99.5% clip bounds were fitted on data the fold was about to be scored on.

## B518 [MEASURED] regime_inflation.py was still broken on main, and worse than described

Unchanged since the foundation snapshot `95105914f` — Session X did not fix it. Measured:

| pre-window daily R | `fwd_all_mean_ratio` | `contamination_flag` | `regime_basis_haircut` |
|---:|---:|---|---:|
| -0.05 | +18.18 | True | 0.055 |
| -0.50 | -2.86 | **False** | **1.000** |
| -5.00 | -0.23 | **False** | **1.000** |
| -50.00 | -0.02 | **False** | **1.000** |

The ratio is only an inflation factor when `mean_all > 0`. Once the concealed loss drags the
full-history mean below zero the ratio goes negative, both thresholds (`>= 1.5`, `>= 1.2`) fail,
and the haircut falls through to 1.0 — **no haircut at all** — for the single worst case there is:
a strategy positive only inside its own selection window. The detector got quieter the worse the
strategy was. Same sign-error family as F38/F39.

Fixed by handling the three regimes explicitly (`mean_all > 0`; `mean_all <= 0 < mean_win`;
`mean_win <= 0`) and adding `regime_sign_inversion`, which fires unconditionally and takes the
haircut floor. All four rows above now flag True at haircut 0.05. Known-answer test
`test_vig_regime_inflation.py` still passes (3/3).

### B558 — The supervisor never stops a book, and the crash loop is ~33 s, not 5 minutes [MEASURED]

Read from the host's own `scripts/run_book_supervisor.ps1` — **18,991 bytes at `redacted_host`, against
the 6,980-byte copy vendored into mainline's `scripts/`. The two have forked**, and the running one
is the larger.

`Test-BookRunning` (`:175-215`) returns `$false` **only** when zero matching `run_book.py` processes
exist. Every other branch returns `$true`, including the stale-heartbeat branch, which logs
`alert_only_no_forced_restart open_position_safety`. So the "supervisor only ever starts a book"
property holds for the version actually running, not just for the vendored one.

A book that dies at load leaves zero processes and is restarted on the next supervisor pass:
`Start-Sleep -Seconds 30` plus a 3 s settle — **~33 s**. The five minutes in this session's prompt is
the scheduled task's re-fire interval, which only matters if the supervisor itself is gone.

### B559 — A crash loop is not an unprotected position: 175 of 175 live book orders carry a broker-side stop [MEASURED]

The book sends `sl` and `tp` with the entry itself (host `execution.py:3674-3675`). Over the host's
own order history (`vps-export-20260725/.../{ftmo,redacted_account}_history_orders_get.jsonl`), of **175**
`W7:`-tagged orders with volume, **175 carry a non-zero `sl`** — 97/97 FTMO, 78/78 redacted_account —
and 127 carry a non-zero `tp`.

So a module-load crash loop costs **exit management and the breach flatten**: no break-even move, no
trailing, no time stop, no partial, no `_apply_breach_flatten`. It does not cost the stop, which
lives on the broker's server and survives any number of restarts. That is still bad enough to order
around, and it is not "naked and unmanaged" — the distinction is what lets an operator decide calmly
instead of fast.

### B560 — The kill flag is the brake and it does not stop the process [MEASURED]

`launcher.py:204-211`: `tick()` computes `place = not (killed or halted)`. The flag pauses
**placement**; the process keeps running and keeps managing open positions, and the supervisor
restarts nothing because nothing is missing. `Stop-Process` is the code-swap mechanism, used exactly
once, and it is not a brake. The runbook pauses with the flag first and releases it last, so at every
point before the restart the operator has a zero-cost way to stop.

### B561 — `.tools/monitor_books.py` belongs in this carry, and the reason is a defect, not a schedule [MEASURED]

Two live processes run it (`--loop 300`), and it is the only thing alerting on the daily-loss rule of
the account being armed. `SRV_OFFSET_H = 3   # FTMO/FN server = UTC+3 (EEST)` drives `srv_today`,
which selects which deals count toward `realized_today` → `daily_pl_pct` → the **−4.5 % "NEAR −5 %
HARD LIMIT"** and −2.5 % soft-stop alerts. It is wrong twice over, both times in the same dangerous
direction:

1. the label is wrong (both servers run the **US** calendar, not EET/EEST) and the number is dated —
   both drop to **+2 on 2026-11-01** while the constant would not;
2. the server clock is not FTMO's reset rule at all, so the monitor's "today" is 1–2 h early for
   FTMO exactly as the governor's was.

Demonstrated: a real losing deal at 2026-10-27 20:00 UTC on FTMO is **counted** by the carried
monitor and **dropped** by the struck code, because `srv_today` had already rolled to 2026-10-28.
Fixing the governor and leaving this would make the risk layer and the alerting layer disagree about
which day it is.

**It is carried surgically (2 anchored edits, not mainline's 255-line divergence) and ordered as a
separate stage D, after the books are healthy.** No book imports it, so it cannot affect the book
restart, and the supervisor restarts it on its own within ~30 s. The window is now computed as an
**instant** rather than a date, because a CE(S)T date compared against a broker-wall date is a type
error wearing a fix; deal times are converted with `broker_epoch_to_utc` under the server rule.

### B564 — The runbook's own health gate was a false negative, in both directions [MEASURED — FIXED]

The first draft told the operator to confirm the kill flag had taken by looking for
`PLACEMENT PAUSED` in `shadow_logs/run_book_console.log`. That string never reaches that file:
`launcher.py:183-199` sends it to `notify_alert`, a push channel. And `tick()` returns early on
`no_new_bar` **without logging** (`:265`), so a healthy H4 book legitimately writes nothing there for
hours. The instruction would have produced either "the flag did not take" or a STOP on a healthy
book.

Both gates now use the per-namespace **heartbeat** (`launcher.py:120-140`), written at the top of
every tick before any broker call, on the same tick that re-evaluates `killed()`. A heartbeat stamped
after the flag file's mtime **proves** that book evaluated the flag. Parsed with
`[datetimeoffset]::Parse(...).UtcDateTime` — the exact idiom the host's own supervisor uses
(`run_book_supervisor.ps1:144-163`), so it is known-good on Windows PowerShell 5.1 rather than
assumed.

### B566 — The reset window moved an hour at every EU DST seam, in the shortening direction [MEASURED — FIXED]

Found by a refuter, not by me. `_reset_window_start_utc` subtracted the offset **at `now`** from a
local midnight that had occurred under the **previous** offset. True on 363 days a year; on the two
the CE(S)T calendar shifts, the window start moved:

| seam | window start moves | effect |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-03-29T01:00Z (spring) | 23:00Z → 22:00Z | window lengthens — conservative |
| **2026-10-25T01:00Z (autumn)** | 22:00Z → **23:00Z** | **window shortens; an hour of realized loss drops out of the daily budget** |

Same direction as the defect B56 exists to fix. Not a regression — the host has the identical defect
at the US dates — and largely absorbed by `_balance_anchor`'s `max()`, whose date key the refuter
verified stable across the seam; both seams are 01:00 UTC on a Sunday, inside the FX weekend, so only
crypto is open. Repaired anyway, because "small and in the dangerous direction" is what this session
is for.

Fix: one correction pass — re-evaluate the offset at the candidate instant and redo the subtraction
if it disagrees. **17,520 hourly probes across 2026–2027: 0 not at 00:00 CE(S)T, 0 backwards steps**
(before: 4 seam events over the same span). The detected-offset path is untouched by construction —
`offset_provider` takes no instant. 8 new tests in `tests/ultimate_book/test_daily_reset_rule.py`
(43 → 51); reverting the fix fails 7 of them.

### B570 — The verifier's authority gate could not pass at the step that runs it [MEASURED — FIXED]

`--check postflight` demanded the carried sha for **every** plan entry, including stage D — which
the runbook deliberately defers to §10. So at §6, where the runbook says "all three must exit 0",
a correct carry exited **2**, one step before the one-way door. That teaches an operator either to
roll back a good carry or to walk past a red gate, and the second is worse.

**No test executed the verifier at all**, which is why it survived; the tests read its source and
its manifest. Five tests now run it, including one asserting exit 0 in the exact §6 state and one
that truncates a carried file and asserts `postflight` sees it.

`--check behaviour` had the mirror defect at §10: it emits `say(None, …)` for an absent stage D, so
it exits 0 whether or not the monitor landed. §10 now gates on a new `--check stage-d`, which fails
unless the monitor is at the carried sha, `broker_clock.py` is present, and the window it computes
agrees with the governor's.

### B571 — Four more ways the runbook produced a confident wrong answer [MEASURED — FIXED]

All found by the runbook refuter, all in the class "an empty variable reads as success".

1. **`$backup` left as `"<the path printed in section 3>"`** is a valid PowerShell string. `Test-Path`
   then missed on all ten targets and the **delete arm fired anyway** — removing `broker_clock.py`
   while leaving `governor_state.py` carried. §9 is now one scriptblock with
   `$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"` and real `throw` guards, and a delete is authorised only by the
   backup manifest's own record that the file was absent.
2. **`"rollback exit: $LASTEXITCODE"` printed a stale `0`.** In a crash loop each book lives ~2 s per
   ~33 s cycle, so `$exes` is very often empty exactly when §9 is needed; `$exes[0]` is `$null` with
   no StrictMode, the `Write-Host "STOP"` did not stop, and `& $null` never updates `$LASTEXITCODE`.
   Now `$ok = $?` as well.
3. **Nothing checked the supervisor was alive before `Stop-Process`.** It has three `exit` paths
   before its loop and its own header says it can hang. §7.1 checks process **and** heartbeat, and
   §7.3 now distinguishes "the books cannot start" (roll back) from "the supervisor is down" (do not
   — the scheduled task re-fires in 5 min, which is **longer** than the 3-minute rollback trigger).
4. **§8's new-pid assertion passed silently on an empty `$oldPids`** — the only check that the books
   are on the carried code. `$null -contains X` is `$false`, so it printed `new_pid=True` for books
   that were never restarted, under the sentence "the books are now on the carried code".

Plus: Session S's `packet_carry` is not on `main` and the runbook never said where to get it, so an
operator was blocked at §1; §10's 60 s wait was shorter than the supervisor's real ~35–40 s loop;
`--check imports` covered one of the eight modules `run_book.py` imports at module top; and the
verifier's docstring claimed "nothing is written outside a temporary directory" while exec'ing the
carried monitor calls `load_dotenv(override=True)`.

### B572 — What the refuters could not break [MEASURED]

Published because a refuter that only ever confirms is worth nothing, and these are the claims the
carry rests on.

* **The construction.** 1,080,000 bitwise comparisons of the carried `_normalize_volume` against
  Session T's, across 18 geometries including `volume_step=1e-8`, denormals, `±inf`, NaN and
  `nextafter` neighbours: **0 disagreements**. 4,549,807 broker-rejectability probes over 13 real MT5
  geometries: **0** results above `volume_max`, below `volume_min`, zero-volume or off-grid. Eight
  mutations of the build inputs → **8/8 named `SystemExit`**; there is no silent-wrong path.
* **The config-free claim, and it is stronger than stated.** `apply_profile_overrides` deep-merges
  (0 of 659 base keys dropped, both profiles); `rt is merged["gtos_vnext_runtime"]` is `True`; there
  is exactly **one** non-test construction site for each of `UltimateBookLiveEngine` and
  `UltimateBookOwner` in the whole host tree. **All three of `operator_profile.yaml`,
  `ftmo.yaml` and `agent_config.yaml` are decision-contract-bound in R2 — and none of the five
  carried files is.**
* **`broker_clock`'s DST arithmetic.** 26,304 hourly comparisons against `zoneinfo`, 2026–2028, on
  all four rules: **0 disagreements**. Imports, by AST: `__future__`, `dataclasses`, `datetime`, and
  nothing else; it loads under `python3 -I -S`.
* **The two original invariants.** Independently re-enumerated with the host's real merged config
  instead of the probe's stub: identical 16/32 split, identical messages. Runtime driving of
  `launcher.tick()`, `manage_open_positions()`, `compute_governor_state()`, `breach_flatten_check()`
  and `run_cycle()` in all 16 surviving states: none misbehaves.
* **The heartbeat rewrite (B564) is correct**, and the struck instruction was genuinely broken: the
  host's own logs contain **0 occurrences** of `PLACEMENT PAUSED`, and `run_book_fn_console.log`'s
  newest entry was **7 days old** while that book was healthy.
* **Overwriting a `.py` that a running Python has imported is safe on Windows** — CPython closes
  source handles after read and invalidates `__pycache__` on mtime+size **equality**, so a
  `Copy-Item`-preserved older mtime cannot yield stale bytecode. The entire design rests on this.

### B573 — A dangerous-direction fallback that is recorded rather than fixed [MEASURED — OPEN]

A refuter enumerated 31 values for the reset rule at a 2 h-disagreement instant. **12 of 12 valid
spellings resolve correctly** — quoted, spaced, tab/NBSP-wrapped, any case, `CET`, `CEST`, `CE(S)T`,
`europe_prague`. But **8 fall silently to the detected server offset with no log at all** (`null`,
`~`, `""`, `"   "`, `false`, `0`, `server`, `SERVER`) and **9 fall with one `LOGGER.error` and no
notification** (list, dict, `true`, `Europe/Berlin`, `EET`, `UTC`, a typo). Every one of those lands
on the **1–2 h-early behaviour B56 exists to remove**, and `broker_clock`'s own docstring calls
`UnknownBrokerClockError` "deliberately fatal" — the governor catches it, converting fail-closed into
fail-open-to-the-old-bug.

**Not fixed here, deliberately.** Surfacing it needs a change in `book_engine.py` (which coerces `""`
to `None` before the builder sees it), and registering `Europe/Berlin` would change
`broker_clock.py` — whose sha is **shared byte-for-byte with Session S's carry**, so touching it
would force S's manifest to be regenerated. The operational risk is covered at carry time:
`verify_carry.py --check behaviour` asserts the resolved window instant for both accounts on the
host, so a misconfigured profile cannot pass the gate. What is left open is a **future** profile edit,
on files that are contract-bound and therefore rarely touched.

Related and also recorded: `scripts/dual_broker_execution_follower.py:915-926` reads the same profile
key and resolves it with `ZoneInfo(tz_name)`. Under the host's condition (no `tzdata`) that raises,
is swallowed by its own `except Exception`, and falls back to `3.0` — **exactly the 2 h-early
behaviour**. So the "deliberately not zoneinfo" choice in `broker_clock` is not stylistic; a sibling
consumer on that host already fails this way. It is on the never-execute list and out of scope here.

### B574 — Two more defects, found by reading my own runbook after the refuters had finished [CORRECTION]

Both are the same shape as the ones the refuters found, which is the point: the class survives one
pass of fixing.

1. **A nested `$_` in the block I had just written to fix a different defect.**
   `@(...namespaces...) | ForEach-Object { $books | Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -like "*--namespace $_*" } }`
   — inside the inner `Where-Object`, `$_` is the **process**, not the namespace string. The filter
   interpolates an object into the pattern and matches nothing, so the block reports "no book process
   for &lt;object&gt;" on a healthy host. It is a **silent wrong answer, not an error**. Rewritten as
   `foreach ($ns in ...)` with the namespace captured explicitly. §7.3's version was already correct
   (`$ns = $_`), which is how the difference was visible at all.
2. **`"STOP: \$oldPids is empty"`** — `\` is bash escaping. PowerShell's escape character is a
   backtick, so `\$oldPids` interpolates the (empty) variable and prints `\ is empty`. In a STOP
   line. Fixed to `` `$oldPids ``.

Also closed: §0 told the operator to record the open-position count "so §8 can confirm it is
unchanged", and §8 never checked it. It does now — and says what a change means (the kill flags are
still down, so the books cannot have opened one; any change is a close, and a close in that window
was the broker's stop rather than the book's exit policy).

guarded at one call site.** `fwd_all_mean_ratio = mean_win / mean_all` is a multiple only

mean went negative the ratio went negative, the flag became structurally unreachable and

its own contamination class flagged at the haircut floor; a non-positive window reports CLEAN
*vacuously* and says so; every result carries `inflation_basis`. Five behavioural tests
including the monotonicity **property** and a regression guard on the positive-history path.

**B469 — best-of-N composition ranking buys +0.527 annualised Sharpe from noise, so every
ranking here carries an interval.** A refuter simulated 20,000 replications with all 32

compares); and a leave-one-out over four provably worthless, interchangeable sleeves **names a
scapegoat 99.2% of the time** at an average apparent damage of −0.385 annualised Sharpe. A
paired day-block bootstrap was added to both the composition ranking and the leave-one-out;
B461's two significant results survive it and nothing else does. [MEASURED — FIXED]

**B470 — what the multiplicity refuter could NOT break, measured rather than assumed.**
p=1.0 padding is monotonically stricter for BH and for Bonferroni: over 200,000 random
families a padded hypothesis was never rejected and never created a rejection, while padding
with the refused sleeves' *actual* p-values would have made BH looser in 0.14% of families.
BH is valid under this estate's real dependence — 20,000 reps at m=32 including sign-opposed
sleeves on identical symbol universes (ρ = −0.6) and a maximally adversarial two-block
structure: realised FDR 0.0594–0.0771 against a 0.0750 target, never above nominal.
Benjamini–Yekutieli is not required and would cost ~4× power (its realised FDR is 0.018).
Two real qualifications: under this dependence P(FDP > 0.5 | any rejection) is **0.107**
versus 0.003 under independence — false admissions arrive in clumps — and the family of 32
has a participation ratio of **4.56**, i.e. it is about five independent questions.
[MEASURED]

**B471 — DSR gates nothing, and its published sweep varies the insensitive axis.**
`gate.py:771` sets `core = ("expectancy", "lifetime", "stability", "robustness",
"significance")`; DSR and PBO are telemetry. So "at what `n_trials` does an admitted sleeve
flip?" has the answer **none, at any `n_trials`, ever** — and the size of the search is
charged nowhere in the pipeline. Worse, the sweep moves the wrong knob: at W's own
`sr_variance`, a 16× increase in `n_trials` (128 → 2048) raises the required daily Sharpe
21.8%, while a 2× error in `sr_variance` raises it **28.8%** — and `sr_variance` is estimated
from the nine *survivors* of the selection, which truncates the dispersion downward and
shrinks the deflation. [MEASURED]

certification among 28) 0.3375 before this session's guards; **P(wave 5 reports ≥1 positive

under one option, BH controls the FDR of the significance rejections at α across a family of

or the ≥74 authored sleeve designs behind the 32. **The zero-admission result is the one kind

**How it surfaced:** the second full-suite A/B reported
`tests/research_infra/test_walkforward_gate.py::test_unpriceable_symbol_is_recorded_not_assumed_zero`
as regressed. Re-run in isolation it **failed at HEAD and passed at base** — a real

earlier — so every cost-bearing number in B650–B672 was computed against the base
broker-truth layer, which is what the branch now carries.

**The generalisable lesson, and it cost two capture cycles:** `git add -A` in a worktree that
concurrent work can write to will commit that work. AB's own first commit was clean; the
sweep happened in the follow-up commit. Stage by path, or diff before committing, when other
sessions are live on the machine.

**B674 — the A/B: 665 bad → 665 bad, 0 regressed, 0 fixed, +42 net new passing tests.**
[MEASURED] Full-suite failure-set comparison `7b0f4f276` → `136dcb9e8`, both trees clean,

10,925, which is **exactly** the 42 new test functions this session adds (7 state parity, 4
port parity, 7 ramp, 10 normalize, 6 trial ledger, 8 bar-provider pre-gap) — no test was
silently gained or lost elsewhere.

**Three capture cycles, and the two extra ones were worth their cost.** The first after-capture
was killed by the harness mid-run and produced nothing. The second flagged B672's citation-guard
regression, which was real and mine. The third flagged B673's broker-truth sweep, which was real
and **not** mine, and which the first two would have hidden — the second capture ran while the
artifacts were being rewritten underneath it, so its `test_high_load_integration` "fix" and its
`test_unpriceable_symbol` "regression" were both artefacts of a tree changing during the run.
Only the third capture ran on a stable tree, and it is the one the receipt embeds. The
`WAVE_6_WORKING_AGREEMENT.md` §7.3 rule — *"any claimed regression is re-run in isolation at
both HEAD and base before you believe it"* — is what separated the real difference from the
noise in both cases, and in the second case it was the rule that found the contamination.

Classified per (symbol, quarter) by `_classify_era`:
`RECORDED` (dispersed per-bar values — a real measurement), `SCHEDULE` (one constant held
across a multi-year block: EURUSD 2000–2003 is exactly 50 points at p10 **and** p99, i.e. the
broker's history-server backfill — MODELLED, not observed), `FLOORED` (a mass at 1 point
beside a plausible tail: GBPJPY 2018 p25=1, p75=18, p90=26 — 0.1 pip is not a GBPJPY spread),
`QUANTIZED` (≤3 distinct values). The model uses the column for **ratios between eras, never
levels**, so the measured 1.00×–1.73× bar-vs-tick level bias (22 symbols) divides out.

### B702 — The era instrument validated before it was trusted: H4 skill 0.334, D1 0.007 [MEASURED]

The 37-day tick window cut into weekly blocks; every ordered block pair gives a true spread
ratio (tick) and a predicted one (bars). 540 pairs, 27 symbols. **352 of the 540 do not move
at all** — quoted spread is quantised to the point, so the tick median is the same integer
week to week and both model and baseline score exactly 0; selecting on the pooled median
picks whichever variant best predicts "no change". Selection therefore runs on the **moved
subset (188 pairs)**, against a "predict no change" baseline: leading variants score **skill
0.33–0.35**. Skill rises with data per era — **0.333 at 7-day blocks, 0.370 at 14, 0.582 at
21** — the signature of estimation noise, not bias. **H4 skill 0.334 against D1's 0.007** over
the same pairs, so H4 is the era instrument and D1 only a second opinion whose disagreement
widens the band rather than voting in it.

### B703 — The out-of-sample calibration point, and what it does not prove [MEASURED]

`ULTIMATE_TICK_SPREAD_GOLD.json` measures XAUUSD over 2025-10..2026-04 at median **0.37**
price on 1,288,483 ticks; the archive window measures **0.46** on 690,463. True era ratio
**0.8043**; the bar column at H4 predicts **0.8007**, error **−0.45 %** (D1: −6.97 %).
**This is n=1 and it is no longer out-of-sample for the winning variant**, because the variant
family was written after this window was inspected. The block holdout is the selection
instrument; this is corroboration.

### B705 — Bands: every term measured, and a floor that exists because of a real failure [MEASURED]

Per-era half-width in log space = sqrt(cross-instrument dispersion² + split-half sampling
noise² + D1-vs-H4 disagreement²), floored per era class at the **measured** median
quarter-to-quarter move of `RECORDED` eras (0.09114 log, n=959), doubled for
`SCHEDULE`/`FLOORED`. The floor exists because a backfilled constant makes every estimator
agree and the split-half noise is exactly zero: **DASHUSD 2026Q1 came out of the first build
as `mid=1.000` with half-width `0.000`** — maximum confidence on the era where the data is
least trustworthy. **9.3 % of FTMO eras and 14.4 % of redacted_account's** exceed the decidability
threshold and are published as `capture_required` with a string naming what would close them,
per the prompt's rule that a band too wide to decide anything is a capture requirement.

### B708 — Entry timing: the FX family pays 13×–38× at the hour its D1 bar closes [MEASURED]

Hour-of-week on the broker wall clock, where hour 0 of a weekday **is the daily rollover and
is where a D1 bar closes**: `GBPUSD` **38×**, `EURUSD` **32×**, `USDJPY` **19.3×**, `USDCAD`
17.6×, `CHFJPY` 16.2×, `EURGBP` 14.0×, `GBPJPY` 13.7×, against each symbol's own median.
It is an **FX/JPY-family effect**: fourteen symbols — every metal, index and oil CFD — do not
quote at all at the rollover, and XAUUSD's own worst hour is 1.14×. By broker 01:00 the
multiplier is back to 1.3–2.0×. Published as a measurement; entry convention is sleeve
geometry and belongs to wave 7's cost-geometry lane. Receipt: `ENTRY_TIMING_V1.json`.

### B709 — The volatility dimension is measurably flat, and that is the finding [MEASURED]

`FOURTH_REVIEW` §4.6 asks for spread as a function of hour-of-week **× volatility state**. The
hour term is strong (B708). The volatility term, at the median, is **1.000 for every
instrument class except metals** (0.963 → 1.013 across quintiles), under *both* a
look-ahead-free trailing D1 state and a contemporaneous one — both were measured so they could
be compared. FTMO's quoted spread on these instruments is close to administered; the variation
lives in the hour and in the tail, not in the daily volatility state. The term ships and is
applied multiplicatively, but a reader should know it is doing almost nothing and why, rather
than finding a 1.000 later and wondering whether it was wired up.

### B710 — Price-proportional scaling: what is refuted is the model, not the slope [CORRECTION]

Regressing log(spread ratio) on log(price ratio) over 1,076 consecutive `RECORDED` quarter
pairs on 43 symbols: **β = 0.823 ± 0.144, R² = 0.0295.** An earlier draft of this session's
own verdict string read *"price-proportional scaling REFUTED: β is 1.2 standard errors from
1.0"*. **Withdrawn — 1.2 SE is not a rejection of the slope.** What is rejected is price as a
*model*: it explains **2.9 %** of the variance in era spread changes. N §8.5's counterexample
(XAUUSD +24 % spread on a −10 % price) is not an exception, it is typical.

### B711 — Four defects in this session's own model, each of which shipped a plausible wrong number first [CORRECTION]

1. **EURUSD silently absent from build 1** — the most-traded symbol in the archive. 100 % of
   its H4 bars inside the reference window record spread `0`, which means "not stored", not
   "no spread"; empty reference → no ratios → dropped without a message. Fixed: the reference
   window widens backwards until it has something to measure, and records by how much.
2. **USDJPY 2021 published as `mid=20.25`, band [0.47, 867]** — the floor filter discarded the
   64 bars reading 1 point and kept the rare legacy 50s. Fixed: floor filtering disabled where
   >50 % of the data sits at the floor.
3. **All 27 EURUSD eras undecidable, half-width ln(2)** — the guard for (2) keyed on the
   variant *name*, but every `trimmed_mean_*` also drops the floor
   (`_trimmed_mean(drop_floor=True)`), so they stayed in and returned the rare 2s against the
   mean's 1.05. Fixed: the guard keys on a behaviour set, `FLOOR_DROPPING`.
4. **A manufactured ln(2) timeframe disagreement** on EURUSD — H4's reference widened 90 days
   and D1's 730, so the two ratios answered different questions. Fixed: the disagreement term
   applies only when both references are comparable.

A fifth, in the validation rather than the model: `refute_price_proportional` collected **zero
pairs** because it read an estimator key `scan-bars` never writes. It crashed on the division
rather than publishing a fabricated β, but a statistic assembled from an empty set is exactly
the failure mode this review exists about; it now recomputes from the bars.

### B715 — The broker-truth artifact was regenerated mid-session, and it exposed a real defect [MEASURED — FIXED]

`BROKER_TRUE_COSTS_V1.json` was rebuilt at **2026-07-29T17:03:02Z**, while this session was

named `CADJPY` and `EU50.cash` because those were unpriced when they were written. The

demonstrably changes under a running session; they now derive their fixtures from the

### B718 — Two defects in this session's own production module, found by re-reading it [CORRECTION]

1. **The coverage merge returned the STRONGEST class, not the weakest.**
   `Coverage.strength` is 0 for MEASURED and 2 for MODELLED (`coverage.py:66`), so
   `min((cov, TRANSFERRED), key=lambda c: c.strength)` returns MEASURED — a `QUANTIZED` era
   on a tick-anchored symbol was reported as a **measured** spread, which is the exact class
   of error `src/costs` exists to prevent. Now uses `coverage.weakest`, which exists for
   this. No test caught it because the tests covered only `RECORDED` and `SCHEDULE` eras;
   `test_quantized_era_is_not_reported_as_measured` closes the gap.
2. **The nearest-era fallback returned a boolean.** `NATGAS_cash` has bars from 2024Q4;
   asked for 2010 it answered with 2024Q4, and a **57-quarter** extrapolation was
   indistinguishable from a one-quarter gap and inherited that era's `decidable: True`. Now
   returns the gap in quarters and refuses beyond eight.

## B600–B649 — Session AA: the fixing machine, and the estate walked with it (wave 6)

Branch `phase6/estate-walk`, cut from `main` at `7b0f4f276`. Prompt
`phase6/SESSION_AA_ESTATE_WALK.md`; working agreement `WAVE_6_WORKING_AGREEMENT.md` §0 —
**the burden of proof is inverted: a sleeve may only be set aside after its repair paths are
enumerated and shown to fail, and "set aside" means parked with its repair list.**

**B600 — the trial-budget ledger now has a prospective half, and it is running.**
`validation_integrity/trial_budget_ledger.py` was built, tested and never run, and what it
built was a RETROSPECTIVE scanner: it reconstructs a lower bound on trials already spent by
scanning `*RESULT*.json` files that survived. In a repair campaign most variants never become
a RESULT file — a sweep cell, a re-walk, a parameter neighbourhood — so that lower bound is
structurally blind to the population it most needs to count. Added `TrialLedger`: append-only
JSONL, `O_APPEND` one line at a time so concurrent sessions can share a file, and it **cannot
raise into a caller's measurement** (a ledger that fails a run would be the brake §3 forbids;
write errors are counted and surfaced in the summary instead). `measured_n_trials()` returns
`max(prospective look events, retrospective lower bound, floor)` with the basis named. The
floor survives because a ledger that started on 2026-07-29 cannot retroactively count the
estate's history. `gate.py:47-48`'s "no trial-budget ledger exists anywhere in this repo" was
true when written and is now false; amended in place. [MEASURED]

**B601 — the four cost terms are kept instead of summed away.** `PricedTrade` gained
`components` (`commission_r`, `swap_r`, `spread_r`, `slippage_r`) and `swap_nights`, read from
`cost_r`'s own detail rather than recomputed — a second implementation of the rollover count
would be a second chance to get the US-DST broker calendar wrong. This is what makes the §2.2
cost-geometry prescription actionable: the four terms have four *different* repairs
(commission scales as 1/stop → widen the stop; swap scales with nights → change the exit;
spread → entry timing and session filter; slippage → nothing here moves it) and a total tells
them apart from none of them. Session N's own correction — "the 31.6 % was mostly swap, not
commission" — is a statement nobody could have made from a total. [MEASURED]

**B602 — `walkforward/exits.py`: the path survives the labelling, and the trail works.**
`primitives.simulate_detail` returns `(R, exit_index)` and throws the excursion away, so no
artifact in this programme could answer "did the setups move and the exit miss it, or was
there nothing there" — which is exactly the query `FOURTH_REVIEW.md` §3.3 asks for and never
assigns to anyone. `replay()` returns `r_gross`, `exit_index`, `exit_reason`, `mfe_r`,
`mae_r`, `bars_to_mfe`, and supports trail arms, a time stop and a pre-rollover flat.
**Parity is fuzzed, not asserted**: 4,000 random OHLC series, both directions, with and
without targets and trails, compared with `==` on R and on the exit index — including the
pessimistic same-bar tie where the stop wins. `simulate` has supported `trail_arm`/`trail_gap`
since it was vendored (`primitives.py:35`) and **no driver ever passed them**, which is why
`asian_fade` and `metal_session_reversion` — both `policy="trailing_runner"` in the production
exit table (`execution_packets.py:57,61`) — could not be walked at all. [MEASURED]

**B603 — the `energy_agri` classifier fix is landed, and its effect on the artifact is two
records.** FTMO files its oil CFDs under `Cash II CFD\`; `build_broker_true_costs.instrument_class`
read any `Cash*` path head as `index`, so `USOIL.cash` and `UKOIL.cash` inherited the index
class's fitted **zero** commission — a false zero on a sleeve that is trading real money
today. Filed by `SESSION_N_W7_RECOST_RESULT.md` §7 and carried as a sensitivity ever since.
Fixed with the same name-based carve-out the metals already use, plus a **cross-account
transfer**: the same barrel is MEASURED at $5.00/lot on redacted_account. That transfer needed an
alias table, because the two brokers spell it differently (`USOIL.cash` vs `USOUSD`) and a
base-symbol match alone silently does not fire — which is how the false zero survived a
classifier that already had a metals carve-out. **Measured: exactly 2 of 334 instrument
records change**, both FTMO oil, `zero`/TRANSFERRED → `$5.00 per_lot`/TRANSFERRED-from-
redacted_account. Everything else is byte-identical. V1 is left intact and `BROKER_TRUE_COSTS_V1_1.json`
is written beside it, so no prior result silently moves and the two can be A/B'd. [MEASURED]

**B604 — `FOURTH_REVIEW.md` §3.1's registry-vs-generator "wiring defect" is wrong in both
halves, and the true version is bigger and more benign.** §3.1 reads `energy_agri`'s 4-symbol
registry against its 2-symbol generator as a defect where "CORN/COTTON are sized-for but can
never fire"; §3.2 reads `idxrev`'s 8-vs-5 the same way. Measured through the production
resolvers:

  * It is **four** sleeves, not two — `energy_agri` (CORN_c, COTTON_c), `idxrev` (EU50_cash,
    FRA40_cash, US2000_cash), `sub_mid_dn_revert` and `sub_xvol_pullback` (both HEATOIL_c,
    NATGAS_cash). **The last is one of the three ARMED sleeves.**
  * They are **not sized-for**. `SleeveSpec.symbols` has no consumer in any sizing or
    admission path repo-wide: it is read by `scripts/w7_live_forensics.py:127`,
    `scripts/w7_packet_forensics.py:161` and `walkforward/registry.build_symbol_allowlist`,
    and by nothing in `admit_and_size`.
  * All four have **one deliberate cause**: the registry carries the AUTHORED universe and
    the generator the TRADEABLE one after the W7 tick-truth and spread-wall exclusions
    (`sleeves/substrate.py:51` for the clean-3 pair, the sleeve docstrings for the other two).

So it is a naming collision — two universes wearing one field name — with one real
consequence: `build_symbol_allowlist` hands the gate the WIDER universe, so the gate's
symbol-consistency check is loose. Pinned with the measured reason per sleeve in
`tests/research_infra/test_wf_registry_surface_reconciliation.py`, plus a test that fails the
day `admit_and_size` starts reading a registry universe — at which point the divergence stops
being documentation drift and becomes a live sizing defect. [MEASURED — CORRECTION]

**B605 — `walkforward/diagnostics.py`: every gate failure is a prescription with evidence.**
The gate already computed every number involved and then flattened them into verdict-reason
strings (`gate.py:836-878`). Diagnostic mode stops flattening: per-gate **margin**
(observed − required, in the gate's own units), the failing folds / symbols / sessions, the
four-term cost decomposition, MFE-MAE aggregates, realised holds, and one of twelve
prescriptions. `GateResult.repair_queue()` emits `REPAIR_QUEUE_V1.json`, one row per (sleeve,
prescription, evidence). **No gate is relaxed and no threshold moved** — `GateSpec` gained no
field, so every existing spec seal is unchanged, and the load-bearing test asserts a negative:
`run_gate` with and without `diagnose=True` returns identical verdicts, gates, q-values and
reasons. Sessions buckets are put on the BROKER's wall clock when a server resolves and
stamped `utc_hour` when it does not, rather than guessing +3 h.

The part worth reading is the three-way split on a negative expectancy, which is §3.3's
unassigned query made automatic on every sleeve: gross > 0 → `COST_GEOMETRY` (naming *which*
term); gross ≤ 0 with excursion → `EXIT_REPAIR`; no excursion → `INVERSE_TEST`. Significance
failures carry a **breadth multiple** — `(z_alpha / z_observed)²`, the pooling factor the
Fundamental Law implies — so "pool the mechanism as a family" arrives with a number attached
rather than as advice. [MEASURED]

**B607 — a defect my own instrument produced, found by reading its output.** A sleeve with

a coverage prescription reading *"capture ticks for []"* — a data-capture ceremony pointed at

**B608 — the carry counterfactual: the tier is measurable, not inferrable.**
`SURVIVOR_BOOK_V1.json` tiers every sleeve UNCONDITIONAL / CARRY_CONDITIONAL by comparing a
break-even hold to an ASSUMED horizon, because no realised hold survived any cache
(`SESSION_N_W7_RECOST_RESULT.md` §8.1). The archive supplies the realised hold off the
simulated path, so the tier can be measured: the identical walk with every swap rate forced to
zero, and read which verdicts move. Labelled a COUNTERFACTUAL everywhere it appears, because
nobody trades at zero swap.

It is strictly better evidence than the "minimal carry" treatment used to date, which
**replaces every trade's holding time with a synthetic 6 hours** (`W_NEGATIVE_CONTROLS.json`
`carry_note`). That changes the EXIT, which changes R itself; zeroing the swap rate keeps
every real hold and changes only the charge. [MEASURED]

**B609 — `metals_core`'s "ADMITs at zero carry" is a different population, and the
disagreement is the selection window.** `FOURTH_REVIEW.md` §3.1 states that `metals_core`
ADMITs the walk-forward gate at zero carry (+0.635 R/day OOS, 100 % folds positive, q 0.082).
Read at source, that number is `W_NEGATIVE_CONTROLS.json` → `real_minimal_carry_restricted`,
and it is **n=131 trades over 52 OOS days on the restricted 2-symbol priced subset with every
hold overwritten to 6 hours**, against a ~12-sleeve family. On the archive regeneration —
n=385, real simulated holds, the full H4 span, family 69 — `metals_core` posts **−0.256 R/day
at measured carry and −0.112 at zero carry, with 20 % of folds positive both ways**. Carry
moves it and does not decide it.

The two populations are not in conflict; the difference is dated. Its five OOS folds run
−0.373, −0.313, −0.561, −0.361 and **+0.327** — every fold before 2022-11 negative, only the
last one positive — and the 131-trade cached stream lives inside that last fold, which is the
window that selected the sleeve (`build_survivor_book.py:60` and `KB7_growth_kelly_sizing.py:130`
share the `d.year >= 2025` predicate; Session V). This is `CLAUDE.md` §4's out-of-window
result reproduced at sleeve level by an independent instrument. **So `metals_core`'s open
question is not holding time; it is the §3.1 frequency-ramp/threshold-drift question Session AB
owns**, and the walk hands AB a fold-level series and a per-symbol split to start from
(XAGEUR +0.620 mean net R on n=44 carries the sleeve's entire positive contribution; the other
five symbols are all negative). [MEASURED — CORRECTION]

**B610 — the three quarantined candidates have complete generators and no registry entry, so

[MEASURED]

**B611 — carry is SIDE-asymmetric, so the diagnosis splits by side.** `cost_r` books
adverse swap only — *"Zero when the swap is favourable"* (`src/costs/model.py:253`), a
deliberate and conservative choice. Measured consequence on a sleeve trading real money
right now: FTMO's oil pays a swap CREDIT long and charges heavily short — **USOIL +4.06 /
−27.50 points a night, UKOIL +21.72 / −104.42** — so `energy_agri`'s entire carry cost sits
on one side of its book, and a symmetric carry repair would pay for a problem half its
trades do not have. `diagnose_sleeve` therefore emits `by_side` (n, mean gross, mean net and
mean SWAP per side) and carries it into the expectancy evidence. What that split then found
is B621, which is larger than the question it was built for.

Also verified here, because a counterfactual nobody checks is just an assertion: the
zero-carry cost basis does exactly what it claims — swap goes to **0.000000** on every
instrument and **every other cost term is bit-identical** (checked on XAUUSD, BTCUSD,
USOIL.cash). [MEASURED]

**B612 — the cost-geometry prescription carries a target, not a direction.** Three of
`cost_r`'s four terms are 1/sl and the fourth (slippage) is fixed in R, so the COST half of
a stop-width sweep is exactly computable without regenerating anything.
`AA_COST_GEOMETRY_FRONTIER_V1.json` re-prices every trade at k ∈ {1, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75, 2,
2.5, 3} and publishes the number Session AD needs: how much bigger gross-in-R must be at
that width to break even. The algebra is stated in the artifact because its headline field
is the most misreadable thing in it — `net(k) = (gross − c_var)/k − c_fixed`, so "widening
helps" is true exactly when variable cost exceeds gross, and in that case net rises toward
the ASYMPTOTE −slippage and **can never become positive** under naive rescaling. Widening
the stop rescues a sleeve only if it makes gross-in-R RISE. Measured: `metals_core` needs
**0.59×** its current gross-in-R at a 2× stop, `fx_jpy` **1.89×**, `fx_jpy_ny` 1.99×,
`liq_asia_up_low_metal` 3.66×. 147 cells, all in the ledger. [MEASURED]

**B613 — the trail repair over-claimed by 39–51 %, and the reason is in the sanctioned
labeller.** Labelling the two `trailing_runner` sleeves under their own contracts for the
first time gave +0.759 R/trade on `asian_fade` and +0.363 on `metal_session_reversion`.
Checked before reporting: **95.8 % of `asian_fade`'s trail exits land on the FIRST bar
after entry.** `primitives.simulate` sets the running extreme from bar *j*'s own high and
then checks, on that same bar, whether the low retraced `trail_gap` from it — so a trail
arms and fills inside one M15 bar at `high − gap`, assuming the high came first. No bar
archive supports that.

The fix is a **switch, not a correction to the labeller**, because parity with `simulate`
is what makes every other number in this package about the estate rather than about a
private reimplementation. `ExitPolicy(trail_lag_extremes=True)` takes the running extreme
only from strictly earlier bars **and** fills at the bar's OPEN when the market opened
through the level — without the second half the fiction just moves one bar right. Default
unchanged; the 4,000-case parity fuzz still passes.

| | plain | trail (production) | trail (honest) | intrabar share |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `asian_fade` | −0.5205 | +0.2382 | −0.0605 | 39.4 % |
| `metal_session_reversion` | −0.2524 | +0.1111 | −0.0755 | 51.3 % |

So the repair is real and large — **+0.46 and +0.18 R/trade** at the conservative bound —
and **not enough on its own to make either sleeve positive**. Both bounds published;
neither called the answer. Only tick data locates the truth between them, which is exactly
§9's forward capture. [MEASURED]
