### B750 — `time_stop_bars` is M15 PRINTED bars for every sleeve, and the `mx_*` family's live exit is 3× tighter than the table [MEASURED]

AA left this to "Nobody, yet" (`phase6/SESSION_AA_ESTATE_WALK_RESULT.md` §4): the column is
recorded per sleeve and deliberately not applied, because the table is ambiguous — `crypto`'s
1280 reads as M15 units against a 320 h H4 horizon, the fourteen `mx_*` sleeves' 96 reads as
D1 bars against a ~3-bar median hold, and `book_owner.py:4139` never resolves it. Resolved
here from the code path that closes live positions, not from the table.

**The unit is M15 bars, counted as bars that actually PRINTED (trading bars), for every
sleeve.** `execution.py:8953-8958`, verbatim: *"Count actual CLOSED M15 bars that PRINTED
since entry_dt -- TRADING bars (they exist only while the market is open), so this skips
nights/weekends/holidays, matching the validated route's bar count instead of wall-clock.
**time_stop_bars is in M15 units for EVERY sleeve** (the H4 sleeves' route maxbars 60/80 were
pre-scaled x16 -> 960/1280 M15)."* `check_time_stop_and_close` calls that counter
(`:9010-9014`) and falls back to wall clock only when the feed cannot be read
(`j46_j49_policy.py:50-64`, *"M15 bars elapsed since fill"*, `// (15 * 60)`), and
`execution.py:6938-6942` names `check_time_stop_and_close` as the W7 book's exit owner —
`exit_policy_v4`'s own wall-clock time stop (`:585` with `execution.py:7248`) is gated off for
book-native trades at `execution.py:6945` and is **not** the W7 rule.

So both of AA's readings are M15 units, and `FOURTH_REVIEW.md` §3.3's reading of the `mx_*`
96 as 96 D1 bars is wrong **in the direction that matters: the live stop is TIGHTER than the
table suggests, not looser.** AA was right that `book_owner.py:4139` resolves nothing — it is
a Telegram card, `f"time stop {time_stop:g} bars"` — it is just not the deciding line.

**Second finding, and it is why this was measured rather than divided.** Printed bars are not
wall clock, so 96 M15 bars is a different number of D1 bars on every symbol.
`execution.py:9008` already knew ("wall-clock over-counts -- index CFDs ~3x") without writing
the ratio down. Measured per symbol from `vps-bars-20260727` (median [p10-p90] M15 bars per
coarse bar): 24/7 FX and crypto **96 [96-96]**, index CFDs and metals **92 [92-92]**, UKOIL
**84**, XCUUSD **88**; H4 is **16 [12-16]** everywhere. Receipt
`phase7/receipts/AD_TIMESTOP_UNITS_V1.json`.

**What binds, against AA's realised holds** — the whole point, because a time stop that never
fires is not a contract:

| sleeve group | live `time_stop_bars` | = own bars | = trading hours | median hold | trades truncated |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| the 12 generating `mx_*` D1 sleeves | 96 | 1.00–1.04 | 24–25 h | 72–96 h | **72.3 %–90.1 %** |
| `ny_crypto_momentum` | 20 | 20 | 5 h | 2.0 h | 37.0 % |
| `kz_london_crypto_low` | 32 | 32 | 8 h | 2.5 h | 23.4 % |
| `asia_pdl_fade` | 32 | 32 | 8 h | 1.0 h | 12.2 % |
| `liq_asia_up_low_metal` | 16 | 16 | 4 h | 0.75 h | 11.5 % |
| every H4 sleeve | 1280 / 960 | 80 / 60 | 320 / 240 h | 16–64 h | **0.0 %** |
| `vol_compression` (D1) | 7680 | 80 | 1920 h | 216 h | **0.0 %** |

The H4 and `vol_compression` rows are exactly the pre-scaling the docstring describes —
1280 M15 = 80 H4 bars = MAXBARS — so **AA's MAXBARS=80 walk already IS their time-stop
contract** and nothing about those sleeves' economics changes. The divergence is the D1 `mx_*`
family and four M15 sleeves, and every published economic number for those describes a
contract the live book does not run.

### B751 — the pre-rollover flat landed one bar late, and one bar is a whole swap night [MEASURED — FIXED]

`fx_jpy_ny`'s §3.2 repair is stated as *"exit 23:45 broker time: caps swap at structurally
zero"*. It did not. `walkforward/exits._rollover_cutoff_index` compared the cutoff against
each bar's **OPEN**, so on an M15 grid `hour=0` selected the bar opening at 23:45 — whose
**close is exactly the broker midnight**. `costs.model.rollover_nights` charges a night at
every broker midnight with `day <= end` (`model.py:236-248`), so that exit is charged one.
Measured on FTMO-Server3, entry 16:00 broker:

| exit | hold | nights | crossings |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| exactly 00:00 | 8.00 h | **1.0** | `['2026-07-07x1']` |
| 23:45 | 7.75 h | **0.0** | `[]` |

The rule whose stated purpose is a structural zero capped it at one. Corrected: the comparison
is now against each bar's CLOSE, which needs the bar interval, so `bar_minutes` is a new
argument and **the rule fails closed without it** — the same doctrine the module already
applies to the server. Added `flat_before_utc` as the general form (be flat before an instant
the CALLER priced), because §5.3's swap-aware exit and the pre-weekend flat both need *some*
rollovers avoided and not others — a triple-swap weekday is worth three nights and a Tuesday
one — and that decision needs the cost model, which this module must not import if the
`simulate` parity claim is to mean anything. Five new tests; two of them assert the
*arithmetic* (`rollover_nights` = 1.0 on the old bar, 0.0 on the new one) so the
"structurally carry-free" claim cannot quietly stop being true. All 8 fuzz blocks of the
`simulate_detail` parity claim still pass. H1: `walkforward/exits.py` is unbound by R2.

### B753 — the carry tiers restated against measured holds: four move, all upward, and the blocker is the tail [MEASURED]

`CLAUDE.md` §4 says *"What now decides OD-3 is holding time."* The survivor book's tiers are
computed at a **modelled** hold: `_NIGHTS = {sleeve: _measured_nights(horizon_h)}`
(`recost_w7_validation.py:238`) is the charged-night count for **every trade held to its full
horizon**, and the artifact says so — `carry_basis: MODELLED_HELD_TO_HORIZON`. Session N §8.1
explains why: no realised hold survived any cache. AA's walk has the realised hold.

This changes that one input. `gross_r`, `true_cost_ex_swap_r`, `swap_r_per_night` and the tier
rule are held at the survivor book's own values, and the rule is replicated from
`recost_w7_validation.py:1062-1073` with a control: **22/22 published tiers reproduce from the
artifact's own inputs**, so any tier that moves moved because of holding time and nothing else.

Measured nights are **0.3 %–37 % of modelled** on every sleeve and both accounts; the H4
book's 13.369 becomes 1.18–5.0. Four tiers move, all upward:

| account | sleeve | published | restated | measured nights | break-even nights |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| FTMO | `fx_jpy` | MEASURED_LIVE_CARRY | **UNCONDITIONAL** | 0.002 | 0.317 |
| redacted_account | `fx_jpy` | MEASURED_LIVE_CARRY | **UNCONDITIONAL** | 0.002 | 0.051 |
| FTMO | `sub_mid_dn_revert` | CARRY_CONDITIONAL | **UNCONDITIONAL** | 1.308 | 11.221 |
| redacted_account | `sub_mid_dn_revert` | CARRY_CONDITIONAL | **UNCONDITIONAL** | 1.177 | 8.371 |

`sub_mid_dn_revert` is the sleeve this lane's prompt calls *"the nearest miss in the core
book"* and asks whether measured holds already sit under its 269 h break-even. They do, by
**8.6× on nights**, on both accounts.

**The one that did NOT move is the interesting one.** `metals_core` on redacted_account stays
CARRY_CONDITIONAL at a measured **mean** of 2.961 nights against a 13.71 break-even — headroom
4.63× — because the rule's UNCONDITIONAL test is the **p99**, not the mean, and on an H4 grid
the top 1 % of holds still reach the 80-bar / 320 h ceiling. **The blocker is the tail, which
is exactly what a time stop controls and what a mean hides.**

So the flip threshold is computable, and it is far cheaper than the brief assumed. The prompt
hypothesises *"a −10 % time-stop tightening flips its redacted_account tier"*. Measured, the
**loosest** time stop that reaches UNCONDITIONAL:

| account::sleeve | own bars | hours | % of horizon | trades truncated | p99 nights after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| redacted_account::`metals_core` | 78 H4 | 312 h | **97.5 %** | 9.6 % | 13.00 |
| FTMO::`fx_jpy_ny` | 29 M15 | 7.2 h | 60.4 % | 3.5 % | **0.00** |
| redacted_account::`fx_jpy_ny` | 29 M15 | 7.2 h | 60.4 % | 3.5 % | **0.00** |
| FTMO::`metals_softband` | 42 H4 | 168 h | 52.5 % | 23.2 % | 7.00 |
| redacted_account::`metals_softband` | 18 H4 | 72 h | 22.5 % | 38.0 % | 5.00 |
| either::`idxrev`, `metals_ob_micro` | — | — | — | — | not flippable: gross is negative before any swap, so carry is not their problem |

`metals_core`-on-redacted_account needs a **2.5 %** tightening, not 10 %. This half prices only the
carry — capping a hold also changes gross, which B756+ measures at the same cells, and the two
halves are read together in the result doc.

**Population caveat, stated in the artifact rather than buried:** the edge terms are from the
W7 validation CACHES and the holds from the FULL ARCHIVE. No population carries both — that is
the gap Session N §8.1 recorded. Strictly better evidence than a horizon assumption; not the
same thing as a single-population measurement.

### B754 — B613's rule stands, its reading does not: the intrabar bias has no fixed sign [CORRECTION]

Every trail cell in this lane runs at both bounds and both are published — 152 cells with both
bounds, no cell reported at the production bound alone. What the measurement refutes is the
reading attached to the rule, that production is the *optimistic* one:

| | n | mean (honest − production) | frac honest better |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| all cells | 152 | — | **42 % better, 41 % worse** |
| trail arm 0.5 R | 50 | **+0.0596** | **0.60** |
| trail arm 1.0 R | 50 | +0.0186 | 0.48 |
| trail arm 2.0 R | 50 | **−0.0240** | **0.18** |
| reversion sleeves | 68 | −0.0074 | 0.35 |
| breakout / continuation | 42 | +0.0535 | 0.48 |

`simulate`'s same-bar arm-and-fill makes the trail exit **earlier**, at a price the bar may
never have offered in that sequence. That does two opposite things — books a better fill
(optimistic) and ends the trade sooner (pessimistic on a runner) — and which dominates is a
property of the sleeve and, more strongly, of the arm. At a tight arm the production trail
fires on noise and cuts winners, so removing it helps; at a wide arm it captures a spike the
honest variant misses. **"Production is the upper bound" is a property of `asian_fade`, a
fade, not of the switch.** B613 measured it correctly on the sleeve it had.

Independent reproduction of B613 itself, which is why the harness is trusted here: labelling
the two `trailing_runner` sleeves under their own live arm/gap recovers AA's figures almost
exactly — `metal_session_reversion` trail gross **+0.1059 prod / −0.0785 honest** against AA's
+0.111 / −0.075, `asian_fade` **+0.2476 / −0.0640** against AA's +0.238 / −0.061.

### B756 — the exit frontier: 1,631 cells, all 25 sleeves improve, none admits, and 23 of 25 beat the zero-carry ceiling [MEASURED]

Five swept surfaces per sleeve (time stop on its own grid, scheduled flats, stop width under
both target conventions, trail at both intrabar bounds, target 1R–8R, and the
`partial_be_runner` surface), each cell re-simulated from AA's stored intents and re-gated with
the **full 32-sleeve family**, the target sleeve's records swapped and every other sleeve left
at its as-walked labelling, `declared_family_size=69` exactly as AA set it — so each row is a
clean A/B and the BH rank stays comparable.

| | |
|---|---|
| sleeves improved | **25 / 25**, dR/day +0.0147 … +0.7711, median **+0.2492** |
| reaching ADMIT | **0 / 25** |
| failing gate at the best cell | `significance` **25**, robustness 13, lifetime 8, expectancy 7, stability 7 |
| best cell beats the ZERO-CARRY ceiling | **23 / 25** |
| composite worse than the best single cell | **17 / 25** |

**The third row is the strategic result and it points the opposite way to the brief.** Every
cell was measured against a zero-carry ceiling — the identical walk with every swap rate forced
to zero, which bounds what any carry repair could possibly be worth. On 23 of 25 sleeves the
best exit geometry beats it. `CLAUDE.md` §4's *"What now decides OD-3 is holding time"* does
not survive contact with the estate's own exit surface: **the levers are geometry and the
multiplicity bill, and neither is carry.**

**The fifth row is the session's best evidence against naive composition.** One post-hoc
composite per sleeve — the argmax of each family stacked — was included to be explicit about
post-hoc selection, and it underperforms the best single cell on 17 of 25, sometimes badly
(`mx_jp225` +0.257 against +0.616). The surfaces interact; "best of each" is not a repair.

Three per-sleeve results worth naming:

- **`mx_btcusd`'s repair is not a carry repair.** Its whole cost is 9.3 % of |gross|, so AA's
  "swap is 77 % of its total cost" is 77 % of a small number and the carry counterfactual moved
  the verdict only because q sat on the BH threshold. Its live 1-D1-bar time stop costs
  **−0.141 R/day**; tightening to 1 bar saves 1.3 points of cost percentage and destroys 61 %
  of the gross. What it wants is a **wider target**: `target_5R` is **+0.309 R/day** on a
  monotone 1R→5R ridge. `significance` is its only failing gate at every cell, exactly as AA's
  §4 routed it — an exit sweep cannot pay a multiplicity bill.
- **`mx_us100` and `mx_us500` ATR-MR are the clearest EXIT_REPAIR confirmations in the estate.**
  Their live 1-bar time stop alone takes capture from −0.181 → +0.271 and −0.102 → +0.295, and
  both go negative → positive on pooled OOS (+0.449, +0.410). They do not need an inverse test.
  `idxrev` is the counter-case and AA had it right: MFE 0.75, best cell +0.0004 R/day, capture
  still 0.010 — `INVERSE_TEST` stands.
- **The `mx_*` D1 family wants a 4–5R target, not the 2R its live contract sets.**
  `target_5R` is the best cell on `mx_btcusd`, `mx_ethusd`, `mx_jp225` and `mx_us30`;
  `target_4R` on `mx_cadjpy`.

Baseline parity: **26 of AA's 32 `B_balanced|v1_1` verdicts reproduce bit-identically.** The
six that moved are the first-of-day set, and they moved because Session Y's fidelity merge
(`90224cfe6`) raised their `live_recall` to 1.0 — they clear the 0.50 floor now and reach a
verdict. AA §2.3's *"their verdict is still NOT_EVALUABLE"* is **stale at wave 7's merge-base**,
not wrong when written.

Also corrected, and filed as a repair row rather than edited into AA's artifact: **AA's frontier
algebra `net(k) = (gross − c_var)/k − c_fixed` assumes the hold is constant in k, and it is
not.** AA re-prices `cost_r` at `sl' = k·sl` holding holding-hours fixed, so its swap term
halves at 2×. Measured by re-simulation the charged nights *rise* — `mx_btcusd` 5.36 → **19.42**,
`metals_softband` 5.93 → 11.33, `metals_core` 4.79 → 10.25, `sub_mid_dn_revert` 1.76 → 6.84 —
so the published required-gross-multiple targets are optimistic for every carry-bearing sleeve
and the error grows with its nights. Even so, **12 of 18 sleeves with a target clear their 2×
requirement**, `metals_core` at 1.085× against a 0.59× brief — and it still REJECTs, which is
the finding: the frontier answers a per-trade cost-geometry question and the gate answers a
per-day stability-and-significance one. `fx_jpy` needs 1.89× and delivers **0.175×**; that is
the honest answer its brief asked for, and its next prescription is the §4.8 meta-label entry
filter.

Receipts `phase7/receipts/EXIT_FRONTIER_V1.json`, `EXIT_FRONTIER_V1_TRAIL.json`,
`AD_FRONTIER_ANALYSIS_V1.json`. 2,036 look events added to the shared trial ledger (total
3,679); those feed `measured_n_trials` → the DSR deflation, which is telemetry, while the BH
family size stays at AA's 69, so the sweep's own size moves no verdict reported here.

**Every added symbol costs it.** The Fundamental Law's √k assumes members of equal

### B809 — a TWO-PART test predicts which families pooling helps, and two of thirty pass it [MEASURED 2026-07-30]

| family | k | IC dispersion ratio | members positive | pooled raw p |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `volume_surge_reversal` × index × D1 | 6 | **0.736** | **6/6** | **0.1204** |
| `energy_fvg_retest` × energy × H4 | 3 | **0.117** | **3/3** | **0.1740** |
| `atr_mean_reversion` × metal × D1 | 9 | 0.610 | 0/9 | 1.0000 |
| `atr_mean_reversion` × energy × D1 | 3 | 0.682 | 0/3 | 0.6621 |
| `donchian_20_breakout` × crypto × D1 | 9 | 3.119 | 5/9 | 0.4442 |
| `crypto_h4_donchian_ac60` × crypto × H4 | 9 | 4.735 | 5/9 | 0.9413 |
| `donchian_20_breakout` × fx × D1 | 14 | 80.132 | 5/14 | 1.0000 |

**Corrected against this block's own first draft, by an adversarial pass after the first
commit.** It said "the two families below a ratio of 1 are exactly the two with the best
p-values." **Seven** of the thirty are below 1. `ic_dispersion_ratio` is `sd/|mean|` and is
therefore **sign-blind**: a family whose members agree on being uniformly bad is as tight as
one whose members agree on being good — `atr_mean_reversion` × metal scores 0.610 with 0 of
9 members positive.

The test that separates them has two clauses: **dispersion ratio < 1 AND every member
positive.** Exactly two of thirty pass, and they hold the two best p-values in the grid.
That is the operational form of the equal-IC assumption — **before spending a session on
breadth, check that the members agree and that what they agree on is positive** — and it is
one query on trades that already exist.

The repair-queue routing was never affected: it already branched on the pooled mean's sign
as well as the ratio, so the five low-ratio all-negative families were already
`PARK_WITH_LIST` and only the two are `SAMPLE_OR_STABILITY`. What was wrong was the sentence,
which is the part a reader carries away. [MEASURED]

### B813 — the era term and the hour term compound, and their product was never validated [MEASURED 2026-07-30]

The probe that found it: R4 came back with the FX D1 families paying **0.46–0.50 R of total
cost per trade**, 80 % of it spread, and a **+0.40 R** saving from a two-hour entry shift. A
spread charge of half the risk unit is not a market, so the probe was suspected before it
was believed.

`spread_model_v1` composes `anchor × era_ratio × hour_of_week` multiplicatively. Measured on
NZDUSD in the 2000s: **era_ratio 13.7 × hour_mult 14.4 = 198× the modern base**, charging
`spread_r` **1.78** — 178 % of the stop. EURUSD's 2000s: 32.6 × 14.7 = 479×, spread_r 0.46.
Across the FX D1 families the mean multiple is **71–79×** and the maximum **880×**, with
only **44 %** of their trades in `RECORDED` eras.

Each factor was validated alone — AG on H4 block pairs (all-hours medians, skill 0.33–0.58)
and on the 37-day tick window (where `era_ratio` is 1 by construction). AG's §10 item 1
already says the pre-2010 FX eras are `SCHEDULE`-class and unvalidatable. What is new is
that nobody had named the **product of two unvalidated multipliers** as its own risk.

Non-FX classes are unaffected: mean multiple 0.44–0.75, and fourteen instruments do not
quote at the rollover at all (AG §5) — which R4 reproduces independently as a ~0.000 R hour
saving on metals, indices, energy and crypto.

Interim treatment, used here and available to everyone: restrict to `era_class ==
RECORDED`. That is outcome-independent for exactly the reason
`GateSpec.coverage_policy="restrict_to_priced"` is — it is a property of the broker's bar
data, not of returns. Under it the FX families stay deeply negative (−0.28 to −0.36), so the
defect inflated the magnitude and did **not** create the sign; the crypto donchian family
improves from p 0.444 to p 0.083. Routed to AG's lane; not repaired here. [MEASURED]

### B814 — the entry-hour repair is real, and its size is not yet known [MEASURED 2026-07-30]

AG measured the FX family paying 13×–38× at broker hour 00. A D1 bar closes at broker 00:00
and this whole family enters at that close, so every fill lands on the worst hour of the
week by construction. Re-pricing the same trades two hours later removes 80–81 % of modelled
cost on the three FX D1 families and ~0.000 R on every other class — the exact signature AG
predicted.

But B813 means most of that charge is an unvalidated extrapolation, so **the ceiling is not
the gain** and this row carries no repair claim. The honest next step is measurable with
data already on this machine: the archive holds H4 bars for every FX symbol, so entering at
the first H4 close after the D1 decision (broker 04:00) can be simulated end to end —
changing the entry price and therefore R, not only the spread charge. One session's work,
and it is the largest single unpriced lever this sweep found. [MEASURED]

### B815 — `mx_nzdjpy`: the break is dated 2025 and it beats its own null [MEASURED 2026-07-30]

Splitting the trade series on the year axis, **2025** maximises |mean before − mean after|
at **0.785 R**: +0.1137 R/trade gross on n=466 before, **−0.6713** on n=37 after.
Permutation null over 2,000 shuffles of the same returns against the same year labels:

A defect in this session's own selection rule, recorded: the first revision picked the
post-hoc bucket under an `n >= 100` floor, which excluded `PERSISTENCE == trend` at n=94 —
the mechanistically right bucket, missed by six trades, in favour of one six trades larger
and 0.08 R worse. The floor is gone and both gates are now published side by side with

# Wave 8 — Session AH (conditioning + entry economics), blocks B1000–B1049

Branch `phase8/conditioning-entry`. Not merged. Receipts under `phase8/receipts/`.

### B1000 — the MT5 bar `spread` column is the MINIMUM spread within the bar [MEASURED 2026-07-30]

`spread_model_v1` reads that column as a level whose ratios track the era. Nothing had asked
which instant of a bar it describes. Answered by exact integer match against tick truth at
M15 inside the reference window, over five candidate statistics and **30 symbols**
(`ah_spread_scan.py bar-semantics` → `AH_BAR_SPREAD_SEMANTICS.json`):

| candidate | median exact-match rate |
|---|---:|
| **min** | **0.9992** |
| open | 0.2390 |
| close | 0.2195 |
| median | 0.0562 |
| max | 0.0077 |

Worst symbol on `min` is EURUSD at 0.9844; best are 1.000. M15 is used because 900 s is short
enough that the five candidates separate — at H4 they do not.

**Why it matters more than a footnote: a four-hour minimum cannot see a one-hour rollover
spike.** So the bar column is structurally incapable of validating the hour term at H4, which
is why the era × hour product went unchecked for a whole wave. At M15 it *can*, and that is
what makes B1002's era-axis test possible at all. [MEASURED]

### B1001 — my own first regressions said "v1 is fine", and they were contaminated [MEASURED 2026-07-30]

The first run of the cross-broker and era-axis fits returned **b = +1.125 ± 0.407** and
**b = +0.930 ± 0.051** — i.e. the multiplicative composition AF filed as a defect is correct.
Both were wrong for the same reason: fourteen archive instruments do not quote at the broker
rollover at all (AG §5) and crypto quotes 24/7 with no widening, so their hour-00 multiplier is
exactly 1.00 and `h_level == base` **by construction**. Such a cell fits the log-log slope at
1.0 no matter which composition is true — and BTCUSD carries a 22.4× level difference between
the two accounts, so it set the cross-broker slope by leverage alone.

This is AG's block-pair failure (352 of 540 pairs did not move, so selecting on the pooled
median picked the variant best at predicting "no change") in a new place, and it takes the same
fix: `MIN_EFFECT_MULT = 1.5`, fit only where the premium exists. Recorded because it was one
commit away from shipping "no repair needed" on a defect that is real. [MEASURED]

### B1002 — the composition is damped: b = 0.4947 ± 0.1003, and b = 1 is rejected on ONE axis, not on the era axis [MEASURED 2026-07-30]

`log(hour-h level) = a + b·log(calm-hours level)`, on the three axes that carry
level-versus-hour variation, restricted to the cells where a rollover premium exists:

| axis | what varies | b | SE | σ from 1 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **B cross-section, `fx`** | **14 cells = 7 instruments × 2 accounts**, leave-one-out | **0.310** | 0.139 | **5.0** |
| B cross-section, `jpy_fx` | same | 0.721 | 0.194 | 1.4 |
| C era axis, M15 bar minima 2024Q1–2026Q3 | 152 within-symbol demeaned points, 14 symbols | 0.669 | **0.219** (symbol-clustered) | **1.5** |
| A cross-broker | same instrument, same instant, two administered levels | 0.825 | 0.935 | 0.2 |

Inverse-variance weighted over the identifying axes: **b = 0.4947 ± 0.1003, envelope
[0.310, 0.721]**. The selection protocol is declared in `ah_spread_compose.py` source *before*
any verdict was computed with it.

**Two corrections in this block that an adversarial pass supplied, and the second is the
strongest thing against this session's own repair.**

**(a) The era-axis SE was an i.i.d. SE on doubly-clustered data, and it read 2.6 σ.** 152
quarterly points come from 14 symbols over 11 shared quarters; a symbol's quarters move together
and a quarter's symbols move together. Symbol-clustered the SE is 0.219 and σ-from-1 falls to
**1.5**, below this fit's own declared `REJECT_SIGMA = 2.0`. A 4,000-draw symbol block bootstrap
gives a 95 % CI of **[0.439, 1.251]**, which **contains 1** (P(b ≥ 1) = 0.237), and **6 of the 14
per-symbol era slopes are themselves ≥ 1**.

**(b) The era axis decomposes into two components that disagree, and the broker-wide one points
ABOVE 1.** A historical 20×–50× era ratio is a *broker-wide* move, so the axis was split:

| component | what it isolates | b | SE | n |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| quarter-collapsed | the cross-symbol mean per quarter — the **broker-wide** era response | **1.463** | 0.684 | 11 |
| within-quarter | one instrument moving alone | **0.879** | 0.044 | 152 |

**So the era axis does not support the damping, and its broker-wide component points the other
way.** The axis that does support it is the affected class's cross-section (5.0 σ i.i.d., 5.79
clustered by instrument, 3.8–5.6 leave-one-out — and 3.2 σ collapsed to 7 instruments), where
v1's leave-one-out prediction error is also **2.2× the damped form's** (0.608 against 0.288).

**What the repair therefore rests on, stated narrowly:** the affected class's cross-section, plus
the a-priori ground AF filed the defect on — v1 charges **178 % of the risk unit as spread** on
NZDUSD in the 2000s, which is not a market, and that argument needs no regression. The era axis
neither confirms nor refutes it. **And the functional form is not uniquely selected:** on the fx
class MAX_PEAK (0.263) and ADD_PRICE (0.278) score within 0.02 of DAMPED_B (0.280) on
leave-one-out, all three far ahead of MULT_V1's 0.608. What the evidence supports is "damped, by
roughly half an exponent"; it does not single out this algebra.

**Which is why every conclusion in this session is published at BOTH `b = 0.4947` and `b = 1`
(v1).** B1008's entry-shift result is *larger* under v1, so the session's headline does not depend
on the exponent at all; B1005's is the one that scales with it, monotonically to zero at b = 1.
[MEASURED]

### B1003 — the repaired composition, and what it does to AF's 198× case [MEASURED 2026-07-30]

`spread(sym, era, h) = anchor × era_ratio ** b × hour_mult(h)`, which is v1 exactly at
`b = 1` and reproduces the reference window exactly at any `b` (`era_ratio = 1` there, which is
where the hour term was measured and is therefore right). Measured at broker hour 00:

| cell | era class | era ratio | v1 product | **v2 product** |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| EURUSD 2002Q2 | SCHEDULE | 50.00 | 650× | **93.4×** |
| NZDUSD 2005Q2 | SCHEDULE | 13.01 | 143× | **40.1×** |
| USDJPY 2007Q2 | SCHEDULE | 12.15 | 117× | **33.9×** |
| EURUSD 2013Q2 | FLOORED | 1.79 | 23.3× | 17.4× |
| XAUUSD 2022Q2 | QUANTIZED | 0.178 | 0.18× | **0.18× (unchanged)** |

Two guards, both load-bearing. The multiplier is clamped at ≥ 1.0 — a wide enough era would
otherwise be charged a rollover *tighter* than its own calm level, which no book quoted. And

published before today reproduces exactly, and `GateSpec.spread_composition` /
`spread_era_exponent` carry it into any gate run — the composition changes the spec seal, which
a test asserts. [MEASURED]

### B1006 — a bias this session sized and did NOT repair, and it runs the same way [MEASURED 2026-07-30]

`era_ratio` is a ratio of bar MINIMA (B1000) while the anchor is a tick p50. Writing an era's
min-to-median factor as `k`, `era_ratio_v1 = (P_era/P_ref) × (k_era/k_ref)`, so the quantity
the model wants is `era_ratio_v1 × (k_ref/k_era)`. For a SCHEDULE-class era the recorded series
is a **constant**, so its min IS its median and `k_era = 1` exactly. Measured `1/k_ref` from
the reference window: **fx 1.500×, jpy_fx 1.333×, metals 1.272×, index 1.103×, energy 1.018×,
crypto 1.000×.**

So on constant-spread FX eras the era ratio is inflated by ~1.5× on top of everything else.
AG measured the same quantity from the other direction (`tick_over_bar_factor`, 1.00×–1.73×)
and applies it **only** to modelled anchors, never to the era ratio. Not repaired here because
it is a defect in the era TERM — closing it means re-deriving `SPREAD_MODEL_V1.json`'s era
table on a min-consistent anchor. It runs the same direction as B1002's repair, so every number
this session publishes is conservative with respect to it. [MEASURED]

AF said the FX D1 cohort fills at the worst hour of the week "by construction". Measured, not

shifted arms land where they should — arm C `{4: 16337, 8: 1}`, arm D `{8: 16337}`. Broker hour
00 is the daily rollover and the measured 13×–38× hour of the week (AG §5); `fx` carries 16.67×
and `jpy_fx` 12.56× there, while `index`, `energy` and `metals` have **no hour-00 cell at all**
(they do not quote) and `crypto` is exactly 1.00. That is what makes the FX restriction a

### B1008 — the H4 re-entry: cost dominates gross by ~10:1, and arm A is AF's population exactly [MEASURED 2026-07-30]

Four arms, one **intersected** population — 16,337 decision bars where all four arms produced
a trade and the bar is engine-reachable, so the counts are equal by construction and the
per-arm difference is the entry instant and nothing else. 4,321 bars are excluded, almost all
Friday D1 bars whose next H4 close is 52 h away (a session gap, not a later fill).

**Arm A reproduces `AF_FAMILY_TRADES.json.gz` 42 of 42 members exactly on trade count AND on
summed R.** Two statistics, both exact, which is what makes the whole comparison about the same
program.

| arm | entry | exit bars | mean gross R | cost R (mid, v2) | median hold h | pre-entry drift R |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A | D1 close (broker 00) | D1, 80 | +0.00741 | 0.2357 | 96.0 | — |
| **B** (control) | D1 close | H4, 480 | +0.00872 | 0.2327 | 84.0 | — |
| **C** | first H4 close (04) | H4, 480 | −0.00672 | **0.0771** | 80.0 | +0.00734 |
| D | second H4 close (08) | H4, 480 | −0.01542 | 0.0823 | 80.0 | +0.01351 |

B exists so the resolution artifact (**+0.0013 R/trade**, A→B) does not get read as the entry
shift. B→C: **cost −0.1567 R/trade** (spread 0.1945 → 0.0348), **gross −0.0154**, **net +0.1412** —
a cost:gross ratio of **10.2 : 1** on the model's own cost convention.

**And that convention is the ceiling, which the first version of this block did not say.**
`cost_r` charges `crossings_charged: 1` (`model.py:403`, `:439`) and evaluates all of it at
`entry_utc`. A round-trip trade crosses the spread twice; the near-universal reading of "one
full spread per round trip" is half at entry and half at exit, and the source does not say
which it means. So moving the ENTRY instant is credited with 100 % of a bill whose exit half the
shift does not move — measured: the exit-hour distributions of arms B and C are near-identical
and the exit-instant spread is 0.0468 R against 0.0456 R. Re-attributed 50/50
(`ah_entry_attribution.py` → `AH_ENTRY_ATTRIBUTION.json`):

| attribution | cost B → C | saving | net | cost : gross |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `model_convention` (what the gate charges) | 0.2343 → 0.0777 | **+0.1567** | **+0.1412** | **10.2 : 1** |
| `half_at_each` | 0.1617 → 0.0830 | **+0.0788** | **+0.0633** | **5.1 : 1** |

A direction-aware split is the same number, because the model's quoted spread is symmetric
about mid. **Cost dominates gross on either reading — 5:1 or 10:1 — so the conclusion holds and
the magnitude is a range.** Every verdict in `ENTRY_HOUR_FRONTIER_V1.json` is charged
`model_convention`, so B1010's four zero-crossings sit at the ceiling and would move less under
`half_at_each`. Caught by an adversarial pass over this session's own headline. Under
`v1_multiplicative` the model-convention saving is 0.4318 R — AF's ~0.40 R figure, reproduced,
and 63 % of it was the composition defect. [MEASURED]

### B1012 — carrier stability, against a chance baseline my first version computed wrongly [MEASURED 2026-07-30]

AF routed 23 of 30 families `MEMBER_CONDITIONING_NOT_BREADTH`. A mixture family has positive
members; selecting them is only a strategy if the same members are positive out of sample. Per
family the pooled series is cut into five chronological quintiles and the carrier set (members
with positive mean gross R, ≥5 trades in that quintile) measured in each, then the Jaccard
overlap between consecutive quintiles is compared against **a chance baseline the script
computes** — without one, a family where 8 of 9 members are positive every fold scores ~0.9 by
arithmetic rather than by stability.

**The first version of that baseline was wrong in the flattering direction, and an adversarial
pass over this session's own claim caught it.** It drew both subsets from every member with ≥1
trade over the family's whole history and used `E|A∩B| / E|A∪B|`. But a quintile's carriers can
only come from the members SCORED IN THAT QUINTILE, and that universe grows from 2–3 to 9 across
quintiles in six of the 23 mixtures because the instruments came online at different dates. The
decisive case: a pair with a=3 drawn from a 4-member scored set and b=4 from a 4-member set has
a **true** chance Jaccard of exactly 0.75 — every possible draw gives 3/4, literally zero
information — where the old formula returned 0.235. Corrected to draw from each quintile's own
scored set and to average `|A∩B|/|A∪B|` over draws (exact enumeration; k ≤ 14 here).

| | first version | **corrected** |
|---|---|---|
| chance baseline range | 0.070–0.448 | **0.083–0.540** |
| overlap beats chance | 16 of 23 | **13 of 23** |
| overlap **below** chance | 6 of 23 | **9 of 23** |
| clears both clauses (overlap > chance AND holdout sign agreement ≥ 0.6) | 4 | **3** |

Observed overlap runs 0.000–0.635. The three that clear both clauses are
`energy_fvg_retest × crypto × H4` (+0.068 over chance, holdout 0.800),
`donchian × index × D1` (+0.065, 0.667) and `donchian × crypto × H4` (+0.039, 0.667) — margins
of 0.04–0.07 on a statistic whose own spread is larger than that. `donchian × metal × D1`, which
cleared the first version, does not clear the corrected one (0.191 against chance 0.238).
[MEASURED]

### B1013 — the honest carrier trade is worth nothing, on two weightings that disagree by 8× [MEASURED 2026-07-30]

Choose the carrier set on quintiles 0–3, score quintile 4 alone. One look per family, the rule
fixed before any quintile-4 number was read, compared against the same quintile-4 trades
unselected — so the number is "what member selection would have bought", not "what the best
members did". **All GROSS R, never net of broker-true cost.**

* **helps in 11 of 22 scoreable mixtures — a coin flip.** (The 23rd chose zero carriers, so
  selection would have skipped the family entirely; its quintile-4 mean was +0.100, which
  counts against selection rather than for it.)
* equal-weight-per-family: median **+0.00326 R/trade**, mean **−0.0355**, range −0.554 to +0.141;
* **trade-weighted over all 16,248 selected against 24,603 holdout trades: −0.004525 R/trade.**

The two weightings disagree by about 8×, and the reason is worth carrying: the equal-weight mean
is hostage to the two thinnest holdouts (20 and 32 selected trades, at −0.554 and −0.454) — drop
them and it becomes **+0.0114**. Both are published because the equal-weight mean is the one a
reader would quote and the trade-weighted one is the one that cannot be moved that way. On every
weighting the answer is the same: **member selection inside these families is worth nothing out
of sample**, and the residual biases in the construction (quintile-3 trades whose exits cross
into quintile 4; the skipped 23rd family) all run in the direction that would *flatter*
selection, so the conclusion is conservative.

**Therefore, and this is the prescription rather than the rejection:** what *does* move these
families is cost geometry — B1005's composition repair is worth up to +0.35 R/day per member and
B1008's entry shift another +0.14 on the FX cohort — plus AD's exit surface. The 23 route to
those, not to member picking. [MEASURED]

### B1015 — the crypto donchian carrier is the CELL, not the symbol [MEASURED 2026-07-30]

The named split (AF §3.2: DASHUSD +0.883 … LTCUSD −0.916 at H4) tested three ways:

* **noise**: permuting member labels over the pooled trades, the observed cross-member SD gives
  **p 0.0015 at H4** and **p 0.382 at D1**. Split-half sign agreement within each member's own
  history: **8 of 9 at H4**, 4 of 9 at D1. So the H4 split is real and the D1 one is not.
* **vintage**: r **+0.623** (t 2.11) at H4 and **+0.649** (t 2.26) at D1 — a consistent
  correlate, and **DASHUSD refutes it as the mechanism**: 1.7 years of history and the best H4
  member in the family.
* **liquidity** (log median tick volume): r **−0.228** at H4 and **+0.472** at D1. Opposite
  signs across timeframes, so it is refuted as an explanation.

**And the statistic the brief did not ask for, which settles it.** The same nine symbols rank
differently at the two timeframes: **Spearman 0.20**, sign agreement **5 of 9**. DASHUSD is
−0.210 at D1 and **+0.883** at H4; XRPUSD +0.147 and −0.604. The carrier is the
(symbol × timeframe) **cell**, so it cannot have a symbol-level cause — maturity and liquidity
are properties of the same instrument in both. [MEASURED]

REJECT. At the sealed `B_balanced` α of 0.10 the admission is **arithmetically unreachable at any
family size** — the largest family admitting `mx_btcusd` at 0.10 is 16 and `gate.py:797` floors
the effective family at `max(n_judged = 32, declared)`. And **α = 0.20 is `options.C_exploratory`'s
alpha**, whose sealed `author_note` (`options.py:110-111`) reads *"RESEARCH TRIAGE ONLY … never
'worth arming'. Do not let a C-pass reach a book."* The receipt's closing line "no threshold was
loosened" was false: α is a threshold and it was doubled. Also corrected: the BH boundary is
**≤ 33**, not 32 — `mx_btcusd` sits at rank 2. [MEASURED]

rule R0 forbids.** It reported both admitting at α = 0.10 at m ≤ 29 using **AF's RECORDED-era p
for `mx_btcusd` beside AA's all-eras p for `sub_xvol_pullback`**. `ai_recorded_era_gate.py`

quantified.** At m = 29, BH rank 1 needs p ≤ 0.003448 and rank 2 needs ≤ 0.006897.
`mx_btcusd` at 0.006399 is **already inside rank 2**; the pair is blocked because

## Wave 10 — Session AN: the population rule (B1250–B1266)

**B1250 — an undecidable era degraded NOTHING, and it is 182 eras rather than one quarter.**
`spread_model.py`'s coverage branch read `if fb is not None and ... not decidable: MODELLED`
**elif** `era_class not in ("RECORDED", "NO_BAR_HISTORY")`, so the `not decidable` arm was
reachable only through the no-bar-history fallback. On the ordinary era path an undecidable
**RECORDED** era matched neither branch and kept the anchor's own class: `BTCUSD 2020Q1` returned
`coverage=MEASURED` on a band whose own `capture_requirement` reads *"band spans 204058.1x, wider
than any verdict can survive"*, and every `coverage_policy="restrict_to_priced"` consumer took it
as priced (AL §3.3). **182 of the model's 275 undecidable eras are `RECORDED`** — 66.2 %, FTMO 134
of 195 and redacted_account 48 of 80 — and none of them degraded anything. `not decidable` now degrades
on every path. Counted exactly: the branch fires on all 275 and **192 change coverage CLASS** (166
RECORDED MEASURED→MODELLED, 26 QUANTIZED TRANSFERRED→MODELLED); the other 83 already sat at
MODELLED, 19 of them because their anchor was already MODELLED — which is why the honest figure is
192 and not the 211 a first draft of the source comment published. Monotone by construction
(`weakest()` cannot strengthen). Five behavioural tests, **each verified RED against the
pre-repair logic by copy-back and GREEN after**. [MEASURED — FIXED]

**B1251 — `require_decidable` is a GateSpec axis, and the seal-honesty rule it follows is
`spread_composition`'s and not `_ABSENT_MEANS_UNCHANGED`'s.** `SpreadModel.estimate` has taken
`require_decidable=` since AG shipped it and **no production path passed it** — its only call
sites anywhere were two tests. `GateSpec.spread_require_decidable` now threads
spec → `panel.price_trades` → `cost_r` → `spread_price`. The seal rule matters and is the opposite
of the drop-when-None rule: `None` and `False` are the *same behaviour*, so they must hash alike or
one methodology seals two ways; only `True` moves the seal. Verified three ways — pre-field spec
loaded from `8db17b29c` gives the identical hash for all three options at None and at False, and
the 18 published `spec_sha256` in the restored cohort reproduce 18/18 at HEAD. [MEASURED — FIXED]

**B1252 — the population rule is now in the seal, which for the whole of wave 9 it was not.**
AL reimplemented the era restriction three times inside one session (`al_decidable_population.py`,
`al_population_intersection.py`, `al_candidate_dossier.py`), each time as a per-trade filter
applied *before* `run_gate` — so two runs on two different populations produced the **same**
`spec_sha256`. `walkforward/era_population.py` names the four candidate rules once with the
argument for each, stamps the rule into `spec_id` (which `canonical()` hashes), and sets the flag
where the rule needs it. Filter and flag are deliberately redundant on the decidable-family rules,
so a divergence surfaces as a refusal count rather than as a silent difference. **Zero seal
collisions across 240 arms.** A design choice reversed mid-session and worth recording: the first
version dropped trades the model cannot classify, which launders a coverage shortfall into a
smaller population — `coverage_frac` would read 1.0 with nothing for `restrict_to_priced` to stamp.
They are KEPT now; the gate owns that accounting. Inert on these cells (0 unclassifiable trades),
so the choice was made on the principle because the measurement could not make it. [MEASURED —
FIXED]

**B1253 — 15 of the 18 published seals were guarded by a COUNT, and a fabricated-hash substitution
proved it.** `test_candidate_family.py::test_the_seal_migration_is_documented_in_both_directions`
pins the BROKEN cohort by exact prefix and the RESTORED cohort by `assert len(seals) >= n`. An
adversarial pass replaced all 18 restored seals with fabricated hashes in a temp copy of the five
artifacts and **the test still passed**. Exactly 3 are pinned by value, by
`test_AA_published_spec_seals_reproduce_again`. `tests/research_infra/test_published_seals_pinned_by_value.py`
pins all 18 by value (7 tests), so a future edit to `_ABSENT_MEANS_UNCHANGED` or `canonical()` that
rewrites the estate's published seals is loud instead of silent. [MEASURED — FIXED]

**B1254 — the coverage repair moves ZERO verdicts, and the commission's stated mechanism for why it
might is not the mechanism.** 48 arm-cells A/B'd with the pre-repair rule restored in-process (no
source reverted): **0 verdict fields moved, 0 sleeve-level coverage stamp fields moved.** Three
reasons, all measured. (1) `coverage_frac` is `n_priced / n_evaluable` and a trade is priced iff
`cost_r` did not RAISE — a coverage CLASS cannot move it, so item 5's *"coverage degradation feeds
`restrict_to_priced`"* is false. (2) **No code reads the coverage class into a verdict at all**: the
field that looks as if it would, `require_measured_cost_frac`, is declared at `spec.py:354` and read
by nothing in `src/` — stronger than the first draft's "it is 0.0 in all three options", which is
true and beside the point. (3) The stamps held for three *different* reasons — see B1255. Every
cost VALUE is byte-identical; this is a coverage-only repair. [MEASURED]

**B1255 — "the stamps were already saturated" was true of 16 of 48 arm-cells, not 48, and the
correction matters because it downgrades a guarantee to a fact.** Found by an adversarial pass. On
the 12 FLAT cells the repair is *inapplicable* (`model.py` enters the era path only when
`spread_band is not None`). On the 36 banded cells `weakest_coverage` is genuinely saturated at
MODELLED. `measured_frac` is saturated at 0.0 on the 16 `mx_btcusd` cells only — 16 of its 232
RECORDED trades sit in a gap-extrapolated era the pre-repair rule already forced to MODELLED, and
BTCUSD's `slippage_r` is TRANSFERRED at every instant. On the other 32 cells `measured_frac` is
LIVE (0.051–0.173) and held by **data**: all 39 fully-MEASURED-cost trades happen to sit in
decidable, non-gapped RECORDED eras, so no MEASURED trade was available to weaken. One undecidable

**B1321 — the p that admits it is a count of duplicate permutation draws, and the verdict flips on
the seed.** 44 trades → **16 OOS days** → block 2 → **8 blocks** → `perm_p_floor` **0.004006**,
against an observed 0.004200: headroom **1.048×**. `perm_null.py:201-202` is
`p = (1 + ge)/(n_perm + 1)` where `ge` counts draws beating the observation, so when the
observation is the maximum over all 2⁸ = 256 achievable sign assignments — which it is — `ge` is
just how many of 10,000 draws DUPLICATED the identity assignment: `Binomial(10000, 1/256)`, mean
39.06, sd 6.24, **p = 0.004006 ± 0.000624**. BH rank 1 (0.002564) is **2.3 sd BELOW** that floor,
so unreachable at 8 blocks; the rank-2 window above it is **1.8 sd** wide. MEASURED on the
production path over 20 permutation seeds: the cell gives p in [0.003500, 0.005799] with sd
**0.000658** against the 0.000624 predicted, and **its verdict flips on 4 of 20 seeds**. Both
controls hold — its ungated parent REJECTs at 20/20 and `mx_btcusd @ target_5R`, the estate's ONE
admission, ADMITs at **20/20** with a worst seed of p 0.002000 still inside rank 1. Nobody had
checked AL's admission for seed stability; it is stable. [MEASURED]

## Wave 11 — Session AS, the live-activation dossiers and the fleet map (B1500–B1549)

Branch `phase11/live-dossiers`. Three work orders: monitoring for the armed FIVE-sleeve book
(AS-1), the exit-contract activation dossier (AS-2), the replay fleet map (AS-3). **No file under
`src/` was modified**; both proposed exit-contract diffs are described, measured and tested but
deliberately not landed.

### AS-1 — the armed five, monitored like they deserve (B1500–B1519)

**B1500 — `fx_jpy`'s archive net expectancy at its own MEASURED carry is +0.041 R/trade on FTMO
and +0.019 on redacted_account, and that single fact is the whole risk story of the five-sleeve
expansion.** Computed from `AD_CARRY_TIERS_RESTATED_V1.json` as `archive_gross − cost_ex_swap −
swap_per_night × measured_nights_mean`. At that rate the sleeve needs **73.1 fills** (FTMO) /
**157.5** (redacted_account) to earn back the 3.0 R floor it would reach in **7.5** / **6.0** at the
rate its own live fills ran at — **roughly 20× faster to the downside bound than to the upside
one.** Not a prediction; the arithmetic of arming a near-zero-expectancy sleeve. The other four
armed sleeves run +0.239 to +1.246 R/trade. [MEASURED]

**B1501 — the live-fill prior for the armed set, and it exists for exactly one sleeve.** Of the
five armed sleeves, only `fx_jpy` has ever filled live: **32 fills** (FTMO 21, redacted_account 11),
all `stack_era: w7_book`, all `sleeve_resolution: exact`, 2026-06-15 … 2026-07-01, in the
2026-07-25 export — the only live corpus on this machine. **−9.269 R gross, −13.948 R net**
trade-weighted; 24 of 32 closed at the stop; the broker charged swap on **0 of 32**; longest hold
7.36 h against a 12-trading-hour stop that never bound. `crypto`, `energy_agri`,
`sub_xvol_pullback` and `sub_mid_dn_revert` have **zero** live fills, ever. [MEASURED]

**B1502 — the loss is real and it is not significant, and both halves have to be said.** Exact
sign-flip permutation over **day** blocks (the dependence unit — Session R measured lag-1 rho
0.511), per account: `fx_jpy`'s gross is distinguishable neither from zero (**p 0.3652** FTMO on
13 blocks, **p 0.3984** redacted_account on 8) nor from the archive gross of +0.28235 it was armed on
(**p 0.1631** / **0.2227**). 32 fills over 13 days cannot establish an edge in either direction.
**That is why every stop condition in this session is a RISK BOUND and not a test** — it bounds
what the owner pays to find out and claims nothing about having found out. [MEASURED]

**B1503 — a gross-negative tripwire must fire on BOTH weightings, and the live corpus is what
forced it.** On the same 21 FTMO fills: **−0.2487 R/fill trade-weighted against −0.1450
day-weighted**, a 42 % attenuation, because the losing days carry up to four fills and the winning
days carry one. `CANARY_OPERATOR_PAGE.md`'s C3 reads only the trade weighting and would therefore
report a sleeve's *worst* reading as its verdict. S2 now requires both, per account, over ≥ 20
fills and ≥ 8 day blocks. [MEASURED — FIXED]

**B1504 — and the pooling trap underneath it, found by getting it wrong first.** Pooling both
accounts into one day block flips the pooled day-weighted figure **POSITIVE (+0.0563)** while both
accounts are individually negative (−0.1450 / −0.1278). Two independent books sharing a calendar
day is not a block. Every figure in the AS-1 artifacts is computed per account for this reason.
This session published the pooled number in its own working notes before catching it. [MEASURED —
FIXED]

**B1505 — all five armed sleeves' live time stops are unit-correct, which is the good news.** Read
from the running module and cross-read against AQ's `spec_audit.sleeves`: `crypto`, `energy_agri`,
`sub_xvol_pullback`, `sub_mid_dn_revert` all carry 1280 printed M15 bars = **exactly 80 H4 bars =
`maxbars`**, classification `UNIT_CORRECT_DOES_NOT_BIND`, truncation **0.0**. `fx_jpy` is 48 of 80
own bars — tighter than research — classification `UNIT_CORRECT_BINDS_RESEARCH_NEVER_APPLIED_IT`,
truncation **0.2 %**, immaterial. **None of the five is in the mis-scaled `mx_*` cohort.**
[MEASURED]

**B1506 — `fx_jpy` and `sub_mid_dn_revert` are zero-carry sleeves and their break-even says so.**
`fx_jpy`'s break-even is **0.317 nights on FTMO and 0.051 on redacted_account** against an archive p90 of
**zero** nights. One night of carry on one trade in twenty ends the redacted_account edge. A stop
threshold that reads as impossibly tight is the sleeve's own arithmetic, not a tight threshold.
[MEASURED]

**B1507 — a first cut of the carry stop condition collapsed to a degenerate zero.** The rule was
`stop = min(break_even_nights, 2 × p90)`, and for a zero-carry sleeve `2 × p90` is 0.0, so the stop
threshold became "any carry at all" by accident rather than by argument. Restated as
`alert = p90, stop = break_even_nights`, with the zero-carry case named explicitly in the artifact.
[MEASURED — FIXED]

**B1508 — `scripts/book_sleeve_telemetry.py`**, read-only, no MT5 import, no config write. Per
(sleeve, account): fills, gross/net R on both weightings, cost, swap, hold distribution, close
reasons, longest stop run, and the six pre-registered conditions evaluated. Exit codes `0`/`1`/`3`
matching `canary_watch.py`, where **3 means "clean, but something could not be checked"** — silence
never renders as a clean bill. Against the historical corpus it reports 0 post-arming fills,
verdict `UNCHECKED`, exit 3, which is the correct answer. [MEASURED]

**B1509 — the pre-arming prior and the post-arming window are never merged, and it is enforced
rather than intended.** `test_pre_arming_losses_do_not_trip_any_condition` drives 40 pre-arming
fills at −1 R each through the evaluator and asserts every condition stays `UNCHECKED`. The prior
is evidence the owner already had when he accepted the risk; presenting it as a post-arming verdict
would be presenting his own decision back to him as news. [MEASURED]

**B1510 — a permutation test that returns nothing above 20 day blocks makes MORE data produce a
WEAKER statement.** The first cut of `signflip_p` enumerated 2ⁿ and returned `p=None` above 20
blocks — which is the *normal* case after a month of trading, not an edge case. Found by a
behavioural test asserting the power disclosure names its own floor. Now: exact enumeration to 20,
then a Monte Carlo **seeded from the data** so the number on the page is reproducible without a
wall clock or a global random state; the resolution floor (1/achievable or 1/draws) is reported
always. Pinned by determinism, boundary-agreement with the exact test (|Δp| < 0.01) and
shift-equivariance tests. [MEASURED — FIXED]

**B1511 — one implementation of the permutation test, not two.** `as_live_basis.py` imports
`signflip_p` from the tool that consumes its artifact rather than re-implementing it. Two copies
drift, and when they do the artifact and the page disagree about the same fills with nothing to say
which is right. [MEASURED]

**B1512 — the de-arm procedure, and the half that costs money if it is wrong.** Removing a sleeve
from `--tags` stops **new generation only**: `book_engine.py:493` applies tags, while
`book_owner.py:503` and `:2694` call `active_specs(None, …)` with tags **not** applied, so a
de-tagged sleeve's open position stays adopted and exit-managed. That is the safe direction and is
why de-arming needs no flatten. Separately, narrowing `--tags` mid-day does **not** reduce that

firing sleeves and `admission.py:1188` takes `na = max(na, override)` — so the other four keep the
five-sleeve multiplier until the decision day rolls. De-arm at a day boundary if the size step
matters. Pinned by `test_de_arm_claims_match_the_source`, which reads the actual lines. [MEASURED]

**B1513 — `phase11/FIVE_SLEEVE_OPERATOR_PAGE.md`**, generated by `as_operator_page.py` from the
committed artifacts with the provenance table stamped; nothing on it is transcribed and the
generator dies rather than printing a stale number. It complements `CANARY_OPERATOR_PAGE.md`

the five sleeves doing, and has any reached the line*. [MEASURED]

**B1514 — `energy_agri` is the only armed sleeve running a `partial_be_runner`, and AD measured
that feature at −0.308 R/day against the plain exit (n=67).** Thin, and a question rather than a

[MEASURED]

### AS-2 — the exit-contract activation dossier (B1520–B1539)

**B1520 — editing `final_target_r` in `SLEEVE_EXIT_PROFILES` is a NO-OP for the entire `mx_*`

real `build_book_trade_params`: the naive 5.0 edit resolves to **2.0 / TP 102,000**; dropping
`final_from_intent` resolves to **5.0 / TP 105,000**. **An activation package that landed

every band, while every spec read and every log said 5R.** [MEASURED]

works, but `TARGET_R` is a module constant every `mx_*` generator reads, so it moves **14** sleeves

`shared_execution_contract_digest_sha256`. **Neither change ends the parked B7.5 campaign option

`test_neither_touched_file_is_bound_by_any_seal_mechanism`. For contrast `config/agent_config.yaml`,

`AK_EXIT_FRONTIER_V2.json` carries **no population key and no `spread_band` key**, which means

**Control: AK's published cell reproduces to the digit** at ALL_ERAS/flat — R/day
1.1564749458527503, p 0.007799220077992201 — so any difference is the standard and not the

### AS-3 — the replay fleet map (B1540–B1549)

**B1540 — `phase11/REPLAY_FLEET_MAP.md` and `AS_FLEET_MAP_V1.json`: 15 members, 54.8 machine-hours
total, 18.8 excluding the parked campaign** — less than one sealed month-window for the entire
remaining fleet. Each member carries driver, machine-hours *with its basis*, memory class, the
verdict it moves, a value 1–5 with the reason it is that number, and what blocks it. Ordered by
**value per machine-hour**, deliberately not by how interesting the question is. [MEASURED]

**B1541 — the map is executable: it checks every driver path on disk and refuses to write if one is
missing.** 5 of 15 members have a driver that exists; **7 need one written first**, and that is
usually the larger cost. The distinction between "the grid exists, re-gate it" and "somebody has to
write this" is the single largest term in what a measurement costs, and a map that blurs it is a
wish list. The check caught one bad path in this session's own first draft. [MEASURED]

**B1542 — the cheapest item on the map is a precondition for the next activation.** F15 — a
read-only `copy_rates` probe on the two terminals, 0.2 MH, orchestrator-executed — decides whether
`mx_btcusd` can be armed **at all**. After AQ's repair an open `mx_*` position requests 7,744 M15
bars per tick, and if the terminal returns fewer than 7,680 closed bars the count can never reach
the budget and **the time stop never fires**; the wall-clock fallback does not catch it because that
path needs a `None`, not a short count. The backstop degrades to **inert**, not late. Top of the
map at 25.0 value/MH. [MEASURED]

**B1543 — the parked campaign costs 72× the item that would move an armed sleeve, and putting both
on one page is the point of the page.** F13 is 36 MH for a verdict the evidence already points at
(pooled must exceed +0.1 from −0.152; four negative January arms) and cannot legally run until a
pooled evaluator that **does not exist anywhere** is written and sealed. F1 is 0.5 MH and removes a
by-hand substitution three sessions have had to remember about an **armed** sleeve. [MEASURED]

**B1544 — the highest-value walkforward item is retrospective.** F6 re-gates published receipts at
each sleeve's live exit contract: AR's own winner lost 58 % of its measured advantage that way, and
AQ's Side-B table already found ten sleeves whose published economics describe a contract the book
does not run. It is the only item on the map that can change a number already in front of the
owner. [MEASURED]

**B1545 — the RESERVE-account activation gate, written as a checkable condition rather than a
date.** The owner set it in words ("after a while when tested on the 2"). Proposed: the third
account arms when **both** live accounts have ≥ 30 post-arming fills with no S1/S2 stop met, a cost
deviation inside the C1 tripwire on those fills, and at least one sleeve's post-arming R/day inside
its own archive band. **Until (a) is reachable the condition is UNCHECKABLE and the map says so**,
rather than proposing a date it cannot support. [MEASURED]

**B1546 — one item is priced at value 1 because that is what it is worth.** F9 (extending the
hour-01 entry convention to members AQ did not cover) is on the map because the commission named it;
AQ gated 72 arms at **0 admits, best p 0.3800**, an order of magnitude from the rank-1 bar. The
convention is a cost repair worth taking and it is not an edge, so extending it tests the same
conclusion again. A fleet map that prices everything it is asked about at 4/5 is not a map.
[MEASURED]

**B1547 — the sparse-checkout gap reproduced in a second worktree.** `BROKER_TRUE_COSTS_V1_1.json`
is tracked in git but its route directory is absent from the sparse profile, so every cost-true
driver dies on `CostTruthError`. AR filed this at B1473; it cost this session a failed run before
`git sparse-checkout add`. The failure mode reads as *"this measurement is expensive"* rather than
*"this worktree is incomplete"*, which is why it is worth a queue row and a fix to the **committed**
profile. [MEASURED]

### The adversarial pass, and what it changed (B1535–B1539, B1548)

Six load-bearing claims went to verifiers instructed to REFUTE and to default to "refuted" when
uncertain, each followed by an independent judge. **None was refuted outright; all six came back
CONFIRMED_BUT_NARROWER**, and between them they found one live defect on armed money, three defects
in this session's own instruments, and four stale or overstated citations. Every one is repaired
below or in the published text.

**B1535 — a live defect on armed money: rehydrating ANY `time_stop` position raised
`KeyError('trigger_r')`. Pre-existing, found by an adversarial pass on this session's dossier,
FIXED here.** `_vnext_time_stop_params` (`execution.py:1532-1562`) correctly returns no `trigger_r`
— a time stop has no break-even trigger — but `:3003` read `params["trigger_r"]` unconditionally.
That is **four of the five ARMED sleeves** (`crypto`, `sub_xvol_pullback`, `fx_jpy`,
`sub_mid_dn_revert`; only `energy_agri` is `partial_be_runner` and its params carry the key), and 28
of the 34 registered profiles. **It was fatal rather than degraded**: `book_owner.py:2729` calls
`hyd(rec)` with **no try/except** when `_live_broker_authority()` is true — which it is on both
funded accounts — and the `except TypeError` at `:2733` guards only the observe-only branch. A
KeyError is not a TypeError. The fix falls back to the payload's own
`gtos_vnext_dynamic_be_trigger_r`, which is exactly what `native_policy_instrumentation`
(`execution_packets.py:172`) already wrote, so it restores the intended value rather than inventing
one. Proved both ways by `tests/ultimate_book/test_time_stop_rehydration.py` (14 tests): reverting
the fix makes exactly the four `time_stop` sleeves fail with `KeyError('trigger_r')` and leaves
`energy_agri` passing. **One consequence of the fix, stated because it is a live-behaviour change:**
the adopt path now reaches the broker-TP modification it previously crashed before. [MEASURED —
FIXED]

**B1536 — two defects in this session's own re-gate driver, both silent.** (1) `failing_gates` was
computed as `sorted(k for k, v in sv.gates.items() if v is False)`, but `gates` values are **dicts**
(`gate.py:114`), never bare bools — so the field read empty on every arm including the REJECTs. The
`reasons` field carried the truth and is what was published, so no verdict was wrong; but it is the
silent-null class again, in my own instrument. (2) `maxbars_share` was stamped from the
**pre-population** row set, so every RECORDED arm reported `n: 88` beside `n_trades: 85`. Both
fixed; the corrected RECORDED shares are `target_4R` **7/85 = 0.0824** and `as_walked` **4/85 =
0.0471**, and both the filtered and pre-population figures are now published side by side. No
economic number moved. [MEASURED — FIXED]

**B1537 — a count rendered as authority was scraped rather than parsed.**
`n_code_authority_paths` published **20** where the tuple has **21**: the extractor kept only
quoted `ROOT/`/`CODE_ROUTE/` literals and silently dropped the unquoted `Path(__file__).resolve(),`
— the runner's self-binding. Now parsed with `ast`, which reports 21 and names the self entry. The
membership conclusion is unchanged (neither touched file is in the tuple under either count), but a
number cited as authority has to be parsed. Also fixed in the same pass: the membership table
checked `src/components/ultimate_book/candidate_registry.py`, a path that **does not exist** — the
real file is `sleeves/candidate_registry.py` — so the row truthfully reported "unbound" about
nothing. [MEASURED — FIXED]

**B1538 — the blast-radius instrument covered one of TWO production resolvers.**
`build_book_trade_params` honours `final_from_intent`; **`native_policy_instrumentation`
(`execution_packets.py:152-181`) does not** — it reads `final_target_r` at `:165-166` unguarded. So
under the *naive* edit the two DISAGREE: 2R at the broker, **5R in the rehydration payload**
`book_owner.py:2724` persists. That divergence was inert only because the hydrator raised
`KeyError('trigger_r')` first — and **B1535 fixed that, so it is now reachable.** The recommended
Route A (drop `final_from_intent`) is the only form of the change under which both resolvers carry
the same number, and that is now a reason for the recommendation rather than a preference. Three new
tests pin it, including one asserting no armed sleeve currently sits on the divergence. [MEASURED —
FIXED]

**B1539 — four citations corrected, one of them dead code.** (1) The de-arm procedure cited
`book_owner.py:503` (`_manageable_symbols`) alongside `:2694`; `_manageable_symbols` has **zero
callers repo-wide** — `b5d1b20d3` replaced its call with `_manageable_pairs` — so it carried none of
the claim. The conclusion is unchanged because `:2694` alone establishes it, and its consumers
(`:1985` `manage_open_positions`, `:2093` `_alert_out_of_universe`) are now named so a reader can see
why it is load-bearing. (2) `na = max(na, override)` is `admission.py:1210`, not `:1188`. (3) H8's
flatten suppression is `:2382` and the observe-only degradation `:2544`, not CLAUDE.md's
`:2364-2373` / `:2526` — one commit stale, behaviour unchanged. (4) The conviction claim is **gated**
on `kelly_running_count` AND `kelly_lite` both being true (`book_engine.py:892`); both are true on
the live hosts, so it holds today as a property of that config and not of the code. **And one thing
the de-arm procedure does NOT cover, now stated:** de-arming via the *include flags* rather than
`--tags` DOES drop a sleeve from `_manageable_pairs` (`:2696-2699`) and would orphan an open
position. `--tags` is the safe mechanism; an include-flag flip is not. [MEASURED — FIXED]

**B1548 — three overstatements in this session's own published text, corrected.** (1) *"every log
would say 5R"* is **false**: `build_book_trade_params` writes the resolved 2.0 into
`gtos_vnext_dynamic_final_target_r` (`execution_packets.py:353`), which is what `book_owner.py`
persists and emits, so the runtime telemetry would correctly read 2R. The discrepancy is
spec-versus-log and **the log is the one telling the truth** — better news for anyone watching a
book and worse for anyone reviewing a diff. (2) *"pooling mixes two independent books"* — they are
**not independent**: 10 of the 11 redacted_account `fx_jpy` fills are the same signal as an FTMO fill
2–58 s apart, gross-R correlation **0.9884** with 10/10 sign agreement. The per-account split stays
(each account is its own book with its own costs, floors and decision) but the reason is bookkeeping,
and the two p-values are very nearly one test rather than two. The `+0.0563` pooled flip is also
driven by a **single fill**; the requirement that S2 fire on both weightings rests on the 42 %
attenuation, which is not thin. (3) *"1280 printed M15 bars = 80 H4 bars"* is a **measured** identity
for these symbols, not a definitional one — `AD_TIMESTOP_UNITS_V1.json` puts
`m15_per_own_bar_trade_weighted` at exactly 16.0 for the four armed H4 sleeves, and at **92** rather
than 96 for `mx_ger40` / `mx_jp225` / the `mx_us*` sleeves. Stating it as definitional is the same
unit conflation AQ caught. Also: the truncation figures are **AD's** wave-7 measurements carried
forward, not AQ's, and `fx_jpy`'s 0.2 % is a **trade** count whose R-weighted figure is ~20× larger.
[MEASURED — FIXED]

**B1549 unused.**
## Wave 12 — Session AU (contract wiring + estate restamp), blocks B1550–B1599

**B1550 — the two frontier exit contracts are wired, selectable per sleeve, and default-off.**

it cannot produce AR's KeyError-against-`DEFAULT_CONFIG` outage, and no byte of either live YAML moves.

[MEASURED — CORRECTS AN AQ ROW]

### AV-1 — proving a bar file's clock from its own bytes (B1600–B1622)

**B1600 — the weekly-rollover probe: a clock test that works on FX.** The exchange-anchor
estimator in `scripts/measure_broker_clock_offset.py` needs a cash-equity open and its own
`ANCHORS` table says a EURUSD probe returns noise, so it cannot classify an FX file. The spot
week begins at the **New York 17:00 interbank rollover** whatever clock the file is written in;
map each week's first and last bar to UTC under a candidate hypothesis, subtract that instant,
and the residual is a CONSTANT under the correct hypothesis and DST-shaped under a wrong one.
**The discriminating statistic is the number of SEAMS in the residual, not its level**, which
is what makes the instrument's own session convention (0 h for spot FX, +1 h for an index CFD
opening an hour into the week) irrelevant. `phase12/receipts/av_timebase_verify.py`. [MEASURED]

**B1601 — the third `time_column_basis`, tested as a hypothesis rather than inferred.**
`broker_server_local_eu_calendar_corrected`: broker wall clock with an EET/EEST offset already
subtracted, so true UTC outside a US/EU DST disagreement window and exactly one hour fast
inside one. Added to `src/utils/research_timebase.py` (R2-unbound, checked) with its own
`to_true_utc` branch, and to `CsvBarSource` as encoding `eu_corrected`. It is run through the
same probe as the other two so a file either fits it or does not. [MEASURED — BUILT]

**B1602 — the disagreement window is COMPUTED, never tabulated.**
`in_us_eu_dst_disagreement(day)` is `round(Berlin − New_York) != 6 h`. A hardcoded transition
table is a calendar claim that goes stale, and this programme has already paid for one of
those (F7). Pinned against seven known dates and cross-checked day-by-day over 2024–2027
against the verifier's own copy so the two implementations cannot drift. [MEASURED]

**B1603 — `data/historical/` carries the EU-calendar correction this repository blamed on the
VPS copy alone.** `research_timebase.py:99-101` says this repo's copy "is ALREADY corrected"
and attributes the defect to the VPS. Measured per file: the repo copy carries it too — its
week-open residual is 0 h outside the disagreement windows and +1 h inside them, on every
window from 2023-03 to 2026-03, on GBPJPY, NZDUSD, GBPUSD, USDJPY, US30_cash and XAUUSD. The
comment's CONCLUSION (leave the directory unregistered, verify the specific copy, write it a
sidecar) was right; its description of this copy was incomplete. [MEASURED]

**B1604 — `data/historical/` is TWO CAPTURES SPLICED at 2026-04-03.** Seven intraday files
resolve to a clock only when truncated there; their tails sit on a different one (`+3`/`+4`
week-open residuals against a `0`/`+1` body). Proved by truncation: `GBPJPY_H1`, `GBPUSD_H1`,
`USDJPY_H1`, `GBPJPY_M15`, `GBPUSD_M15`, `USDJPY_M15` and `US30_cash_M15` all go
REFUSE_UNRESOLVED → STAMP_EU_CALENDAR_CORRECTED when cut. [MEASURED]

**B1605 — sidecars gain a declared validity window, and the reader fails closed outside it.**
`valid_from` / `valid_through` on the sidecar; `read_bars` raises
`TimeBaseOutOfDeclaredRangeError` (a subclass of `UndeclaredTimeBaseError`, so existing
fail-closed callers keep failing closed); `CsvBarSource` **drops** out-of-window rows and
reports the count on `describe()["rows_dropped_outside_declared_timebase_window"]`, because a
silent drop is the failure mode this programme keeps re-finding. [BUILT]

**B1606 — the bounded-prefix search, and the monotonicity it must not assume.** When a whole
file is unresolved, bisect for the longest prefix that proves a clock. The bisect assumes the
predicate is monotone in the cut date and **it is not** — a few contaminated tail weeks can sit
inside a passing prefix without yet moving the modal share, and my bisect landed on 2026-04-08
where the hand truncation resolved at 2026-04-03. Corrected: the bisect chooses only the
HYPOTHESIS, and the bound comes from the **first seam observed over the whole file**. [MEASURED
— FIXED]

**B1607 — the control the probe must never contradict.** `data/historical_2026/` is FTMO
broker-local by an independent exchange-anchor measurement. The per-file probe returns **50
STAMP_BROKER_LOCAL and zero contradicting verdicts** there, under-claiming on 22 files for
reasons that are all explainable (24/7 instruments have no weekly rollover gap; a European
index's Friday close moves with EU DST against a US-calendar broker clock; some series are
under the 12-week floor). **Under-claiming is the correct failure direction**, and it is pinned
by a test that fails if any control file is ever assigned a different clock. [MEASURED]

**B1608 — my first classifier refused the control on an arbitrary week count, and the floor
was standing in for a real condition.** `MIN_WEEKS = 30` refused 44 known-good files at 29
weeks. The real requirement is that the three hypotheses are IDENTICAL outside a US/EU
disagreement window, so a file whose span contains none cannot separate them at any length.
Replaced by that condition (`REFUSE_SPAN_TOO_SHORT_TO_DISCRIMINATE`, ≥ 2 evaluable weeks each
side). **The control is what caught it**; on the target files there was no independent answer
to check against. [MEASURED — FIXED]

`data/historical/GBPJPY_D1.csv` classified as broker_local purely because the parser turned

midnight is the real convention), which is what made it dangerous. [MEASURED — FIXED]

**B1610 — holiday displacement is not clock evidence, and a capture boundary is not a market
boundary.** Two filters, both principled rather than tuned: a residual further than 4 h from
the file's own modal residual cannot be a clock (no two candidate clocks differ by that much),
so it is a market holiday moving the week's first PRINT and is excluded and counted; and the
first and last evaluable week of every file are dropped, because a file starting mid-week has
no rollover in it and one cut on a Wednesday has no close. [MEASURED]

trade trains on its own outcome, no trade trains on an outcome that had not happened when it
was entered, the purge/embargo §4.8 requires is the gap itself, and there is no separate test
set to leak through because every score comes from a model that could have existed at that
instant. A test walks every scored row and checks the eligible training set against the row's
own entry time. Quantile cuts are taken on the TRAINING window's distribution, never the
scored one. [BUILT]

### AV-4 — what pooling actually buys (B1647–B1660)

**B1647 — the sample constraint is two currencies, and the estate has been treating them as
one.** The gate's null is a block sign-flip on the pooled DAILY series, so the resolution
currency is distinct decision DAYS: a member firing on days its family already covers adds a
trade to an existing block and buys ZERO resolution; one firing on days nobody covers adds a
block. Calendar time and width are therefore different purchases and only one of them is on
sale. [MEASURED]

**B1648 — width is exhausted on 29 of 30 families.** Census at the ratified rule, 30 of 30
REJECT: **CALENDAR_TIME_ONLY 13, NEITHER_REACHES 15** (p = 1.0 — the effect has the wrong sign,
so no amount of data helps), **BOTH 1** (`fam_donchian_20_breakout_crypto_d1`, p 0.0938),
**NOT_EVALUABLE_AT_RANK 1**. The mechanism, measured: the median member brings **31.8 %** of
its own decision days as NEW blocks and 8 families are under 20 % —
`fam_donchian_20_breakout_fx_h4` at **1.2 %** with 9.42 trades per block, which is fourteen
members watching one market. [MEASURED]

**B1649 — the FVG family cannot admit at rank 1 at ANY effect size.** AP §1.5 routed
`fam_energy_fvg_retest_energy_h4` as "the residual is sample". At **9 gate blocks** its p-floor
is **0.00205** while the BH rank-1 bar at m = 298 is **0.000336** — the bar sits BELOW the
floor, so the honest report is `NOT_EVALUABLE_AT_RANK`, not a p (wave-11 §2). Its own
acquisition arithmetic: 17.2× the data, +146 blocks, ≈ **16.5 more years** at its measured 8.8
blocks/year. `maxbars` share 7.5 %. [MEASURED]

**B1650 — pooling is not uniformly bad, and AO's result is a property of day-overlap.** Pooling
HELPED the FVG family (pooled p 0.206 against a best solo of 0.390 — ratio **0.53**) and HURT
`fam_volume_surge_reversal_index_d1` (**1.42**), whose six members share **84 %** of their
decision days. AO measured the second shape on nine BTC members; it reproduces here on a
different family, and the first shape shows it is not a law about pooling. [MEASURED]

**B1651 — the requirement, in both currencies, per family.**
`fam_volume_surge_reversal_index_d1`: 72.5× the data, +2,073 blocks — **56.3 more years** at
its own 36.8 blocks/year, or **327 more members** at its own 6.3 new blocks per added member.
The z-scaling assumes the effect size holds as the sample grows, which is the OPTIMISTIC case
given AN's measured 7.6× chronological decay; stated as a caveat on every requirement. [MEASURED]

**B1652 — two block counts appear and they are not a contradiction.** The raw stream's
decision-day count (46 / 237) and the gate's bootstrapped block count (9 / 29) measure
different things: the gate counts inside its SCORED FOLDS, after the population filter and the
thin-fold drop. The resolution verdict is taken on the gate's and the acquisition arithmetic on
the raw rate, and the artifact stamps both with that note. [MEASURED]

**B1653–B1660 — the member→family map is rebuilt from the production `FamilyMember`, not from
the member name.** The family key is `fam_<mechanism>_<ASSET CLASS>_<tf>` and the asset class
is not recoverable from `mxf_<mechanism>_<symbol>_<tf>` by string surgery. AR §5.7's finding is
the argument: two naming conventions for one object made a triple-count invisible to the eye
AND to the ratchet, and it was caught by identity rather than by name. Unmapped members are

**B1702 — so the lever is memoisation, not suppression, and the engine's own cache does not
take it.** `package_new_entry_authority_payload_hash_sha256`
(`moonshot_scheduler_v4_best_trade_allocator.py:896-908`) computes
`canonical_preimage = _stable_sha256_material(payload)` — the recursive canonicalisation plus
`json.dumps` that **is** the expense — and only then consults
`_PACKAGE_AUTHORITY_HASH_CACHE`. The cache therefore saves the sha256 and none of the cost.
Two independent validators (`signed_envelope_failures` and
`package_new_entry_authority_immutable_payload_failures`) pull the *same* payload object out of
the *same* surface and hash it separately, per surface, per candidate. [MEASURED]

**B1703 — a design died to a microbenchmark before it was written.** The obvious accelerator
for `abc.Mapping` dispatch (80.0 s of self-time across `__instancecheck__` 65.8,
`__subclasscheck__` 9.9 and `__subclasshook__` 4.3) is a surrogate class with a fast
`__instancecheck__`. Measured on this machine over a mixed workload: abc **88.5 ns**, metaclass
surrogate **126.0 ns**, concrete `dict` **16.9 ns**. The surrogate is **42 % slower than the
thing it replaces** — `abc`'s check is already C-cached and a Python-level `__instancecheck__`
adds a frame the C path does not have. Only concrete-type rebinding wins, which converts
exhaustiveness from a style choice into a measurement obligation; hence the `--verify` mode
that computes both answers on every check and counts disagreements. [MEASURED]

**B1704 — the sealed contract pins cyclic GC off for the whole replay day, so the intra-day

`replay_acceleration_attempt5_typed_sparse_runner.py:16838-16839` and `chunk_size = 1`
(`b7_5_post_acceleration_runner.py:110`), so the GC-off window is exactly the window in which
`THIRD_REVIEW.md` §A1 measured the heap ramping 0 → 5.5 GB and collapsing at the day boundary.
Re-enabling GC is the obvious memory fix and **the sealed lane cannot take it**: the R2-bound
`verify_denominator_to_deployment_execution.py:5161-5167` requires
`automatic_gc_enabled_before_explicit_collection` and `..._after_...` to be exactly `False`, and
records them per chunk. Any real fix to the ramp is a contract regeneration, not a runtime flag
— which is the price the next session needs before it budgets the memory work. The patch is
built, default-off, and flagged `sealed_compatible=False` in every receipt it appears in.
[MEASURED]
