**B1707 — peak RSS went UP, and the memo's design is why.** 7.72 → 7.99 GB (**+3.4 %**). The
identity memo holds a **strong reference** to every keyed payload — deliberately, because that
is what makes `id()` reuse impossible and the identity argument sound — and that also pins
everything each payload transitively references. `MEMO_MAX_ENTRIES` is 4096 and was chosen
without measuring what a payload retains. +270 MB for a 2.0 % hot-path saving is a bad trade,
and it is the kind of regression that ships unnoticed unless the A/B measures peak RSS as well
as wall. [MEASURED]

**B1708 — the shipped ABC patch recovered about a quarter of its 80.0 s target because
`Sequence` was left on abc, and turning it on is a verify decision rather than a judgement
call.** The hot recursion tests `isinstance(value, Mapping)` and then
`isinstance(value, Sequence) and not isinstance(value, (str, bytes, bytearray))`. Every scalar
leaf — most nodes — fails the first (now 16.9 ns) and pays the full abc price on the second.
Rebinding `Sequence` → `(list, tuple)` is **exactly** equivalent *at that call site* because
the next clause excludes str/bytes/bytearray anyway, and **not** equivalent in general: `str`,
`bytes`, `range` and `memoryview` are Sequences and are not in the tuple. There are 37 other
`isinstance(..., Sequence)` sites in the timewarp loop and 11 in the allocator; a site of the
form `if isinstance(v, Sequence): for item in v:` would iterate a string's characters under abc
and skip it under the tuple — a silent behaviour change. Registered in the patch table,
**off by default**, opt-in via `--abc-symbols`. [MEASURED]

**B1709 — two runs of one arm CANNOT produce identical ledgers, and the reason is structural,
not economic.** The engine refuses to reuse an output namespace
(`configure_output_namespace`, `attempt5_output_namespace_must_be_new`) and stamps the
namespace **inside row values** — `campaign`,
`package_replay_order_executable_bound_order_id` — and inside payloads that are then hashed,
so `packet_sidecar_id` and six sibling digest fields differ by construction and no string
normalisation can recover them. Raw frozen-vs-fast difference count 328; after normalising the
namespace out of string values, **244, every one a 64-hex provenance digest across 7 field
names, with ZERO moved quantities** over **123,813** scalar field comparisons. A comparator that
classifies its own leftovers as benign is marking its own homework, so the claim is made
against a control — the frozen engine re-run under a different prefix, compared by the same
comparator. [MEASURED]

**B1710 — the acceptance instrument broke three times before the engine did, each time as an
absence that read as a pass.** (1) The missed-opportunity aggregate summed `net_r`/`exact_r`;
neither field exists on a missed row, so it returned +0.0/−0.0 over 8,807 rows with every one
silently skipped — and two such zeros compare EQUAL, so the comparator would have reported
`R_IDENTICAL` while comparing nothing. Now mirrors
`analyze_b7_5_selection_sizing_matrix.py:742-770` exactly (`opportunity_net_proxy_r` under the
diagnostic-scoreable gate; 1,539 scoreable rows, +335.85 / −2077.44 R on the fixture) and
counts `unreadable_proxy_rows`. (2) `extract_economics` returned an empty payload for an absent
route — four digests of the empty string — and that empty payload **overwrote a good comparison
file**; it now raises `economics_route_absent`. (3) A run-namespace prefix shorter than 8 chars
is a substring of every 64-hex digest, so normalising `"a"` rewrote every `a` in every digest
and made two DIFFERENT digests compare equal; caught by its own unit test, now refused with the
refusal reported. **"Silent nulls fall loudly" is a rule about your own instruments before it is
a rule about the engine's.** [MEASURED — FIXED]

**B1711 — the reproduction is proved by CONTROL, and the control makes the claim airtight.**
Running the frozen engine a second time under a different output prefix and comparing it to the
first frozen run produces **exactly the signature the fast lane produces**: 244 differences,
all 64-hex provenance digests, **0 moved quantities**, across the same seven field names at the
same multiplicities — `packet_sidecar_id` 92, `scheduler_packet_sidecar_id` 77,
`scheduler_option_trace_projection_sha256` 25,
`finalizer_primary_probe_risk_authority_packet_hash_sha256` 21, `candidate_packet_sidecar_id`
10, `execution_packet_sidecar_id` 10, `risk_authority_packet_hash_sha256` 9. **The fast lane
differs from the frozen engine in exactly the way the frozen engine differs from itself.** Row
counts identical on all three runs. This is the acceptance the commission set, and it is a
control rather than an assertion — a comparator that classifies its own leftovers as benign is
marking its own homework. [MEASURED]

**B1712 — the control also measures run-to-run noise, which the speedup has to clear, and
nobody had that number before.** Two frozen runs of the identical 2-day fixture on this
machine: **636.7 s and 624.6 s — a 1.94 % spread**; peak RSS 7.72 and 7.73 GB (stable to
0.1 %). So the fast lane's 594.3 s is **1.061× against the frozen mean**, with a per-run band of
1.051–1.071×. The improvement is real and it is about three times the noise. Any future
optimisation claim on this fixture that quotes a single frozen run as its baseline is quoting
inside a ±2 % band. [MEASURED]

**B1713 — the authority payload hash is called 52.0 MILLION times on a two-day fixture, and
99.89 % of those calls see a payload object nobody has hashed before. The cost is the CALL
COUNT, not the call.** [MEASURED — memo counters, `AX_REPRODUCTION_RECEIPT.json` →
`fast.memo_report`.] 52,064,280 calls over 8,812 candidates = **5,902 recursive
canonicalisation + `json.dumps` + SHA-256 operations per candidate**. The identity memo AX
built to attack the 210.4 s subtree achieved a **0.11 % hit rate** (55,672 hits; 3.1 % frozen
passthrough; **0 mismatches**, so it was correct and merely useless) because the caller rebuilds
the payload as a **new dict** each time — the repetition is *logical*, not *referential*, so no
identity key can ever hit. It saved ~0.2 s, cost ~5 s of `id()` lookups across 52 M calls, and
added **+270 MB of peak RSS**; it is now **default-off**, and the number it produced is worth
more than the patch was. Two untested directions follow: memoise one level up (the attribution
projection does key on stable surfaces), or stop recomputing a digest the caller already holds.
The engine's own cheap 12-field cache key exists (`_package_authority_hash_cache_key`) and is
discarded in favour of recomputing the full material — trusting it is a contract-level decision
with a quantifiable collision risk, not an implementation one. [MEASURED]

**B1714 — two concurrent arms are possible and not worth it: 1.224× real throughput for
+4.39 GB of swap.** [MEASURED, `AX_CONCURRENCY.json`.] `S0R0` + `S1R1`, both on the fast lane,
both on the 2-day fixture, both completed with row counts identical to every other run.
Concurrent wall **971.3 s**; each arm's own wall under contention 964.7 / 962.3 s against
**594.3 s solo** — a **1.62× per-arm slowdown**. Against the honest serial reference
(2 × 594.3 = 1,188.6 s) the pair bought **1.224×**, not 2×. Machine swap grew **4.39 GB**
(peak 9.20 GB used; macOS extended the swap file 5,120 → 9,216 MB) and mid-run the two arms
sat at **88.9 % and 26.5 % CPU** — one running, one page-starved. **Do not quote the harness's
own `speedup_vs_serial: 1.984`**: it divided the sum of the *contended* arm walls by the
concurrent wall, which approaches `len(arms)` whenever two processes overlap at all — it
measures overlap, not benefit. The field is renamed `overlap_ratio_not_speedup` and the harness
now refuses to guess a solo reference it cannot know. Sampled peak total RSS (7.38 GB for BOTH
arms, against 7.99 GB for ONE arm solo) is not the arms shrinking — it is macOS compressing
their working sets out from under the sampler; RSS stopped measuring demand and the swap figure
is the one that means anything. AX-3's precondition ("if AX-1 collapses the footprint") was
**not met**: peak RSS went 7.72 → 7.99 GB. [MEASURED]

**B1715 — the per-ledger SHA-256 does NOT establish nested-field equality across runs, and the
receipt says so instead of implying otherwise.** A ledger digest hashes rows that contain the
run-namespace-derived packet digests (`packet_sidecar_id` and six siblings), so it can never
match between two runs — it is a within-run integrity artifact, not cross-run evidence.
**Nested (non-scalar) fields are therefore not independently verified.** What IS verified is
**123,813 scalar field comparisons with zero moved quantities** (5 trade rows × 1,322 fields,
10 order × 1,171, 96 scorecard × 1,098) plus the frozen-vs-frozen control on the 244
packet-digest differences. The 4 per-ledger digest entries in the signature are structurally
downstream of those 244 and were not independently controlled, because the frozen baseline's
digests were computed before namespace normalisation existed and its output route had already
been auto-deleted. Closing that gap is one line of future work: recompute the ledger digest
with the seven packet-digest field names excluded. [MEASURED — limit disclosed]

**B1852 — six of the eight wired frontier sleeves killed `run_book.py` at LAUNCH, after
validation had accepted them.** The banner rendered `float(_o["final_target_r"])`
unconditionally and the six `time_stop_*` cells carry no such key, so
`--frontier-exits vol_compression` (or any of the five `mx_*` short horizons) raised

Repaired on mainline **and** in the carried payload by
`execution_packets.describe_frontier_contract`, which renders whichever contract keys the

**B1853 — `run_book.py`'s host bytes are pinned by no artifact, and the answer is a variant
table rather than a guess.** The Stage-0 token ceremony (`phase3/TOKEN_CARRY.md`) recorded line
counts and no sha256. The host's state is nonetheless *bounded*: its `book_owner.__init__` (the
Session S payload) accepts neither `recover_pre_gap_bar` nor `vol_level_tilt`, so any `run_book`
from Session AI onward would raise `TypeError` at startup on both namespaces — and both books

`a850baf45cab` (18,700), `96ac1b566dc8` (19,218), **`014ce9df03fa` (19,886, the wave-3
integration state and the primary)**. A payload is pre-built for each with its own exact
after-sha256; `--check preflight` reads the host's sha256 and names one, and an unrecognised
sha256 is a **STOP with the bytes printed** rather than a default. The derivation is re-run in

**B1854 — the whole-file/anchored-edit split, decided by import closure rather than by size.**
`execution_packets.py` and `order_router.py` carry whole: each one's diff against the lineage is
**exactly** the change being carried and each one's import header is **byte-identical** to the
lineage's, so neither adds an edge to the host's module graph (pinned behaviourally by an AST
subset check). `book_owner.py` is ~330 lines of diff and 4,100 lines longer on mainline, so it
carries as the host's own bytes plus **four** anchored edits — the whole of AU's threading: the
kwarg, the field, the router construction, the adopt-rehydration call. `run_book.py`: two
anchored edits, deliberately **without** mainline's `recover_pre_gap_bar`/`vol_level_tilt`
kwargs. [MEASURED]

**B1855 — nine of sixteen partial states are unsafe, and a module-top import probe finds ZERO
of them.** All 2⁴ subsets materialised as real trees and probed. Session AC's grid found half

`UltimateBookOrderRouter.place` wraps its body in `except Exception` — *"the book NEVER breaks

healthy, exit management keeps running, and **every unit refuses to place, forever**. Worse than

## Wave 13 — Session BA, the redacted_account weekend-holding solution (B1900–B1913)

Receipts: `phase13/receipts/BA_WEEKEND_V1.json`, `phase13/receipts/BA_EARLY_CLOSE_DATES_V1.txt`,
`phase13/receipts/ba_weekend.py`, `phase13/receipts/REPAIR_QUEUE_BA.json`,
`receipts/session_ba_ab/SESSION_BA_AB.md`. Owner package
`phase13/BA_WEEKEND_POLICY_OWNER_PACKAGE.md`; result doc
`phase13/SESSION_BA_WEEKEND_SOLUTION_RESULT.md`. Nothing armed; no config byte; VPS untouched.

**B1900 — the weekly close is broker-local Saturday 00:00, measured on 18 symbols.** Across the
non-crypto symbols the armed four trade, **99.65–99.93 %** of calendar weeks in
`vps-bars-20260727` contain exactly one weekend gap, and the last H4 bar before it OPENS at
broker **Friday 20:00** — closing exactly at Saturday 00:00. Both live servers resolve the same
instant on **all 365 days of 2026** (`America/New_York + 7 h`), so a policy measured on the FTMO
archive is a policy about the redacted_account account. That equality is what makes the live default
`flatten_before_hours=4.0` *identical* to the research `m0` cell rather than analogous to it.
[MEASURED]

**B1901 — `BTCUSD` and `DASHUSD` trade through most weekends, so "the weekend" is a property of
(symbol, week).** BTCUSD gapped the weekend in **43.8 %** of its weeks and quoted straight
through the other 56.2 % (weekend-bar share 0.196); DASHUSD gapped 14 %. Every one of the 18
non-crypto symbols carries **zero** Saturday or Sunday bars. Consequence: the `crypto` sleeve's
weekend exposure is 45.9 % of trades under a calendar reading of the firm rule and **15.5 %**
under a market-close reading. [MEASURED]

**B1902 — the weekend-crossing census's own R comparison is survivorship and must not be read as
the cost.** Crossing trades average +1.036 / +1.038 / +1.902 R gross against +0.482 / +0.245 /
+0.212 for non-crossing ones on `crypto` / `sub_mid_dn_revert` / `sub_xvol_pullback`: a trade
still open on Friday night is a trade that did not stop out earlier in the week. Crossing is an
OUTCOME, not a treatment. `energy_agri` INVERTS (−0.135 crossed vs +1.436), which is what makes
the confound visible rather than plausible. Only the counterfactual replay prices the policy.
[MEASURED]

**B1903 — the Friday flatten costs the armed four −0.7753 R/day, 42.8 %, and two thirds of it is
one sleeve.** At the ratified rule (`RECORDED`, `CANDIDATE_BOOK_V1` V9 = 53, `B_balanced`
α 0.10, mid band, chronological folds): `sub_xvol_pullback` −0.5139 (**66.3 % of the bill**,
+1.0215 → +0.5076), `crypto` −0.2192 (28.3 %), `energy_agri` −0.0242 (3.1 %),
`sub_mid_dn_revert` −0.0180 (2.3 %). **368 gated cells, 0 ADMIT.** Flattening beats dropping at
three of four cost bands for every sleeve; the exception is **`crypto` at the HIGH band, where
the calendar flatten takes it to −0.0382** (+0.1815 under the market-close reading), which is the
one place the compliance cost turns a sleeve's funded-book membership into a real question.
Post-flatten book sum by band: +1.1214 / +1.0847 / +1.0345 / +0.8830. The DELTA is band-invariant
(B1905) and the LEVEL is not, and a drop-or-keep decision reads the level. [MEASURED]

**B1904 — the crypto reading is worth 28 % of the bill, +11.7 pp of `p_pass` and 78 days.** Under
the market-close reading `crypto`'s bill is **−0.0005 R/day** instead of −0.2192, the
four-sleeve book's redacted_account two-phase `p_pass` goes **0.6282 → 0.7447** (se ±0.0022) and
median calendar days to a payout **689 → 611**. One support ticket decides it; the conservative
reading is the default until it is answered (OD-BA-1). [MEASURED]

**B1905 — a cost delta is not a band quantity.** The flatten's delta is identical to **eight
decimal places** at flat/low/mid/high (`−0.51388000` × 4 on `sub_xvol_pullback`), because it
changes gross R and swap while leaving the trade SET — and therefore the spread charge —
untouched. Cells that DROP trades do vary by band (`m24h` on `crypto`: −0.3218 / −0.3246 /
−0.3250 / −0.3544). So the ratified "admits at N of 3 bands" phrasing describes a LEVEL;
publishing the band column for a same-population delta is still right and reading a spread
across it as evidence would be wrong. [MEASURED]

**B1906 — zero margin is dominated by one bar of margin on all four sleeves.** `m_inclusive`
(exit exactly at the weekly close) vs `m0`: `crypto` −0.3416 vs −0.2192, `energy_agri` −0.0505
vs −0.0242, `sub_xvol_pullback` −0.5896 vs −0.5139, `sub_mid_dn_revert` −0.1009 vs −0.0180.
Holding the last four hours of the week costs more than it earns AND is charged the weekend
rollover, so the a-priori default is the cheaper cell as well as the fillable one. [MEASURED]

**B1907 — the entry embargo is REFUTED as a repair, and `p_pass` is how it hides.** On three of
four sleeves it makes the flatten worse. The one combination that looks better —
flatten + 48 h, −0.4147 R/day against −0.7753 — gets there by **halving the number of book
days**: the daily mean is restored (+0.12301 vs +0.12225) while median calendar days to a payout
goes 689 → **832** and %/month falls to 0.236 against the do-nothing 0.408. `p_pass` is a
probability of *ever* clearing and is blind to speed. Default 0, recommend 0. The
`embargo_only` arms are information and are NOT legal — an embargo without a flatten does not
make an account compliant. [MEASURED]

**B1908 — HOLIDAY FRIDAYS DEFEAT A SATURDAY-ANCHORED DEADLINE, and this is a BREACH class, not a
cost class.** The identity check ("every priced weekend-flat exit lands on the instant the live
switch closes at") came back **7 mismatched of 271 (2.6 %)**, all Christmas or New Year, all
−20.0 h. Mechanism: when Friday is a market holiday the week's last close is **Friday 00:00
broker**, so a Saturday-anchored deadline aims 20 h into a market that already shut — the
position rides the weekend and every log reads healthy. Found by this session against its own
mechanism. [MEASURED]

**B1909 — two mitigations ship for B1908 and neither is durable.** (1)
`--weekend-early-close <dates|file>`: a non-trading day at the END of a week pulls the whole
deadline back a day; a **13-date list derived from the archive** closes the residual to **ZERO**
over all 271 exits. (2) `--weekend-flatten-before-hours 24` (flat by Friday 00:00 broker every
week): automatic, robust to any Friday holiday by construction, costs an extra **0.1167 R/day**
across the armed four (−0.8920 total). The durable fix is the broker's own session table, which
`broker_net_cost_engine.py:44-45` already names as authority this repo does not have and
`src/mt5/mt5_real.py` does not expose. Queued. [MEASURED / BUILT]

**B1910 — the derived holiday list needed two filters and a corrected denominator, and only one
check ever noticed.** Bar absence cannot distinguish a market holiday from an archive coverage
gap. The first derivation returned **497 dates** including whole months of 2018 and 2021; a 52 h
ceiling on the gap plus a 60 % quorum over the symbols that never print a weekend bar took 187
candidates → 13, all recognisable market holidays. The quorum's DENOMINATOR was then wrong too
(all voting symbols, when half the metals cross-pairs' archives begin in late 2020), which
silently dropped 2020-12-25 — one of the seven exits the derivation exists to catch — and the
residual went 0 → 7. **The check that caught both was the same one**: "with the list, how many
exits would the live rule close LATER than the replay did?" It must be zero. [MEASURED]

**B1911 — the grid reading was wrong on its first run and its own impossibility caught it.** The
first market-close deadline took *the next weekend close anywhere in the series*, which for a
continuously-quoted crypto week resolved to a gap years later and collapsed the grid reading
onto the calendar one. It printed as a result — `crypto`'s grid cell came out WORSE than its
calendar cell, which cannot happen when one rule is strictly weaker than the other. Fixed by
keying gapped weekends on the Saturday's ISO week; the in-flight sweep was killed and re-run.
[MEASURED — my own defect]

**B1912 — the mechanism, and why its degradation is asymmetric.**
`src/components/ultimate_book/weekend_policy.py` (new, pure) + `book_owner` (`weekend_policy=`,
`weekend_policy_preflight`, `_weekend_flat_close` before the time stop, `_weekend_entry_block` in
the intent loop) + five `run_book.py` flags. Default OFF == byte-identical; **no key in any
config file** (both live files are hashed into an activation-token digest; a test asserts it).
A dark clock makes the ENTRY side refuse and the EXIT side do nothing — never invent a close on
a guess, never add exposure you may not be able to manage. And because a compliance guard that
degrades to "no weekend is due" is a funded account holding through one, the failure is moved to
LAUNCH: armed policy + unresolvable server or missing `broker_clock` → `run_book.py` returns 5
and notifies CRITICAL. **`src/utils/broker_clock.py` was ABSENT from the live host at the
2026-07-26 export** (`packet_economics.py:41-49`), so carrying it is a precondition of arming.
**And the policy cannot survive the gate being shut — H8 one layer up**: `_manage_engine` returns
`live_broker_authority_false_observe_only` before the weekend check, so on a funded redacted_account
account shutting `ultimate_book_live_broker_authority` stops the compliance close as well as
everything else and the account holds through the weekend. Pinned by a test. **80 tests**,
including the entry side driven end-to-end through the real `run_cycle`. [BUILT]

**B1913 — the four-sleeve book still has no cache-population MC, and every book figure here is
archive-population.** `phase8/receipts/BOOKS_MC_V1.json` covers the armed THREE on the W7 recost
caches (`p_pass` 0.9331 redacted_account); `sub_mid_dn_revert` was armed 2026-07-30. This session's
book branch is AI's own book-4 construction (`price_trades` → `build_daily_panel`, confidence
weights from `effective_registry`) on the archive, published four ways —
`RECORDED_oos_only` (the gate's own fold test days, and the branch quoted), `RECORDED`,
`ALL_ERAS`, `RECORDED_fwd_2025plus`. The last exists because `p_pass` is concave in the daily
mean, so a delta measured at p 0.70 is not the delta at 0.93. **The estate's MC convention
consumes the FULL day series including train days, and on `energy_agri` that convention and the
gate disagree on the SIGN of this policy's effect** (gate OOS −0.024 R/day, full-series panel
+0.397) — which is why the OOS-only branch exists and is the one quoted. [MEASURED — limit
disclosed]

## Session BB — the fill truth and the sleeve-supply hunt (wave 13, B1950–B1999)

**B1950 — the family and the CUT RULE declared before any gate ran.** `CANDIDATE_FAMILY_V10.json`,

fills/week through the live guards, report every member with no top-k, take the economics column
from the published verdict at the ratified rule. Written to merge by union — a sibling wave-13 V10
supersedes it losslessly. [DECLARED]

**B1955 — the estate has been quoting DECISIONS as if they were FILLS, and the gap is 32.1 %.**
The live placement path holds at most one open position per **broker symbol across the whole
book** (`book_owner.py:1823-1850`, symbol-scoped via `_same_broker_symbol_open_exposures`
`:386-399`) and dedups per (sleeve, symbol, decision day) (`:1727-1735`); a blocked signal is

decisions → 590 live-equivalent fills**: `sub_xvol_pullback` −60.2 %, `crypto` −48.1 %,
`energy_agri` −37.3 %, `sub_mid_dn_revert` −21.4 %. It is almost entirely a sleeve blocking
ITSELF on consecutive H4 bars — only **6** cross-sleeve blocks in the whole archive. Split by
gate: 148 `symbol_occupied`, **131 `already_placed_today`** — nearly half, and the half that
survives any exit-model objection because it is a day key. [MEASURED]

**B1958 — measured two independent ways, agreeing exactly.** A guard-only replay written here
and `walkforward.book_replay.replay_book` (the production sizer + governor + gates, Session X)
reach the identical fill count on the identical candidate set: **579 = 579** on the full archive,
**115 = 115** on the full-surface window (`C2_guard_only_vs_book_replay`). The mechanism is not
new — X implements it and published its rejection counts — **applying it to the CADENCE is**,
and that is where it bites: `mc_firm_rules._derived` (`:622-624`) divides by `book_days` and
`:417` multiplies by `book_days_per_calendar_month`, both from per-sleeve day sums with no

**B1962 — the armed four's cadence and the calendar it implies.** On the window where all four
symbol surfaces exist (2024-10-29…2026-07-27, set by DASHUSD's H4 start — availability, never
results): book-days/month **5.636 → 4.227**, fills/week **2.509 → 1.387**, density
**0.2725 → 0.2044**. Time to target on the book's own realised daily series at the PRODUCTION
sizer (median effective risk **0.12–0.17 %** of equity per trade, not the 2.0 % dial): **+1.97 %
median 62 calendar days** (p10 14, p90 164), +5 % 144, +10 % 281. **Cadence is stable and
expectancy is not** — five chronological folds run 1.32/1.10/1.27/1.82/1.42 fills per week with

**B1968 — the calibrated quiet alarm, shipped.** `scripts/book_silence_check.py`: **warn at 15
silent WEEKDAY sessions (~3 calendar weeks), alert at 22 (~1 month)**, all three estimators
(empirical, geometric, moving-block bootstrap) agreeing, at 1.1 and 0.0 expected false alarms
per year on the observed history. Counts weekday sessions, not calendar days — a weekend is not
evidence and a calendar-day rule fires ~40 % early over a long weekend. Thresholds are read from
the receipt at run time and it refuses rather than falling back to a literal; exit code carries
the state; it prints on every run that it cannot distinguish a dead worker from a quiet market.

**B1980 — the supply hunt: nothing in the estate buys cadence AND edge.** Ranked by MARGINAL

**B1995 — this session's own headline was REFUTED by its own adversarial pass, and the
refutation is the more useful result.** BB's first draft asserted an estate-wide supply/edge
anti-correlation. Measured: Spearman(marginal fills/week, OOS R/day) = **−0.214, p 0.267** over
28 candidates — not significant — and because `pooled_oos_mean_r` is R per DAY, a sleeve firing

## Wave 13 · Session BC — the command center (B2000–B2049)

**B2000 — the two existing operator pages take the armed set and the account state as strings the
OPERATOR TYPES, which makes the check a tautology in the failure mode it exists for.**

passes while the book trades a different set. Both facts are machine-readable in the VPS export.

set looks safer. The modal record carries 10 tags (2,362 of FTMO's 2,654 **cycle** records — the 2,782 total also counts 128 `manage` records, which carry no `tags` field). [MEASURED]

that condition is now CHECKED rather than assumed.** Three timeframes advance on this host: M15 (15)

window the count is published as a LOWER BOUND. [MEASURED]

than reconciled.** The launcher's `_active_specs` does not apply the DF-1 filter

**B2050 — the modelled-cost gap is TOTAL, and three allowlist keys have had no producer all
along.** Of the 99,112-packet live export, **zero** packets carry `pretrade_total_cost_r`,
`pretrade_spread_r`, `gtos_vnext_pretrade_cost_model`, or `economics.cost.modelled_cost_r`. The
three `pretrade_*` keys have been in `_runtime_learning_trade_context`'s flat allowlist since before
the packet carry; nothing ever wrote them. That is why P's *"a small change to that allowlist"*
(B213) read as cheap. [MEASURED]

**B2051 — OD-P3's filed repair does not fail loudly; it fails quietly at 6.21x the bytes. My own
first draft claimed the opposite.** Adding `gtos_vnext_pretrade_cost_model` to the flat key list
emits the 42-key `build_pretrade_cost_packet` return value, which carries `profile.server`, and
`server` is in `FORBIDDEN_RAW_KEYS` with a recursive scan — so I wrote a test asserting the packet
would be **quarantined**. It is not: `_clean_mapping` redacts the value to `server_hash_sha256`
**before** `_contains_forbidden_raw_key` runs, so the naive repair validates clean and ships a hash
of the broker server name in every packet as noise. Measured cost: **2,764 bytes against 445**
derived, and at `position_managed` volume **217.5 MB against 35.0 MB per 37-day window** — on the
stream OD-P1 exists to shrink by three quarters. Built as a derivation of scalars.
[MEASURED — my claim corrected before publishing]

**B2052 — F38's shape survives in the PRETRADE model, and the packet now says so.**
`total_cost_r` is `spread + slippage + swap` (`broker_net_cost_engine.py:578-583`) and charges **no
commission**, while `build_cost_block`'s realized side charges `broker_entry_commission` and
`broker_exit_commission`. So `modelled − realized` is biased by the whole commission bill in a known
direction and a reader would book it as slippage-model error. `modelled_cost_excludes:
["commission"]` is published unconditionally (even with no modelled cost, so "no exclusions listed"
cannot read as "no exclusions") and `modelled_vs_realized_comparable` is **three-valued** — False
when the realized side charged commission, None when either side is absent, True only when
subtraction is safe. A bare boolean lets absent evidence read as a green light. [MEASURED]

`direction` on 225, and `symbol` on **0**. Of 277 multi-member units, **exactly 1** spans two
sleeves — P expected that to be the common case (*"anything spanning two sleeves of a cluster …
yields `{}`"*), and the measured common case is ONE sleeve on SEVERAL SYMBOLS. So `symbol` disagrees
on all 277 and is refused by the same test that recovers `sleeve` on 276. The
`_first_unit_sleeve` representative-guess would fire on 277 rows and be **wrong on 1**; that is not
a bound on tomorrow's, since it scales with sleeves per cluster and the registry resolves 32. Trap
pinned inert (a test fails if `SizedUnit.sleeve_members` stops being a tuple), not widened.

needed a head. Same defect Session AP found and fixed once (B1350–B1399), re-opened and run nine
versions further. [MEASURED]

`CANDIDATE_FAMILY_V12.json` (`phase14/receipts/cc_family_v12.py`) is V11's membership with V2's

and fails when one supersedes the head, so "somebody forgot to append" is a red test instead of a

**B2207 — the iteration ledger is a SIBLING of the DSR trial ledger, and the reason is arithmetic.**
The commission left the mechanics open. `measured_n_trials()` is a max over prospective look events
and feeds the **DSR deflation**, so lane iteration written into that ledger raises the estate's DSR
bill with every exploration — the backward leak `TRAINING_LANE_RATIFICATION.md` §1.2 names (AW paid
a 486-look family bill for research triage). A `surface` field cannot fix it, because
`measured_n_trials` would have to learn to *subtract*, and a bill you can subtract from is not a
ratchet. Measured as behaviour: 25 lane looks move `n_prospective_look_events` by **exactly 0**.
The two summaries are reported side by side and never summed. [BUILT + MEASURED]

**B2208 — and the sibling is not a bypass, structurally.** `graduate()` reads its provenance out of
the iteration ledger and refuses `provenance_missing`. Logging is therefore a **prerequisite for
billing**, not an alternative to it — the cheap ledger is the only road to the expensive one.
[BUILT]

**B2209 — three things a caller cannot forge.** (1) The **surface stamp**: `record()` takes DATES
and classifies them through the map, so `surface="TRAIN"` cannot be asserted over a span that
touches March. (2) The **verdict vocabulary**: `admitted` / `rejected` / `graduated` raise — they
are the sealed gate's words and a TRAIN/VAL look cannot produce one; a look reporting an admission
has either mislabelled itself or run the gate without billing it. (3) **`billed`**, written `false`
by the module and not a parameter. [BUILT]

**B2210 — the ledger would have refused the estate's own standard walk, and the fix is checked both
ways [MEASURED].** First working version refused `GateSpec.global_span` (1992-02-18..2026-07-27)
with "touches 31 TEST days" — because that span **contains** March. But spanning is not consuming:
`panel.py` drops every trade whose label span touches a blackout before pricing and `folds.py:125`
pushes fold boundaries out of one. So `engine_reserved_blackout=` lets a walk declare what its own
engine drops, and it is validated in **both** directions — it must COVER every lane-blackout day in
the span (a narrower engine blackout is a real divergence and is refused) and contain **nothing but**
blackout days (excluding an inconvenient window is a filter wearing a blackout's name). Attempting
to exclude the live forward stream that way is refused by the second check. [MEASURED — FIXED]

**B2211 — `UNCOVERED` is deliberately not a possible value of a row's `surface` field.** The first
version returned it as the "most restrictive present", which made the estate's commonest walk stamp
itself `UNCOVERED` — a field whose commonest value is a non-value trains readers to ignore it and
buries the TRAIN/VAL distinction that decides whether the used-once disclosure applies.
Uncoveredness is now loud in three other keys instead (`surfaces_present`, `n_uncovered`,
`clean_for_iteration: false`) and `surface` stays the question it claims to answer. [CORRECTED]

**B2212 — the graduation biller, and what "atomic" honestly means for two files.** The declaration
is written to a pending path, **loaded back through the estate's own validating loader**, checked
for a non-decreasing bill, and only then `os.replace`d — `load_candidate_family` has no fallback by
design, so a half-written declaration would stop the estate's billing entirely. The bill is paid
**before** the receipt, so a crash between them leaves the estate over-billed, never under-billed.
[BUILT]

**B2213 — and `graduate()` is idempotent, which is what makes that crash window repairable.**
Called again for a candidate already in the family it does **not** re-bill: it finds the paid bill
and emits the missing receipt (`billed_looks=0`, `idempotent_completion=True`, no successor file
written). A ratchet a retry could pay twice is not a ratchet, and one whose retry path needs a human
editing JSON is a ratchet that gets edited. Measured: 53 → 54 on the first call, 54 → 54 on the
second, one receipt row. [MEASURED]

**B2214 — five refusals, each the fail-closed direction, each pinned behaviourally.**
`provenance_missing` · `provenance_touches_test` (read off the **stamp**, not the row's label, so a
hand-edited ledger row claiming `surface: VAL` while carrying TEST days in its stamp is still
refused — tested by forging exactly that row) · `provenance_spec_mismatch` (the thing sent to the
gate must be a thing that was looked at) · `unknown_family` (no default family, no fallback) ·
`declaration_lost_the_rule`. The last is not hypothetical — it is B2205 turned into a guard. A
refused graduation writes no successor file, asserted. [BUILT + MEASURED]

**B2215 — the record wires to the frozen gate through the estate's existing resolver, not a second
one.** `GraduationRecord.apply_to_spec(spec)` delegates to `candidate_family.with_declared_family`,
so the gate stays a pure function of its spec and there is no new way to set a family size. The
record carries the ratified rule's `family` / `basis` / `alpha` / `option` forward, so a reader of a
graduation never has to ask which standard it was judged under. [BUILT]

**B2216 — incubation: the three constraints are enforced at three different moments, because they
are three different kinds of constraint.** Weight (≤ 0.05) and the rules are properties of ONE
record → enforced at `register()`. Capacity (≤ 5 concurrent) is a property of the SET and
"concurrent" means **armed** → enforced at `arm()`, so filing dossiers is free and arming is what
the ratification bounds. The ceremony is a property of the TRANSITION → `arm`/`pull`/`promote` each
refuse without an `OwnerCeremony` carrying who decided, when, and the receipt. Pretending they are
one check is how a registry becomes a form nobody fills in honestly. [BUILT]

**B2217 — "pre-registered" is checked against the arming time, not asserted.** `arm()` refuses when
the ceremony's `decided_utc` precedes the earliest rule's `pre_registered_utc`
(`rules_not_pre_registered`) — a rule written after the fills were visible is a rule chosen once
the answer was known. `PreRegisteredRule` also requires a `basis` naming the artifact its threshold
came from (a threshold with no basis is a number somebody liked, and it is the field a rushed
dossier drops first), and its class vocabulary **excludes `inference`** on purpose: AS's framing,
adopted — a stop rule bounds what the owner pays to find out, it does not test an edge. [BUILT]

neither added sleeve passing an admission standard — and CA's revival candidates will be the same
shape. Each basis must cite its own evidence (a graduation record, or the owner's decision) and

risk-accepted sleeve be quoted later as an admitted one. [BUILT]

**B2222 — a structural check on what the lane can reach.** No module under
`src/research_infra/training_lane/` names `agent_config.yaml`, `profiles/redacted_account`,

**B2223 — the atomic-append guarantee is stated correctly here, and `trial_budget_ledger` states it
wrongly.** That module cites `PIPE_BUF`, which is POSIX's guarantee for **pipes**; for a regular
file the honest statement is `O_APPEND` (seek-to-end and write are one atomic step w.r.t. other
writers) plus the observation that a single `write()` may in principle return short. So
`append_only.append_row` compares the returned count against the payload and **raises on a short
write rather than completing it** — retrying the tail is exactly what would tear the row after
another session's line. Filed against `trial_budget_ledger` rather than edited: not this session's
module, and its behaviour is correct even though its citation is not. [MEASURED — FILED]

**B2224 — the two ledgers have opposite failure policies, deliberately.** `TrialLedger` swallows
write errors because it must never brake a measurement (wave-6 agreement §3). The iteration ledger
is a **provenance chain**, so a lost row is a graduation that fails hours later with a refusal
nobody can explain — `strict=True` is the default and a write error raises at the point of loss.
Reusing `TrialLedger._append` would have meant reusing the policy. [BUILT]

**B2225 — CC-6, the trainer-session template** (`phase14/TRAINER_SESSION_TEMPLATE.md`): what a

(`phase14/WAVE_AGREEMENT_TRAINING_LANE_SECTION.md`), written as a drop-in replacement for

**B2227 — 60 behavioural pins, no source-string assertions**
(`tests/research_infra/test_training_lane_protocol.py`). Every test calls the machinery and

**B2228 — `IN_FLIGHT_WAVE_RANGES` re-classified, and my first reading of it was wrong in the
permissive direction.** Writing B2200+ raised the ceiling from B2075 past both siblings' ranges,
which `WAVE_10_WORKING_AGREEMENT` §5 makes this session's problem. I predicted CA's `(2100, 2149)`
and CB's `(2150, 2199)` would both be DEAD — the reasoning being that every wave-14 commission
declares its allocation in RANGE form and `_RANGE` excuses a range. **That is wrong, for the reason
`KNOWN_GHOSTS["B1786"]` already records: `_RANGE` exempts a range's UPPER bound and not its lower**,
so `B2100–B2149` is itself read as a citation of B2100. Dropping the two entries made B2100 and
B2150 dangle in the same run. Both are therefore **ACTIVE**, not dead, and stay until CA's and CB's
blocks land. Only CC's own entry is dead (B2200 is defined, so its lower bound resolves), dropped
per the guard's own remedy, with **CD's `B2250–B2299`** added as a pre-declaration so the table
survives the moment the siblings retire theirs — the move AY made for AZ. Recorded rather than
quietly corrected because the error's direction is the one that matters: it would have deleted two
live exemptions from other sessions' work. [CORRECTED]

**B2229 — two pre-existing ghosts, hidden by the ceiling and surfaced by this session's blocks.**
B2086 and B2094 are cited by Session BD and defined nowhere; they sat above the B2075 ceiling and
were invisible until B2200+ moved it. Both are the `B1976` shape rather than lost evidence:
`phase13/SESSION_BD_AB.md:110` quotes a commit subject **verbatim inside a `gtos-ab-receipt-v1`
fence** whose self-containment guard exists precisely so its bytes are the capture's bytes, and
`SESSION_BD_LIVE_DEBT_SWEEP_RESULT.md:304-305` names the ranges *in the act of recording that they
do not resolve* — BD's own correction, ending "do not cite a block number until the block exists".
The authoritative numbering is B2050–B2075 contiguous. Added to `KNOWN_GHOSTS` with that reason,
which is what the allowlist is for; the alternative was editing an immutable receipt. This is the
third instance of the class (B1484, B1786, B1976) and the third time the ceiling moving is what
made it visible. [MEASURED — FILED]

**B2230 — an adversarial pass on my own incubation registry found a real hole in the one check
that makes "pre-registered" mean anything.** `arm()` compared the ceremony against the
**earliest** rule's `pre_registered_utc`. That is the wrong bound: "pre-registered" is a claim
about EVERY rule, so an incubant whose STOP rule predates the ceremony and whose PROMOTION rule
was written an hour after it **passed** — and a promotion rule added once the fills are visible
is exactly the rule the constraint exists to stop. Now bound on the LATEST rule.
Two more in the same pass: timestamps were compared as **strings**, and ISO-8601 offsets are not
lexicographically ordered (`"…T00:00:00Z"` sorts above `"…T00:00:00+00:00"` because `'Z' > '+'`
while denoting the same instant), so the check would have failed on whichever session happened
to spell it with `Z` — both spellings are valid and both appear in this estate's receipts; and
`sorted()` over `(instant, dict)` pairs raised `TypeError` when two rules shared a timestamp,
because Python fell through to comparing the dicts. All three found by writing ONE test that
combined the offset spellings with a late promotion rule. Also: a hand-written ruleless row now
refuses with `rules_missing_on_record` instead of crashing on an empty `min()`. [MEASURED — FIXED]

**B2231 — the mandated A/B method has a landmine, and this session stepped on it [MEASURED].**
A single unreproducible failure appeared in a wide sweep —
`test_fast_engine_accel.py::test_route_cleanup_refuses_the_namespace_root_itself` — and passed
on every re-run. Chased rather than shrugged off, and the mechanism is exact:
`ATTEMPT5_NAMESPACE_ROOT` is an **empty directory**, git does not track empty directories, so
its absence leaves `git status` **clean** and `git checkout -- .` **cannot restore it**.
Reproduced deterministically: `rmtree` the root, `git checkout -- .`, run the test → fails; run
the whole file → passes, because the sibling test recreates the root with `parents=True`. So it
fails exactly once after any working-tree clean and then heals itself, which is the hardest
shape to attribute. **The working agreement MANDATES A/B by copy-back — which is such a
clean** — so this was going to be paid for again by whoever next did an honest A/B, and it
would have read as "your change broke the fast engine". Repaired at the test: the precondition
is now explicit (`mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)`) with the reason on it, which also keeps
the assertion meaning what its name says — `_remove_route` cannot be shown to REFUSE a root
that is not there. Verified from a genuinely absent root. [MEASURED — FIXED]

and never the first, which is the only reason Session CD's regeneration is legal. `train_engine/
lane.py` emits a `LANE_TRADE_TABLE.jsonl` under its own stamp and auto-writes one unbilled row into
CC's shared iteration ledger per arm, with the surface computed from the days the GUARD enumerated
rather than from a span a caller supplies. A lane look can never emit a TRAINING artifact and a
training run can never emit a lane one: each emitter checks the authorization object, not the
caller's intent. [BUILT]
